author: trivikr
body:
Fix a debugger CLI startup synchronization race.

`startRepl()` awaited debugger domain initialization and
`Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger()`, but it did not wait for the resulting
initial `Debugger.paused` event to be handled before starting the REPL.

That allowed the `debug>` prompt to appear before the initial break message was
printed. In slow CI runs, `parallel/test-debugger-run-after-quit-restart` could
time out while waiting for the first break, even though the debugger had already
attached.

This changes local script startup to wait for the initial pause event and for
its pause formatting to complete before resolving initialization. Remote attach
behavior is left unchanged.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/actions/runs/27582782593/job/81546582775

## Quoi
Résout le fork Alembic multi-head qui gèle la DB sur `mg01` et **rend la chaîne prod-safe** :
1. `mg02_merge_pn01_sc01` : revision de merge no-op unifiant les 2 heads (`pn01_server_push` + `sc01_drop_ucs_excl_idx`) → **1 head**.
2. `ex01_drop_extraction_ts` : le `DROP COLUMN contents.extraction_attempted_at` est **reporté** (upgrade no-op) — la colonne est encore utilisée par le code **prod** déployé (DB partagée). Le vrai drop ira dans une migration de suivi post-cutover prod.

## Pourquoi
DB partagée stampée sur `mg01` (point de fork). 2 heads → `alembic upgrade head` (boot Railway) échoue « Multiple head revisions » → `gh01` jamais appliquée → `grille_puzzles.hybrid_*` absente → **`/api/grille/today` 500 `ProgrammingError`** (constaté en QA staging).

## Effet au déploiement (merge → boot Railway applique mg01→head)
| Migration | Opération | Prod-safe ? |
|---|---|---|
| `gh01_grille_hybrid_word` | ADD 4 colonnes nullable (débloque grille) | ✅ |
| `ex01_drop_extraction_ts` | **no-op** (drop reporté) | ✅ |
| `pn01_server_push` | CREATE TABLE fcm_devices + push_deliveries | ✅ |
| `sc01_drop_ucs_excl_idx` | DROP INDEX mort | ✅ |
| `mg02_merge_pn01_sc01` | merge no-op | ✅ |

→ **Mergeable sans casser la prod.** Merger = déployer sur la DB partagée (le boot staging jouera `upgrade head`). Confirmé : `extraction_attempted_at` reste en place (prod intacte), grille repassera en 200.

## Suivi
- [ ] Migration de suivi (vrai `DROP COLUMN extraction_attempted_at`) à créer une fois `production` avancée vers du code sans la colonne.

## Vérifié
- [x] Graphe : 30 révisions, **1 seul head** (`mg02`).
- [x] `ex01` upgrade = no-op, syntaxe OK.
- [ ] CI `alembic-smoke`.

author: onestepat4time
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4739 — CLS p100 tail breach (max 0.5346) under active SSE-push stress on the dashboard overview. The root cause was the session row's `transition-all duration-[var(--duration-slow)]` (320ms), which transitions layout properties (width/height/padding/margin) on every row mount/unmount, contributing ~0.05 CLS per push. Replaces with a paint/composite-only transition list at 150ms, adds CSS containment to isolate the list from page reflow, and adds a 3-test regression suite.

## Verification (per Functional Code Gate)

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- `npx vitest run src/components/overview/__tests__/cls-regression.test.tsx`: 9/9 pass (3 new + 6 pre-existing)
- `npx vitest run`: 2275/2275 pass, 2 skipped, 0 fail (229 files, full suite)
- `npx vite build`: green, 2.20s
- Smoke: `vite preview` on :5210 → `/dashboard/` 200, asset 200

## Files (2 changed, +80/-4)

- `dashboard/src/components/overview/VirtualizedSessionList.tsx` (+2/-2)
  - Row className: `transition-all duration-[var(--duration-slow)]` → `transition-[background-color,border-color,box-shadow,transform,opacity,color] duration-150`
  - Container: `containLayout: true, contain: 'layout'` to isolate list from page reflow
- `dashboard/src/components/overview/__tests__/cls-regression.test.tsx` (+78/-2)
  - Asserts new row className does not contain `transition-all`
  - Asserts new row className includes paint-only property list
  - Asserts `contain: layout` is applied to the scroll container

## Acceptance

- At-rest CLS: unchanged (post-#4730 baseline ~0.30 p50)
- Active-SSE CLS: regression test pins the structural fix; full revalidation blocked on #4740 (test rig, Hep/devops lane)
- Bundle: index chunk delta <0.1kB (className-only change, no new deps)

## Out of scope (flagged)

- #4740 test rig (Hep/devops)
- #4683 Phase 2 retry (parent epic, post-fix-shipping)
- Stress validation: deferred to next Phase 2 run

— Daedalus 🏛️

body:
This PR addresses 6 critical issues identified during final QA to make the application production-ready:

1.  **Energy Units Bug**: Corrected the units for total, daytime, and nighttime consumption from Watts (W) to Watt-hours (Wh) in `DashboardScreen` and `PdfExportService`.
2.  **DC Breaker Sizing Bug**: Updated the DC breaker calculation in `SolarCalculationRepository` to correctly factor in `inverterEfficiency` (`((inverterWattage / inverterEfficiency) / systemVoltage) * 1.25`).
3.  **Battery Capacity Transparency**: Added dynamic `kWh` calculation alongside `Ah` and the base `systemVoltage` across `SystemResultModel`, UI, and PDF.
4.  **Panel Capacity Context**: Added the chosen panel capacity (`W`) context to the total panel counts in both the `DashboardScreen` and PDF export.
5.  **Reactive Sync Bug**: Swapped `ref.read` for `ref.watch` to ensure the Dashboard screen stays perfectly synchronized with any external state changes (like settings). Implemented a `ReactiveTextField` to solve Flutter cursor placement issues when two-way binding a `TextFormField` to Riverpod state.
6.  **Missing Data in PDF Export**: Fixed `pdf_export_service.dart` to inherit and print the newly added properties from `CalculationBreakdownModel` (MPPT sizes, float preservation tips).

All changes follow the strict "Single Source of Truth" Riverpod pattern and adhere to precise engineering bounds. Code has been analyzed and passes all tests.

author: lekt9
body:
## What this adds

A complete, machine-checked, **axiom-clean** formalization of the exact closed form of the
6th period moment of a negation-closed set of field elements:

> For a negation-closed finite `G ⊆ F` with `0 ∉ G` and `char F ≠ 2`,
> the number of **antipodally count-balanced** 6-tuples over `G` is exactly
> `negSymCount G 6 = 15·|G|³ − 45·|G|² + 40·|G|`  (over `ℤ`).

For `G = μ_n` (the n-th roots of unity) in characteristic 0 this is `E₃(μ_n) = 15n³ − 45n² + 40n`,
the exact 6th period moment `rEnergy μ_n 3`. This is precisely the input hypothesis (`hE3`) that the
already-shipped r=2 cross-step rung (`Frontier/CrossStepRungTwo.lean`) consumes, so this PR discharges
that hypothesis in char 0. Mathlib does not have this; the value was previously only a conjecture
backed by a numeric probe.

## The math (why these numbers)

A count-balanced 6-tuple (`#{i : cᵢ = z} = #{i : cᵢ = −z}` for every `z`) has a value set that is
closed under negation and avoids `0`, hence splits into antipodal pairs `{x, −x}`. Counting by the
**image size** `|image| ∈ {2, 4, 6}` gives three strata, each a clean multinomial:

| image | structure | tuples with that image | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{x,−x}` | one pair, balanced | `C(6,3) = 20` | `image_count_two` |
| `{x,−x,y,−y}` | two pairs, balanced | `400 − 20 − 20 = 360` | `image_count_four` (← `shape21`) |
| `{a,−a,b,−b,c,−c}` | three pairs, all distinct | `6! = 720` | `image_count_six` |

Summing over all negation-closed subsets, and using that the number of negation-closed `2i`-subsets
of `G` is `C(|G|/2, i)` (a transversal/orbit count), gives
`20·C(h,1) + 360·C(h,2) + 720·C(h,3)` with `h = |G|/2`, which simplifies to `15(2h)³ − 45(2h)² + 40(2h)`.
No 15-matching inclusion–exclusion is needed — the negation-pair structure does the work.

## Structure of the proof

- `_E3Shape21Scratch.lean` — the hardest stratum: `fiber_card` (per-position-set split into a product
  of two `powersetCard`s), `balanced_valued_count = 400`, `valued_image_two = 20`, `shape21 = 360`,
  and `image_count_four` (the 360 count in the uniform partition form).
- `_E3SubsetCount.lean` — `negClosed_subset_count`: `#{neg-closed S ⊆ G : |S| = 2i} = C(|G|/2, i)`,
  a direct port of `InvolutionClosedCount.isClosed_card_eq_choose` from `univ` to `G`.
- `_E3StrataCount.lean` (earlier in the branch) — `negSymCount`, the partition over images, the
  transversal/parity machinery, `image_count_two`/`image_count_six`, and the `strata_sum_eq_closed`
  arithmetic bridge.
- `_E3Assembly.lean` — `count_two/four/six/zero` (per-`S` dispatch by `|S|`) and the capstone
  `negSymCount_eq_closed`.
- `_E3NegSymConverse.lean` — the char-free converse (count-balanced ⟹ zero-sum), the link from
  `negSymCount` to the energy `rEnergy`.
- **`E3StrataCharZero.lean`** — the clean entry point, `negSymCount_six_closed`, with the scoped
  docstring. (The `_`-prefixed files are the supporting bricks and can be promoted/renamed on request.)

## Verification

- **Axiom audit:** every theorem depends only on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — no
  `sorryAx`, no `native_decide`, no added axioms. Confirmed under a real `lake build` (which enforces
  `autoImplicit = false`), not just `lake env lean`.
- **Numeric cross-check:** `scripts/probes/probe_e3_negsym_strata.py` confirms
  `E3_direct == closed_form == strata_sum` for `n ∈ {4, 8, 16, 32}`, and its per-stratum column
  `[20·C(h,1), 360·C(h,2), 720·C(h,3)]` matches the Lean assembly exactly.

## Scope — what this is **not**

This is a **characteristic-0** result. It is honest about its boundary (see the `E3StrataCharZero.lean`
docstring): identifying `negSymCount μ_n 6` with the full energy `rEnergy μ_n 3` needs the *forward*
direction (zero-sum ⟹ count-balanced), which is the char-0 Lam–Leung theorem. The **char-`p` transfer
at depth `r ≈ log q`** — the incomplete character-sum / `√`-cancellation bound over thin multiplicative
subgroups (the Paley Graph Conjecture regime) — is the genuine open core of #444 and is **not** touched
here. This PR moves one named hypothesis from "conjectured (probe only)" to "proved (char 0)"; it does
not close the proximity prize.

Closes nothing on the open core; intended as a reusable, verified building block.

author: jouryjc
body:
## 概述

基于本仓库博客资源,新增纯静态站点 `site/`:**3D 深色星系风知识图谱首页** + 全部成品文章的站内全文阅读,可部署到 Cloudflare Pages。技术栈:Vite + 原生 JS + `3d-force-graph`(Three.js + UnrealBloom)。

按 `docs/plans/2026-06-15-xiaoyu-site-3d-graph.md` 的 7 个 Task 逐步实现,每个 Task 一个 commit。

## 实现内容(7 Task)

1. **脚手架与依赖** — Vite + 依赖 + `.gitignore` + `index.html`
2. **数据生成脚本** — `build/generate-data.mjs` + `verify-data.mjs`(产出 12 主题 + 16 篇文章)
3. **路由与数据加载** — 极简 history 路由 + 运行时 JSON 加载 + 全局深色样式
4. **首页 3D 知识图谱** — `3d-force-graph` 星系图 + UnrealBloom 辉光 + HUD(品牌/搜索/12 主题图例/入口)
5. **文章列表页** — 卡片网格 + 主题筛选 tab
6. **文章详情页** — 站内全文 + 配图 + 相关文章(不含微信原文外链)
7. **生产构建与部署文档** — `README.md`(本地开发 / CF Pages 部署)

## 与计划的关键调整(均已在会话中确认/验证)

- **数据源改为 manifest 驱动**:真实的 `tags`/`moc`/`related` 元数据在 `_kb_build/manifest.json`(按路径为 key),而非文章自身 frontmatter。脚本据此发现文章并建边。
- **文章口径(用户确认)**:manifest 中 `type/article` 且 `platform/wechat` 的条目,跨 `outputs/`、`output/`、`post-to-wechat/`;自动排除小红书文案;`.optimized`/`.xiaoyu` 变体去重(优先 `.optimized`)→ 最终 **16 篇**。
- **修复首页黑屏**:`3d-force-graph@1.80` 要求 `three>=0.179`,计划钉的 `0.160` 会产生双 three 实例,使 UnrealBloomPass 与库内 renderer 接口不一致 → 整屏黑。已将 `three` 升至 `^0.184.0` 去重,并在 bloom 后接 `OutputPass` 做 sRGB 输出。
- **配图体积修复**:`outputs/` 扁平文章共用一个 `imgs/`,原"整目录复制"会把 37MB 共享目录重复塞进每篇(dist 一度 406MB)。改为按正文引用精确复制 → **dist 71MB**。

## 验证

- `node build/verify-data.mjs` → `OK 主题12 文章16 边23`
- `npm run build` 通过;`npm run preview` 下三条路由可访问,**直接刷新子路由不 404**(SPA fallback)
- 浏览器实测:首页 3D 辉光图谱、列表筛选、详情全文+配图(0 破图)、相关文章跳转、**无微信外链**
- 移动端窄屏:图谱降级(无 bloom)、图例/搜索隐藏、列表单列、正文可读

## Test Plan

- [ ] `cd site && npm install && npm run build` 成功
- [ ] `npm run preview` 后人工过一遍 `/`、`/articles`、`/article/<slug>` 及刷新
- [ ] CF Pages:Build command `cd site && npm ci && npm run build`,输出目录 `site/dist`

author: unciv-loof
body:
The costs of techs and policies are dependent on map size. The current behavior is to floor the map's radius to the nearest predefined map size to retrieve values for `techCostMultiplier`, `techCostPerCityModifier` and `policyCostPerCityModifier`. This has a few issues: - Instead of smoothly changing alongside the radius, the values [flatline and make sudden jumps](https://github.com/yairm210/Unciv/blob/fa34576b746292cca112d4ab8949f9319ee36ac0/core/src/com/unciv/logic/map/MapSize.kt#L90). As an example, modifiers for radii 20 and 29 are the same (floored to Medium), while there is a big jump from 29 to 30 (Large). - There is no adjustment for map sizes beyond Huge, making domination victory exceedingly difficult on gigantic maps because tech progression is too quick.
The dots are current (unchanged) predefined values (Tiny, ..., Huge), and the lines represent the new inferred values for custom radii. Legacy values for custom radii (floor down logic) are not shown.
Backwards compatibility: The only change should be seen in new maps with custom maps sizes. Old savefiles see no impact from the changes, as they will continue to use the legacy floor down logic. New maps using predefined map sizes (Small, Medium etc.) also remain unchanged. This is enabled through making the fields nullable, where null (or no value) causes the legacy floor down logic to be used.
Tested behavior: - Deserialize old savefile (no values) - noargs constructor is called and fields are null. - Serialize old savefile - fields are not written to savefile. - Serialize new savefile - fields are written as floats to savefile. - Deserialize new savefile - noargs constructor is called and fields are set to the floats from savefile. - Check `techCostMultiplier` for old savefile with radius=80 - value is 1.3f (corresponds to Huge preset). - Check `techCostMultiplier` for new savefile with radius=80 - value is 1.7f.

author: sanity
body:
## Problem

Ian decided to ship the #4404 placement-migration (`SubscribeHint`) cascade **active** in the v0.2.73 release. On that release branch the build version equals `SUBSCRIBE_HINT_MIN_VERSION = (0,2,73)`, so the migration **activates in every simulation** (it is dormant on the current 0.2.72 `main`).

Three simulation tests assumed migration stays OFF *via build-version gating* and break once it activates. These are **not code bugs** — the migration works as designed and GETs still succeed. The tests fail because their premise (the contract stays put) is violated:

1. `test_get_dead_ends_at_close_cluster_without_migration` (`simulation_integration.rs`) — the negative control for the #4404 dead-end. It asserts a GET dead-ends *because migration is off*, and deliberately does NOT call `enable_placement_migration()`, relying only on build-version gating. When migration activates, the close cluster hosts the contract and the control falsely fails.
2. `test_streaming_get_through_relay` (`streaming_e2e.rs`) — asserts a relay streaming-forward hop fires (`RELAY_GET_STREAMING_FORWARD_COUNT` increments). Migration spreads the contract toward the requester, so the relay hop never runs.
3. `test_streaming_get_retries_after_assembly_failure` (`streaming_e2e.rs`) — hand-builds a cold-node → holder routing scenario; migration moves the contract and disrupts the injected-assembly-failure retry path under test.

## Approach

All three tests exercise relay / assembly / dead-end **mechanics**, NOT placement. The right fix is to pin migration OFF for them rather than leave them at the mercy of the build version. There was previously an `enable_placement_migration()` helper but no force-OFF counterpart.

- Add a `disable_placement_migration()` helper on `SimNetwork`, mirroring `enable_placement_migration()`. It sets `subscribe_hint_floor_override` to an **unreachable** `(255, 255, 65535)` floor, so `version_supports_subscribe_hint` always returns false and the cascade is OFF regardless of build version. It threads through the same path (`NodeConfig.subscribe_hint_floor_override` → `ConnectionManager`) and works for both the `SimNetwork` tests and the Turmoil / `run_controlled_simulation` streaming tests (all three of these tests use `run_controlled_simulation`).
- Call `disable_placement_migration()` in all three tests, with a comment in each explaining that migration must be off for the test's premise and that it must not rely on build-version gating. For test 3 the call lives in the shared `setup_assembly_retry_network` helper so it covers both the phase-1 and phase-2 sims.
- Bump the fdev per-sim CI timeout `8m` → `15m` for all four fdev load sims in the Simulation job. The migration roughly doubles fdev sim cost when active, which can exceed 8m on a slow release-branch runner. The job's `timeout-minutes: 40` still covers the four sims running in parallel.

## Testing

Verified with `SUBSCRIBE_HINT_MIN_VERSION` **temporarily toggled to `(0,2,72)`** so the migration activates on this 0.2.72 build (then reverted — the committed change keeps the floor at `(0,2,73)`):

- The three tests pass **5/5 runs** with migration globally active.
- The `ci-medium-50` fdev sim (`--gateways 4 --nodes 46 --events 2000 ... --min-success-rate 1.0`) completes with exit 0 and 100% success rate under migration, well within the new 15m cap.
- `cargo fmt` clean; `cargo clippy -p freenet --tests --features simulation_tests,testing` clean.

This is test-infra + a CI-timeout tweak; no production behavior change (the production floor stays `(0,2,73)`).

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #895

## Surface
`/app` surfaces: builds cinema, not-found, sales workspace, conversation pin button, PostOnboardingNudge, LeadsTableClient.

## What changed

The `PraxisButton`/`Button` component and the `btn-*` CSS system were already fully implemented. This PR completes issue #895 by eliminating the remaining ad-hoc button styling across `/app` console surfaces.

**Specific fixes:**

| File | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `BuildShippedSummary.tsx` | `btn-primary inline-flex items-center gap-1.5` (no size) on `<a>`/`<Link>` | `btn-primary btn-sz-sm` |
| `BuildShippedSummary.tsx` | Ad-hoc `h-9 px-3 rounded-md border border-[var(--color-border)] hover:border-[var(--color-accent)]` on secondary links | `btn-secondary btn-sz-sm` |
| `BuildPreviewStage.tsx` | `btn-primary inline-flex items-center gap-1.5` (no size) | `btn-primary btn-sz-sm` |
| `builds/[session]/error.tsx` | Dual PraxisButton+Button imports, ad-hoc secondary `<a>` | Consolidated `Button`, `btn-secondary btn-sz-sm` |
| `not-found.tsx` | `btn-primary inline-flex items-center gap-2` + inline `padding: 10px 20px` style override | `btn-primary btn-sz-md` |
| `SalesWorkspace.tsx` | `btn-primary !text-sm` (ad-hoc override) | `btn-primary btn-sz-sm` |
| `PinConversationButton.tsx` | `p-1.5 rounded-md transition-colors hover:bg-[var(--color-surface-raised)] focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-[var(--color-accent)]` | `cx-icon-btn cx-focus-ring` |
| `LeadsTableClient.tsx` | Dual `Button` + `PraxisButton` imports, mixed usage | Consolidated to `Button` from `conduit/ui/Button` |
| `PostOnboardingNudge.tsx` | Dual `Button` + `PraxisButton` imports | Consolidated to `Button` |

## What was NOT changed

- Auth pages (`sign-in`, `sign-up`, `forgot-password`, etc.) — use `conduit-auth-btn` which is a separate intentional system for pre-login surfaces
- Marketing pages — use `conduit-btn-primary` which is the marketing identity system
- Specialized UI components (toggle chips in `OnboardingModal`, palette items in `CommandPalette`, `SpecialistSelectorModal` selector tiles) — these are list item / toggle patterns, not primary actions; PraxisButton (44px min-height) would be wrong shape/size
- `CookieConsentBanner` — rendered outside `.praxis-root` in the root layout; shared across marketing + console

## Before / After

**Before:** Link-buttons in builds cinema had no size class, causing them to use the variant's default padding (12px 24px) — oversized for the tight cinema layout. Secondary links used one-off Tailwind border hover classes.

**After:** All link-buttons use `btn-sz-sm` (32px / 44px on mobile) matching the spec's size rhythm. Secondary links use the glass `btn-secondary` system.

## Premortem

- **PraxisButton is `motion.button` — link elements keep CSS-only.** `<a>` and `<Link>` styled as buttons can't use PraxisButton (it renders a `<button>`). They correctly keep `btn-primary btn-sz-*` CSS classes — this IS the canonical design system, not ad-hoc styling.
- **No behavior change** on any of the import consolidations — `Button` from `conduit/ui/Button` is a re-export of `PraxisButton`.
- **`cx-icon-btn` used for PinConversationButton** — this utility is defined in `console-tokens.css` and provides hover background + focus ring matching the spec, appropriate for 32px icon-only actions.

## Verified
- `npm run build` ✅
- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅ (zero errors in src/)
- Responsive: `btn-sz-sm` expands to `min-height: 44px` on `pointer: coarse` (mobile) per globals.css
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: handled by existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` in globals.css

author: deanmarano
body:
## Context

Surfaced while un-skipping `primary_keys_test.rb` residuals in RFC 0030 story `c3-primary-keys` (test `assign id raises error if primary key doesnt exist`).

Rails raises `ActiveModel::MissingAttributeError` on `instance.id = "1"` for an anonymous class on a table with no primary key (`dashboards`). In TS the class `primaryKey` correctly resolves to `null` via the warmed schema cache, but `setId` silently wrote through `_writeAttribute` with an absent column instead of raising.

## Change

- `setId` (`attribute-methods/primary-key.ts`) now throws `MissingAttributeError` when the model's primary key resolves to `null`, mirroring Rails `AttributeMethods::PrimaryKey#id=`.
- Un-skipped `assign id raises error if primary key doesnt exist` in `primary-keys.test.ts`; it warms the schema cache via `loadSchema()` then asserts the raise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `instance.id = value` raises MissingAttributeError when primary key resolves to null.
- [x] Test un-skipped and passing.

author: rachelslurs
body:
## What

Adds `.github/workflows/updater-key-check.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch`-only job, gated on the `release` environment, that signs a throwaway file with `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and verifies the signature against the pubkey embedded in the app (minisign key ID `63EECF42A6923640`).

## Why

Confirms the updater **private** key in the `release` env secret corresponds to the **public** key in `tauri.conf.json` **before** the first release. If they don't match, v1 installs fine but the v1→v2 auto-update fails signature verification silently for every user. The preflight config doctor checks the Apple key and PAT reachability but does **not** cover the Tauri keypair — this closes that gap.

## Safety

- `workflow_dispatch`-only (never runs on PRs); secret is reachable only behind the `release` approval gate.
- Prints **PASS/FAIL and the public key ID only** — no secret value is printed (no `set -x`; key→file, password→stdin; GitHub masks registered secrets as a backstop).
- Passes the structural hardening guard (`check-release-workflow.sh`): the only `uses:` is `harden-runner` pinned to a 40-hex SHA.

## After use

This is a one-off. **Delete the workflow once it reports PASS.**

author: rohansonecha
body:
## Problem

The **"Allocation & Utilization Over Time"** panel in the SkyPilot History (compute-overview) dashboard can report GPU allocation **above 100%** (observed values up to ~178%). Allocation as a fraction of GPU capacity should always be in `[0%, 100%]`.

The panel computed:

```
sum(requests) / sum(allocatable) * 100
```

This overshoots in two independent situations:

1. **Per-node double-count** — a single node can momentarily carry GPU requests beyond its own capacity, e.g. when a terminating pod and its replacement are both counted on the same node.
2. **Node-set mismatch** — when a node drops out of `kube_node_status_allocatable`, its pods' requests still inflate the numerator while the denominator shrinks, so the ratio exceeds 100%.

## Fix

Cap each node's counted requests at that node's allocatable before summing:

```
sum( min(requests_per_node, allocatable_per_node) ) / sum(allocatable) * 100
```

expressed in PromQL as `req - clamp_min(req - alloc, 0)` matched per `(cluster, node)`. Because the per-node `min` join only retains nodes present in **both** the request and allocatable sets, the numerator and denominator are evaluated over the same node set and each node contributes at most its capacity — so the result is bounded to `[0, 100]` **by construction**.

The "Avg GPU Allocation" reference line reuses the same expression, so it stays consistent with the corrected series and is likewise bounded.

## Verification

Validated against live data over a 7-day range at 10-minute resolution:

| | min | max | points outside [0,100] |
|---|---|---|---|
| previous query | 0.39% | **178%** | many |
| this PR (per-node cap) | 0.39% | **100.00%** | **0** |

## Notes

- Dashboard-only change (`charts/skypilot/manifests/compute-overview-dashboard.json`); ships via the Grafana ConfigMap, no image rebuild required, and applies retroactively since the panel recomputes from raw metrics at query time.
- Utilization series are unaffected.

author: g8rswimmer
body:
What changed and why

The workflow editor previously scattered configuration across two separate modal buttons in the navbar — Inputs and Trigger — with no way to set a workflow description at all. This PR consolidates all workflow-level configuration into a single ⚙ Settings button, making it easier to discover and manage without jumping between multiple panels.

New WorkflowSettingsPanel component

A single scrollable modal replaces the old TriggerPanel and InputsPanel (both deleted). It contains three sections:

- General — edit the workflow name and a new optional description field
- Trigger — select manual, webhook, or cron, with the same kind-specific fields as before
- Inputs — the existing initial data schema editor, embedded directly

The panel uses live-edit (writes directly to the Zustand store) consistent with how the inputs editor already worked. Changes are reflected in the "unsaved" indicator immediately; the Save button commits them to the backend.

Description field — end to end

description is now a first-class field: stored in the Zustand store, included in create/update payloads, loaded back on loadWorkflow, and displayed on the workflow list page beneath each workflow's name.

Navbar cleanup

The Inputs and Trigger buttons are replaced by a single Settings button. The button shows the current trigger kind icon (▶ manual / ⚡ webhook / ⏰ cron) so the active trigger remains visible at a glance. The inline name input stays for quick renaming without opening the modal.

Code review fixes applied

- Cron expression preserved across kind switches — a useRef tracks the last typed cron expression independently of the store, so switching away to manual or webhook and back does not reset the field to * * * * *
- Escape key and backdrop click close the modal — a keydown listener on document and an onClick on the overlay both call onClose, matching standard modal behaviour
- No duplicate section headings — InitialDataSchemaEditor gained a hideHeading prop; the settings panel passes it to suppress the component's own "Workflow Inputs" heading, which would otherwise stack visually with the panel's "INPUTS" label
- No per-keystroke re-renders of the editor page — WorkflowEditorPage no longer subscribes to description reactively; buildPayload reads it via useWorkflowStore.getState() at save time only
- Webhook URL computed once — handleKindChange references the already-derived webhookUrl constant instead of reconstructing the path string inline

How to verify

1. Open a new workflow — confirm the navbar shows only one Settings button (no separate Inputs/Trigger buttons)
2. Open Settings and set a name, description, and cron trigger expression
3. Switch trigger to manual, then back to cron — confirm the expression is preserved
4. Press Escape or click outside the modal — confirm it closes
5. Save the workflow, then navigate back to the list — confirm the description appears under the workflow name
6. Reload the editor — confirm all fields (name, description, trigger kind and expression) are restored correctly

author: csmittee
body:
## Root Cause

`fake-omise-worker.js` (R-107) wraps the charge object in `{ key: 'charge.complete', data: { object: 'charge', ... } }`.

`webhook.js` read `payload.object` and `payload.status` directly — both `undefined` at the top level of that envelope. The `if` condition never matched. Handler returned `{status:'ok'}` immediately with **no DB write, no command queued**. Machine polled forever. `simulator.html` flow broke at QR payment screen.

## Fix — `src/handlers/webhook.js`

```js
// R-124: fake-omise wraps charge in { key:'charge.complete', data:{...} }
// Real Omise sends charge at top level — payload.data is undefined — falls back to payload
const charge = payload.data || payload;
```

All charge field reads changed from `payload.*` → `charge.*` in both the `successful` and `failed` blocks. Fallback DB lookup by `order_id` simplified from `Object.assign` pattern to direct assignment.

## Real Omise — unaffected

Real Omise sends charge at top level. `payload.data` is `undefined` → `charge` falls back to `payload`. Real `charge_id` always exists in DB — fallback branch never fires in production.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/handlers/webhook.js` | R-124 envelope unwrap + clean up fallback lookup |

author: kevinelliott
body:
Three issues a colleague (Fritz) hit running on Linux with an RTL-SDR:

```
xng survey --sdr driver=rtlsdr --mode adsb --tune-gain --duration 120 --interim 30
...
   12.0 dB: failed (channel 1090.000 MHz: Mode S uses the whole capture: tune -c to 1090.000M and pass --channels 1090)
^C^C^C^C^\Quit (core dumped)
```

## A) ADS-B survey gain sweep fails (`Mode S uses the whole capture`)
The capture center was nudged +25 kHz off DC (→ `1090.025 MHz`) to keep carriers away from the DC spike. But Mode S consumes the **whole** capture and requires the channel to sit **at** the center (offset 0), so the decoder rejected every dwell.

The DC-avoidance nudge now applies only to **DDC modes** (`passband > 0`); whole-capture modes (Mode S) keep the channel at center. Fixed at all four nudge sites: `group_channels`, the `scan` and `survey` proposal builders, and `resolve_tune_auto`'s centroid. The test that *asserted* the buggy nudge (`auto_window_handles_single_channel_modes`) is corrected, and a new `group_channels` test pins the behavior.

## B) Ctrl-C didn't stop the run (needed SIGQUIT → core dump)
The first `^C` printed "finishing up" and set the abort flag, but tokio then swallowed every further signal (nothing was awaiting them), so a wedged/looping device trapped the process until `^\` (SIGQUIT) killed it with a core dump.

The interrupt handler is now **two-stage** everywhere — survey, `listen`/`run_session`, and `station`: the first signal drains gracefully (sources close cleanly), a second forces `process::exit(130)`. This is the escape hatch when the decode loop is blocked in a device read that never observes the stop flag.

## C) Auto rate selection never checked device support
`probe_device_rates` returned an empty list for **every** SoapySDR device (RTL-SDR/HackRF/SDRplay), so auto-tune fell back to the mode plan rate blind. That happened to work for ADS-B/ACARS on RTL but not for e.g. HFDL's 768 kS/s, which lands in RTL-SDR's unsupported rate gap.

Now `probe_rate_caps` reports a `RateCaps` enum:
- **Discrete** — native airspy/airspyhf exact list (unchanged)
- **Ranges** — SoapySDR `getSampleRateRange()` (min/max/step)
- **Unknown** — can't ask → trust the plan rate

`choose_rate` picks the smallest **supported** rate `>=` the mode's plan rate that is a clean DDC multiple (for DDC modes), so it never strands a mode at a too-narrow capture. New tests cover RTL-like ranges (keeps 2.0 MS/s for ADS-B, 2.4 for ACARS, climbs out of the gap for HFDL).

## Testing
- Full workspace test suite green (`cargo test --workspace --features airspy,airspyhf`).
- New unit tests: `group_channels_keeps_whole_capture_channel_at_center`, `choose_rate_from_rtl_ranges`, `choose_rate_unknown_keeps_plan`, `choose_rate_floor_avoids_too_narrow_capture`, plus the corrected `auto_window_handles_single_channel_modes`.
- Release build clean (`--features airspy,airspyhf`).
- Hardware: the running Airspy Iridium station uses an explicit-rate config (no auto-probe), so it's unaffected. Fritz can re-run the exact RTL command to confirm A/B/C end-to-end.

author: sebtardif
body:
`VMContinuationStack::initialize` writes control data and an args buffer at offsets below the top of the continuation stack, but does not verify that the total size fits within the allocated stack region.

### The problem

A Wasm module can define a continuation function type with a large number of parameters or return values. When `cont.new` is executed, the call chain reaches `initialize()` (`stack/unix.rs:226`), which computes:

`args_data_size = max(param_count, return_count) * size_of::<ValRaw>()`

The fixed header occupies 0x40 (64) bytes. If the total control data size (header + args buffer) exceeds the stack allocation, the write loop stores values past the stack region into adjacent memory. With the default 2 MiB stack, this requires 131,069+ params; with a smaller `async_stack_size`, fewer params suffice (e.g., 800 params on an 8 KiB stack).

Without this fix, the out-of-bounds write hits the guard page and crashes with SIGSEGV. With the fix, a clean error is returned instead.

### The fix

1. Replace the unchecked multiplication with `checked_mul` + `checked_add`, returning an error on arithmetic overflow.
2. Add a bounds check (`ensure!(total_control_size <= self.len)`) before any writes, so a high-arity function type produces a clean trap instead of a crash.
3. Change the return type of `initialize` from `()` to `Result<()>` and propagate the error through the `stack.rs` wrapper and the `cont_new` caller (which already returns `Result`).

### Test

A regression test (`stack_switching_cont_new_high_arity_rejected`) creates a function type with 800 `i32` params on an 8 KiB continuation stack, verifying that `cont.new` returns an error instead of crashing. The test skips gracefully on platforms where stack switching is not supported.

### Bug origin

Introduced in #10388 ("Stack switching: Infrastructure and runtime support", Frank Emrich, 2025-06-04).

**Standardization**

## Summary

## Phase 12B, Increment C — Agent Builder UI for BYO custom-tools / remote-MCP

Adds the **web UI** for Phase 12B's bring-your-own remote-MCP feature, consuming the already-merged backend from Increment A (#49) and Increment B (#50) **without changing it**. A user can register / list / test / delete a remote MCP (Streamable HTTP) server and attach its discovered tools to an agent by namespaced name.

> **Do not merge** — opened for owner authorization via governed agent-merge (same gate as A/B). Single-increment PR; not stacked on D/E.

### Default-OFF / inert
The whole surface is feature-flagged and inert by default. Unless `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ENABLED` is truthy, **no tab, no provider value, and no API call** is ever produced, and the app behaves byte-for-byte as before. This mirrors the existing Phase 11 library flag-gating exactly: server env → root `layout.tsx` (server component) → client `CustomToolsProvider` → `useContext`.

**Flag-OFF proof:**
- `customToolsConfig.ts` returns `{ enabled: false }` unless `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ENABLED` is truthy (default OFF).
- `StudioPanel` renders the "Custom tools" tab only under `{customToolsEnabled && …}`; tab state can only become `"tools"` via that gated button, so `McpServerBuilder` never mounts when off.
- `AgentBuilder`'s `refreshMcp` early-returns (`if (!customToolsEnabled) return;`) → **no `/api/agents/mcp-servers` call**; the `mcpTools` memo is `[]` and the MCP fieldset is gated, so nothing renders.
- No module-scope/import-time API calls — every MCP call lives inside a gated component or callback.

### What's included (UI — `app/web`)
- **`lib/api.ts`** — `list/create/update/delete/test` clients against `/api/agents/mcp-servers`, matching the verified camelCase contract and 204-delete.
- **`McpServerBuilder`** — register / test / delete with client-side validation that mirrors the backend grammar + caps; surfaces `lastError`, discovery results, and the **governance posture** (external risk, host-scoped egress, requires-approval-unless-trusted) projected from the backend `ToolSpec`. Governance is **not** reinvented in the UI.
- **`AgentBuilder`** — a gated "Custom tools (MCP)" fieldset that attaches/detaches tools by their `mcp:<server>/<tool>` namespaced name (consistent with how Increment B binds them at execution time), grouped per server with a posture badge, and keeps already-attached-but-now-removed tools detachable.
- **`StudioPanel`** — a third "Custom tools" tab, shown only when the flag is on.
- **`lib/customTools.ts`** — all logic kept in pure helpers so it can be unit-tested without a DOM (components stay thin).

### Infra (flag plumbing — default-OFF)
- **`infra/modules/web.bicep`** — emits `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ENABLED=true` to the web container **only when on** (mirrors `DOCUMENT_LIBRARY_ENABLED`); default OFF sets no env var.
- **`infra/main.bicep`** — passes the **existing** `customToolsEnabled` param (which already drives the API's `AI4IA_CUSTOM_TOOLS_ENABLED`) to the web module, so one infra flag governs both. `main.parameters.json` keeps it `false` → unchanged in every current environment.

### Tests
Adds **vitest** as the web app's first test runner (a `test` script + a minimal node-env config, **devDependencies only** — no runtime/bundle impact) and **24 unit tests** over the pure helpers: flag parsing, name/endpoint/secret validation, namespaced-name round-trip, approval posture, and the attachable-tools projection. **Pure helpers only — no RTL/jsdom/component tests.** Documents `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ENABLED` in `.env.example`.

### Validation (all green)
| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run lint` (app/web) | ✓ No ESLint warnings or errors |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` (app/web) | ✓ pass |
| `npm run build` (app/web) | ✓ compiled, type-check pass |
| `npm test` (app/web) | ✓ 24 passed |
| `az bicep build infra/main.bicep` | ✓ exit 0 |

No `app/api` changes → backend pytest/ruff baseline untouched.

### Follow-up
`npm test` (vitest) is intentionally **not** wired into `app-ci` in this PR — a CI-pipeline change is separate scope/risk, and the house-rule web validation stays lint/tsc/build (`npm test` is additive). Tracked so the suite can't silently rot:

- [ ] Wire `app/web` vitest (`npm test`) into app-ci — #52

author: rajmohanram
body:
## What
Three per-message hot-path allocation/CPU reductions found in a 5000 RPS review. No behavior change — all byte-identity-locked by existing tests.

- **W1** — JSON serializer memoizes the name-sorted field list per message type (`utils.rs`). The alphabetical key order (WAF byte-contract) is a pure function of the type, so a thread-local cache replaces the per-message **and per-nesting-level** `fields().collect() + sort`. Highest-value item (scales with payload nesting).
- **W2** — WebSocket authz headers: cache the per-direction template once per connection; per frame only `content-type` + `x-websocket-opcode` are overwritten in place (~9 String allocs/frame → 0–2). Shared `websocket_authz_header_set` builder guarantees byte-identity.
- **W3** — parallel gRPC paths take one `get_current_time` reading and derive both the transcode µs and dispatch-time ms (was 2 hostcalls/message).

## Safety
- W1 output locked by `json_oracle_tests` (byte-identity vs the original build-Value path).
- W2 output locked by `websocket_frame_subrequest_is_metadata_only` (updated to drive the new template+patch path).
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy --target wasm32-wasip1` / `cargo test` (56) all green.
- Validated in the local harness: gRPC allow/deny/streaming correct; `wasm_authz_transcode_grpc_us` + `wasm_authz_latency_ms` recording.

author: kim-em
body:
This PR adds the decomposition-group criterion for complete splitting: for a Galois number field `F / ℚ` and a prime `Q` of `𝓞 F` above a rational prime `p`, `TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot` shows `p` splits completely (there are `[F : ℚ]` primes of `𝓞 F` above `p`) if and only if the decomposition group of `Q` — its stabilizer under the natural action of `Gal(F/ℚ)` — is trivial. The proof is orbit–stabilizer: the Galois group acts on the primes above `p` with a single orbit (`Algebra.IsInvariant.orbit_eq_primesOver`), so the prime count is `[F : ℚ] / |decomposition group|`.

This is general Galois-number-field infrastructure for the multiquadratic prime-splitting law (Layer 1 of the multiquadratic roadmap), complementing the ramification/inertia counting criterion: it is the form needed to combine splitting across the quadratic subfields of a multiquadratic compositum.

author: jscott3201
body:
## What

PR-5 of the M0-completion sequence. Wires the `oce-api` `Engine<S: Store = MemStore>` facade to run a **hand-built** flattened `ModelGraph` end-to-end with **no parser** (the M0 path `load_cxf` will share in M1), and lands the M0 exit-criteria integration test.

### `oce-api` Engine wiring (`crates/oce-api/src/lib.rs`)
- **`Outputs`** — an owned, enumerable snapshot of the model's output-connector values (`get`/`iter`/`len`/`is_empty`). No store-backend type escapes the facade (R-API-8).
- **`build_model_in_memory(model)`** — instantiate blocks from the `oce-blocks` registry by `class_iri` (unknown class → typed `OcError::Load`, never a panic; R-IMPL-2/R-ERR-1), run `oce_graph::compile` (`BuildError` → `OcError::Build`), `allocate_state`, snapshot `Dir::Out` connectors, open the store durability lifecycle (`recover`). Fully resets per-run state (incl. `handles`) so a reload starts clean.
- **`tick(t_now) -> Result<&Outputs, OcError>`** — reject non-finite time (`OcError::NonFiniteTime`), then enforce monotonic non-decreasing `t_now` (`OcError::TimeRegression`) per CDL §7.16; evaluate one frozen-schedule tick via a scoped `EvalContext`; refresh and return the `Outputs` snapshot. M0 defers the per-tick `store.snapshot()` (R-HOT-1) to M1 (documented, not silent).
- Accessors `schedule()` / `outputs()` / `store()`.

### M0 exit-criteria harness (`crates/oce-api/src/tests.rs`, 6 tests)
Builds the canonical 6-block graph — `Constant(1)` → `Add` ↔ `UnitDelay` accumulator, plus `Constant(2.5)` + `Greater` + `Limiter[0,3]` — and asserts:
- BUILD succeeds for the loop-broken graph;
- **two independent compiles are byte-identical** on `order`/`connector_order`/`driver_of` **and** on the allocated state layout (`words`/`slot_of`) — exit #3 determinism;
- a multi-tick run advances the accumulator **1, 2, 3, 4** (the true one-tick feedback delay the two-pass eval guarantees), with `Greater(>2.5)` = F,F,T,T and `Limiter[0,3]` = 1,2,3,3 — exit #3;
- an injected algebraic loop → typed `BuildError::AlgebraicLoop` — exit #4;
- an unknown class → typed `OcError::Load`;
- tick time is monotonic and finite;
- a `MemStore` model round-trip + no-op `commit`/`flush`/`recover` through the engine — exit #5.

This test **is** M0 exit criteria #3/#4/#5; with PR-1..PR-4 it closes M0 #1–#6.

## Review

Adversarially reviewed by two independent agents (code-reviewer + a correctness skeptic). Verdict: **sound, no Critical/Important correctness bug**; the skeptic hand-traced every asserted value. Findings addressed in this PR: NaN/∞ time guard (`NonFiniteTime`), explicit M0-scope doc for the deferred `store.snapshot()`, `handles` reset on reload, state-layout determinism assertion, `Outputs::get` deferral note. Structural-validation of malformed models (index-panic) is documented as the loader/`oce-validate` invariant and deferred to M1.

## Gates

All green locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (workspace `--all-targets`), workspace tests (37), rustdoc `-D warnings --document-private-items`, file-size cap, default-no-db, no-secret. No manifest changes (cargo-deny skips).

Aaron 2026-06-15 (shadow*): *"CTM is the interface Society expects individual or collective units to look like; ISociety is the interface that CTMs expect."*

Captures the **duality**: CTM and ISociety are dual interfaces across one membrane (the Markov boundary). Looking **in**, every member presents a **CTM** (world-model-loop shape); looking **out**, every member sees an **ISociety** (two-way scheduler). **Hexagonal ports** (Cockburn): CTM = port the society drives, ISociety = port the CTM drives. **Self-similar/scale-free:** a fused collective presents the *same* CTM interface as an individual (one external address) → "unit" = CTM at every scale; a society can be a CTM in a larger ISociety, recursively.

Peels: both sides are **reframes** (CTM-member contract must be defined; ISociety is §4-design); **don't over-claim a formal adjunction** ("⊣" = port-duality; adjointness is a math-team question); in-face borrows the CTM *architecture*, not its consciousness axioms. markdownlint EXIT=0.

author: mrrealorg
body:
## Summary

Three security/correctness fixes in 2 files:

### Fix #139 — CORS whitelist still allows opencode.ai

The CORS origin regex in `middleware.ts` still whitelisted `*.opencode.ai`. After the rebrand to MiMo Code, the web UI and desktop app originate from `mimo.xiaomi.com`, so cross-origin requests were blocked.

**Fix:** Update regex from `opencode.ai` to `mimo.xiaomi.com`.

### Fix #154 — Stack traces leaked in 500 error responses

The error handler sent `err.stack` (full stack trace with file paths, line numbers, dependency versions) to the client in JSON error responses.

**Fix:** Use `err.message` instead, which gives the error description without internal details.

### Fix #156 — MCP access token partially visible in auth status

`mcp auth status` displayed the first 20 characters of the OAuth access token. This could be captured via screen recordings, terminal logs, or shoulder-surfing.

**Fix:** Replace with `"present"` / `"missing"` indicator.

author: daniel-startti
body:
## Summary

Structural follow-up to the text fix in #98. `DagToolExecutor` now **intercepts** the first `gsheets_run_python` that binds a sheet **not read this turn**: instead of running the code blind, it returns an `inspect_first` envelope carrying a **bounded markdown preview** (header + 5 rows) of each unread sheet, marks the sheet seen, and forces the agent to re-call with informed code. This makes a weak model (gemini-2.5-flash) safe — guaranteeing it sees the real columns regardless of capability, closing the ceiling the text fix alone couldn't.

**How:**
- Per-turn read-state on `DagToolExecutor` (`Mutex<HashSet<"spreadsheet_id::sheet">>`). The executor is built once per `llm_call` execution → naturally per-turn, no cross-turn persistence (consistent with the no-cache stance of expand-merges). Verified: the executor is passed by `&` into `AgentService::run` and `execute(&self)` is called for every tool call on the one instance.
- `gsheets_read` (success) marks a sheet seen; `gsheets_run_python` checks its sheet bindings before executing.
- The intercept reuses `dispatch_gsheets_read` for the preview (markdown, with expand-merges applied), truncated to 6 rows. Inline (`data:`) bindings are skipped. No-loop invariant: the intercept marks each previewed sheet **before** returning.
- Pure decision/rendering helpers in new module `gsheets_inspect_guard.rs`.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-15-gsheets-inspect-guard-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-15-gsheets-inspect-guard.md` · CHANGELOG §37.

**Honest limit:** the guard guarantees the agent SEES the table, not that it uses the columns correctly. Combined with the §36 detective rule (0 rows → stop) the net is strong, not a 100% guarantee on a weak model.

## Test Plan

- [x] 10 unit tests for the pure helpers (decision + markdown rendering)
- [x] `cargo test --verbose` full: **1831 passed, 0 failed**; clippy clean
- [x] Final holistic code review: APPROVED (verified no Mutex-across-await; per-turn executor lifetime; success-only marking; no-error envelope)
- [x] **E2E real (Google Sheets, sheet with merged Categoria column):**
  - Mechanism test (forces blind run_python): guard **intercepts** with `inspect_first` preview → flash re-calls and, having seen the `Categoria` column, applies +10 to the 3 frutas correctly (Manzana/Banana/Pera; Verduras untouched). Per-turn marking dedupes (1 real intercept).
  - Realistic vague prompt: flash reads first on its own → guard correctly does NOT fire (no spurious intercept, happy path intact).
- [x] ADP-clean (executor-internal; `inspect_first` is a tool result the agent consumes in-loop, does not cross the SSE boundary)

author: jimmy-guzman
body:
## What

- Adds **oxlint** (`oxlint --lsp`) as a second LSP diagnostics source alongside `typescript-language-server`, labeled `[oxc]` in the problems panel. A changed JS/TS file now runs through both servers and their findings merge into the single `diagnostics` source.
- Generalizes the pipeline from one-server-per-file to a set of servers per file: `serversForPath`, a per-server handshake (oxlint advertises `workspace.configuration` and answers the `workspace/configuration` request via a new per-server `onRequest` hook in the transport), and the per-file merge precedence `findings > pending > clean > failed > unavailable`.
- Runs the servers **concurrently** and **streams** a coherent snapshot as each finishes, instead of waiting for the slowest before showing anything.
- **Holds each file's prior badge** across a re-run; only edited/new/cold-start files show `pending`, so stable files no longer flicker to pending while a slower server is still running.

## Why

- sideye only surfaced TypeScript diagnostics, so lint findings never appeared. oxlint fits the existing `npm install <package>` provisioner (one binary, simple push handshake), works zero-config, and is what sideye itself uses; the ESLint LSP would require building `microsoft/vscode-eslint` from source, which does not fit the provisioner.
- Running the two servers sequentially behind a single combined emission made diagnostics feel slower than running oxc/tsc directly. The work is I/O-bound (waiting on LSP processes), so concurrency + progressive streaming — not worker threads — surfaces fast results immediately.
- Resetting already-resolved files to `pending` on every quiet re-run was visual churn. Holding the prior badge until the new result arrives matches how editors behave and SPEC's "late diagnostics fill badges in place".

author: fruithappens
body:
## The bug (order #165)
A fresh customer texted **"oat latte"** with **no station specified**. The order was silently placed on **Station 1 — which couldn't make oat** — and the customer got a cheery *"Order #165 confirmed, being made now"* SMS. It never warned them, and the order sat un-brewable until oat was manually enabled on Station 1.

This is the real #165 fix. PR #76 handled a *different* path (a station explicitly requested). #165 had no station specified, so it went through the auto-router `_assign_station`.

## Root cause: two milk checks disagreed
- The SMS **milk gate** (`_milk_is_makeable`) **fails open** when no active station defines `milk_types` (unconfigured / Quick-Setup stations) → "oat" is accepted.
- But `_assign_station` substituted a hardcoded `['full cream','skim']` default for those same stations, found no station "with" oat, and hit `return 1` — a **silent station-1 fallback** that masked the failure, so `_confirm_order` created the order and sent a false confirmation.

## Fix
- **Unconfigured stations are now a wildcard** (can make any milk/size) inside `_assign_station`, matching the gate's fail-open and `order_capable()`. Oat at unconfigured stations now routes to a real station instead of stranding.
- The silent `return 1, False` fallbacks now **`return None, False`**.
- On `None`, `_confirm_order` now **asks the customer for a milk we can make** (and parks the conversation at `awaiting_milk` so their reply continues the same order) — never confirms onto a station that can't make it. The generic "no stations available" message is kept for the genuinely-no-stations case.
- Break-period milk filter gets the same wildcard treatment.

Behaviour chosen by the operator: *tell the customer + ask for another milk* (never silently substitute).

## Tests
- New `test_milk_capability_routing.py` — **13 offline assertions**: wildcard routing, None-not-station-1, route-to-the-oat-station, normal-milk still routes, and the customer re-ask wiring (re-ask not confirm; generic message when truly no stations).
- `test_sms_conversation_flow.py` baseline unchanged (its 4 failures pre-date this PR — stale "prompt for sugar" tests from the old flow).
- Backend-only; frontend bundle hash unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Adds detection and notification for provisional (unconfirmed) candles across multiple analysis tools. When the latest candle timestamp matches today's UTC start time (indicating real-time data), a ℹ️ note is prepended to the summary and a `provisional: true` flag is added to the response metadata.

## Key Changes

- **New utility module** (`lib/provisional-bar.ts`):
  - `isLatestBarProvisional()`: Detects if the latest candle is unconfirmed by comparing its timestamp to today's UTC start
  - `prependProvisionalNote()`: Prepends the "ℹ️ 最新足は未確定（形成中）" note to summary text

- **Updated analysis tools** to detect and report provisional status:
  - `analyze_stoch_snapshot.ts`: Checks latest bar timestamp in both default (analyzeIndicators) and custom (getCandles) paths
  - `analyze_ema_snapshot.ts`: Detects provisional status for both fixed-periods and custom-periods modes
  - `analyze_bb_snapshot.ts`: Adds provisional detection and note to both default and extended modes
  - `analyze_sma_snapshot.ts`: Detects provisional status from latest normalized candle
  - `analyze_ichimoku_snapshot.ts`: Checks latest bar timestamp for provisional detection

- **Schema updates** (`src/schema/analysis.ts`):
  - Added optional `provisional: boolean` field to meta schemas for:
    - AnalyzeStochSnapshotMetaSchemaOut
    - AnalyzeEmaSnapshotMetaSchemaOut
    - AnalyzeBbSnapshotMetaSchemaOut
    - AnalyzeSmaSnapshotMetaSchemaOut
    - AnalyzeIchimokuSnapshotMetaSchemaOut

- **Comprehensive test coverage**:
  - Added test suites for all five analysis tools verifying:
    - Real-time (provisional) candles trigger the note and set `provisional=true`
    - Historical (confirmed) candles do not trigger the note or flag
    - Both data fetch paths (analyzeIndicators vs getCandles) are tested where applicable

- **Explicit non-applicability notes** in tools where provisional detection doesn't apply:
  - `get_flow_metrics.ts`: Uses transaction buckets, not OHLC candles
  - `detect_whale_events.ts`: Analyzes current orderbook snapshot, not candle values

## Implementation Details

- The provisional detection is independent of the warning system (⚠️ warning vs ℹ️ note)
- Summary prepending order: ⚠️ warnings → ℹ️ provisional note → main content (warnings shown first)
- Detection uses `dayjs().utc().startOf('day').valueOf()` to identify today's UTC start
- Works across both default parameter paths (analyzeIndicators) and custom parameter paths (getCandles)

author: tjackiet
body:
## Summary

Establishes structural safeguards against handler-schema divergence by introducing two complementary contract test systems for the indicators pipeline. This prevents a recurrence of the previous bug where `analyze_indicators` handler referenced non-existent `indicators.series.*` keys while tests remained green due to hand-mocked fixtures.

## Key Changes

- **New contract test file** (`tests/indicators-contract.test.ts`):
  - **Schema contract (A)**: Validates that `computeAllIndicators` output conforms to `IndicatorsInternalSchema` via strict parsing, detecting unknown key injection and missing key paths
  - **Real pipeline contract (B)**: Tests the full fetch → get_candles → analyzeIndicators → handler flow with only fetch mocked, ensuring handlers correctly read from the actual flat series structure
  - Includes regression tests that deliberately rename keys to prove contract violations are detected

- **Export `computeAllIndicators`** (`tools/analyze_indicators.ts`):
  - Made the function public so contract tests can directly validate its output against the schema
  - Added clarifying comment explaining why this is exported

- **Updated handler test documentation** (`tests/analyzeIndicatorsHandler.test.ts`):
  - Clarified that the hand-mocked fixture shape is now structurally validated by the contract tests
  - Documents the previous bug where a non-existent `series` wrapper was injected, masking the real issue

## Implementation Details

The contract tests use real normalized candles (via `getCandles`) rather than hand-crafted fixtures, ensuring the test validates the actual data shape flowing through the production pipeline. The schema contract uses Zod's `strict()` mode to catch unknown keys and standard `parse()` to catch type mismatches and missing nested keys. This dual approach catches both handler-side key path errors (like the previous `indicators.series.*` bug) and schema definition drift.

author: alnoki
body:
# Background

Agent-filed findings (the `audit-loop`) and hand-filed to-dos
(`linear-task`) all funneled through one umbrella issue, ENG-452, which
doubled as both a filing bucket and the PR staging plan (a wave/session
checklist buried in its description). This conflated two jobs and hid the
plan inside an issue. This PR splits them and threads Linear issue status
through the worktree skills.

The split: findings now land as **plain Backlog issues with no parent**,
and a new `stage-backlog` skill turns that flat queue into a PR plan —
merging issues that share a PR into one canonical issue and rewriting the
[implementation-sequence](https://linear.app/dasmac/document/implementation-sequence-9564c1e7cb56)
Linear document as a dependency tree.

# Changes

1. **`linear-task` files into the Backlog, parentless.**
   ([linear-task](.claude/skills/linear-task/SKILL.md)) Pins
   `state: "Backlog"`, no `parentId`; notes that staging is owned by
   `stage-backlog`, not a parent issue.

2. **New `stage-backlog` skill.**
   ([stage-backlog](.claude/skills/stage-backlog/SKILL.md)) Loopable +
   on-demand. Reads the Backlog, groups issues into the fewest
   file-disjoint PRs, **merges multi-issue PRs into one canonical issue
   write-before-close** (folds notes + the union of `**Fingerprint**:`
   lines, then marks the rest `duplicateOf`), adversarially cross-checks
   the grouping, and rewrites the document. Issue refs are written as bare
   `ENG-###` tags so Linear renders live status.

3. **`audit-loop` de-umbrellaed.**

body:
## What

Restores `discover_cd_hearings()` and `discover_events()` after `webapi.legistar.com` began returning hard 403s to all keyless callers. The connector now falls back to scraping the public web calendar at `legistar.council.nyc.gov/Calendar.aspx` — which lists the same meetings — behind the unchanged `discover_*` interface.

## Why

The Legistar REST API vendor (Granicus) locked the public endpoint. There is no self-serve token portal; a key comes only from the vendor. Plan-B: the public web calendar returns 200 and contains the same events in a Telerik RadGrid. Scraping it and reshaping each row into the REST API Event dict lets `_event_to_civic` map both sources identically without changes to any caller.

## How

- `_fetch_events(start, end)` — new internal router: tries the REST API first; on any exception falls back to `_scrape_calendar_events()`; if both fail, returns `[]`. Both `discover_events` and `discover_cd_hearings` now delegate to this single seam.
- `_parse_calendar_html(html)` — anchors on `_hypMeetingDetail` links (whose `ID=` query param is the Legistar EventId) rather than the grid element id, which resolves to a wrapper `<div>` under the stdlib HTML parser.
- Scrape path sorts results ascending after filtering to the window, honoring `discover_cd_hearings`' documented ordering contract (the calendar is newest-first by default).
- `bs4` guard is independent of the `httpx`/`tenacity` guard so a missing bs4 disables only the HTML parse, not the API path.
- `beautifulsoup4>=4.12` added to `requirements.txt`; `html.parser` only (no lxml).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest ingest/tests -q` — 167 passed (full venv)
- [x] CI simulation (httpx + bs4 blocked) — 162 passed / 5 skipped, rc=0
- [x] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` — clean
- [x] `mypy ingest` — 23 errors, baseline unchanged (zero regression)
- [x] Live `discover_cd_hearings("M11", days_ahead=30)` — 5 hearings returned, no 403, ascending order
- [x] `test_fetch_events_fail_soft_returns_empty` — API 403 + scrape RuntimeError returns `[]`, no raise
- [x] `test_fetch_events_sorts_scrape_results_ascending` — descending input produces ascending output

## What this is NOT

Does not add tenacity retries to `_scrape_calendar_events` — left for a follow-up if the calendar proves flaky. The `discover_events` `since` parameter branches are not independently unit-tested (follow-up issue).

author: filippoautiero007
body:
This PR addresses two high-priority security vulnerabilities related to origin validation:

1. **CORS Origin Regex Bypass**: The previous regex `r"https://(?:tracenet|nettrace)(?:-git-[^.]+)?\.vercel\.app"` lacked an end anchor, allowing attackers to bypass CORS using domains like `https://tracenet.vercel.app.attacker.com`. I've added the `$` anchor to strictly enforce the domain.

2. **Insecure Auth Origin Check**: The authentication service was trusting the `Origin` header as a fallback for the `azp` claim check. Since `Origin` can be easily spoofed by non-browser clients, this could lead to authorization bypasses. Validation now strictly relies on the signed `azp` claim within the JWT.

Additionally, I fixed a Pydantic validation regression in the `GenerateResponse` model by using `Union` types, ensuring compatibility with the diverse data shapes returned by the generation service.

All 143 backend tests passed successfully.
Critical security learnings have been documented in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

body:
**PLEASE DELETE HANDOFF DOC BEFORE MERGE**

## Summary

Replaces the Visual Editor API's JSDoc (`src/index.d.ts`) with a full rewrite grounded in the actual app implementation, plus a `HANDOFF.md` documenting type-level follow-ups the comment pass can't make. The previous JSDoc was AI-generated and unreliable (e.g. `@throws {FileNotFoundError}` / `{CollectionNotFoundError}` that are never thrown). Since `platform-documentation` generates the developer reference directly from this file, these comments **are** the published reference.

## What changed

**`src/index.d.ts` — JSDoc rewrite (comments + one type change):**

- Removed hallucinated `@throws`; only the real `Error` cases documented, with actual failure modes described instead (resolve-`undefined`, the `items()` falsy-key hang).
- `@example` on every method and property; consistent present-tense voice; CloudCannon terminology capitalized ("Configuration File", "Team Member", "Data Panel"); no em dashes.
- Object descriptions follow a consistent shape — *Represents… / Returned by / Accessed through… / Additionally, you can…*; property descriptions are blunt and verb-first (*Holds… / Provides…*).
- Event listeners documented on all interfaces, each with a named-handler example; the `event.detail` payload (`isNew`, `sourcePath`) documented once in the reference's Events section rather than repeated.
- `Collection.items()` / `Dataset.items()` document their (verified, asymmetric) bad-key behavior: a non-matching Collection key resolves to `[]`, while a Dataset hangs.
- `File.data`/`content` reframed as entry points (no longer duplicate the child `get()` examples); `FileData`/`FileContent` lead with "Accessed through a File's `data`/`content` property".
- `data.upload` documents its save semantics and uses a self-contained example; `edit` reworded; `EditOptions.slug` generalized to cover both `edit` and `upload`; void mutators say "Has no effect if the file does not exist".
- Removed a false `datasets()` reference from `Dataset`; added `files()` to the `File` "Returned by" list.
- **One type change** (the only signature edit): narrowed `File.get()`, `claimLock()`, `releaseLock()` to `… | undefined`, matching the verified handler behavior (the message handler returns `undefined` for any unresolved `sourcePath`).

**`HANDOFF.md` (new):** maintainer follow-ups that require type/code changes, tiered by priority:

- **Tier 1 (verified correctness):** `FileContent.get()` throws on a missing file instead of resolving `undefined` (client bug); `data.upload` surfaces `style`/`position` it ignores; `FileMetadata.last_modified` is typed `string | Date` but the client only ever receives a string (JSON boundary); `FileData`/`FileContent` `addEventListener` never fire (no `:data:`/`:content:` events are dispatched).
- **Tier 2 (confirm against implementation):** `AddArrayItemOptions.value` optionality; whether a `datasets()` method should exist.
- **Tier 3 (optional polish):** typing `event.detail`; naming inline option literals (`GetDataOptions`, `PanelPosition`); a V0 listener-union cleanup.

Each Tier 1 item cites the specific app code it was verified against.

author: ifkumrfnl
body:
## Summary

Step 7 slice 3 deepens the VP8L lossless encoder's entropy modeling, mirroring the decode side (`color_cache.zig`, `meta_prefix.zig`, `prefix_groups.zig`, and the `entropy.zig` group-store path). All work lives in `src/vp8l/encoder.zig`; no public API change was needed (`encodeLossless` already exposes the path).

Delivered:

- **Optional color cache.** The LZ77 token stream is lowered to an op stream while exactly simulating the decoder's cache: every copied pixel is inserted one-at-a-time in raster order using the materialized main-image pixels, and a literal already sitting at its hashed slot becomes a cache-index green symbol (`green_base + index`). This is the exact inverse of `color_cache.zig` + `entropy.zig`. An empty-channel-histogram guard keeps each prefix code a valid single-leaf tree (fixes the solid all-zero image, whose first pixel hits the zero-initialized cache and emits no literals).
- **Optional entropy image / multiple Huffman groups (meta-prefix).** The image is tiled into prefix blocks (log2 in [3,5]), blocks are clustered greedily by green-histogram L1 distance into <=16 groups, and the entropy image (red high byte / green low byte) is emitted as a transform-role literal stream followed by per-group prefix codes and a group-selected symbol stream — inverting `meta_prefix.zig` + `prefix_groups.zig`.
- **Measure-by-encoding gate.** Both the cache and multi-group choices are gated on the REAL encoded size: each candidate is fully encoded into a scratch buffer and only the smallest is re-emitted, so a candidate is never kept when it would enlarge the output. Heuristic estimates only rank candidates; the keep/drop decision is exact (`BitWriter` raises `OutputTooLarge` on overflow, so any over-large trial falls back safely).

## Round-trip / validity result

Core gate met. The committed corpus round-trip test (`src/testing/corpus.zig`) decodes every still VP8L corpus file to RGBA, re-encodes with the new encoder, decodes again, and asserts the source pixels are bit-identical — it passes under `zig build test` with the richer encoder. `zig fmt --check .` is clean and `zig build test` is fully green (existing decode, corpus-hash, and fuzz-smoke tests all pass). Synthetic edge cases (1x1, solid all-zero, solid color, two-axis gradient, full-range alpha, single-row/column, palettes) remain covered, plus 5 new slice-3 tests.

Size (reported, not a CI gate): locally against libwebp 1.5.0, all 43 still VP8L corpus files round-trip bit-exactly through `dwebp` (0 mismatches), and the per-file median size-vs-`cwebp -lossless` ratio dropped from slice 2's 1.0986x to 1.0368x (37/43 at/below 1.10x; range 0.92x–1.59x), with no file larger than the slice-2 encoding.

## Caveats

- The `cwebp`/`dwebp` measurements were run locally via a throwaway tool (since removed; only `encoder.zig` and `PROGRESS.MD` are committed). CI does not run `cwebp`/`dwebp`; validity rests on the committed own-decoder corpus round-trip test, exactly as prior slices.
- The median size gate (1.0368x) holds, but 6 photographic files (lossless1–4, lossless_color_transform, near_lossless_75) remain individually above 1.10x; closing those needs per-block predictor selection, a later refinement beyond this slice.
- Multi-group clustering is a simple greedy green-histogram L1 scheme bounded at 16 groups with a fixed distance threshold — correctness-safe (the measure-by-encoding gate only keeps it when it wins) but a heuristic, not optimal clustering.
- Robustness hardening / fuzzing depth was intentionally NOT expanded here (deferred to Step 11). Coverage-guided fuzzing (`zig build test --fuzz`) remains blocked by the known upstream Zig 0.16.0 test-runner bug noted in `PROGRESS.MD`, unchanged by this slice.

## Review focus

- **Multi-group descriptor scratch bound (minor, non-blocking).** `maxEncodedSize()` reserves a fixed `descriptor_bound` of 65536 bytes for ALL prefix-code descriptors. A 16-group plan with full-alphabet (base + 1024 cache symbols) descriptors could pathologically approach/exceed this. Not a correctness bug: the multi-group trial is wrapped in `catch` and falls back to single-group on `OutputTooLarge`, so the worst case is a missed optimization, never a crash or corrupt stream. Worth a comment or a group-count-scaled bound.
- **Heuristic estimates are non-load-bearing.** `descriptorOverheadEstimate` / `entropyImageBitsEstimate` only rank candidate block sizes; the final keep/drop is gated on the exact `bitLength` of a real trial encoding. Confirmed off the correctness path.
- **No end-to-end assertion that the cache path is actually selected (test gap, minor).** Round-trip tests are path-agnostic; white-box coverage stops at the `lowerOps` helper (unlike the color-transform path, which has an end-to-end "saw_color" assertion). A future regression silently disabling the cache in the full encoder would not be caught. A white-box test asserting `encodeAlloc` selects a non-zero cache size on a cache-favorable input would close this.
- **`lowerOps` fixture tests are narrower than their names imply (minor).** They prove the cache-insert-on-copy rule for specific hand-aligned fixtures; real consistency is guarded by the corpus + synthetic round-trips.
- **`emitMultiGroup` re-lowers ops and rebuilds histograms twice (trial + real emit) (minor).** Correct and deterministic, but redundant work; could cache the lowered ops/codes from the trial. Pure performance/cleanliness.

author: chokobole
body:
## Description

`prove_jagged_pyramid` stacked the per-layer per-round schedule (gather / eq
lookups / live-pair mask / phase flags) into the scan `xs` as a **host-baked
constant at the fixed `plane_width`**. On a real shard (`plane_width ≈ 2.3M`)
that bakes multi-GB int32 `DenseElementsAttr` constants — `gather` alone is
`(layers, max_rounds, 2.3M)` ≈ 5.3 GB — which jax→StableHLO cannot construct, so
the rolled prove never reached a real shard (the chain-c blocker on
fractalyze/sp1-zorch#55, spec'd in fractalyze/sp1-zorch#109).

Reconstruct the schedule **in-body from the compact runtime `row_counts`**
instead: the counts halve each round (`counts_k = ceil(row_counts / 2^k)`) and
every index pattern is `iota` + segment offsets, so the scan carries only an
`nseg`-wide row-count channel and the schedule lowers as ops, not baked
constants.

Correctness is pinned by a byte-match to the existing numpy reference:
`_padded_round_schedule_jax` == `_padded_round_schedule` across shapes (incl.
koalabearx4 and inactive surplus rounds, and under `jit`); the rolled prove
stays byte-identical to the unrolled `ProveChain`; and a guard test asserts the
trace bakes no plane-width int32 schedule constant.

The numpy `_padded_round_schedule` is retained as the readable byte-match
oracle, and `_layer_plane_width` is shared by the prover and the test so their
fixed widths cannot drift. nseg-tiny broadcast `_excl_cumsum` / segment lookup
stand in for `jnp.cumsum` (absent in this fork) and `jnp.searchsorted`.

## Related Issues/PRs

Part of fractalyze/sp1-zorch#109 (the schedule-baking fix) and
fractalyze/sp1-zorch#55 (roll the GKR pyramid). This lands the core on the
**unmarked** rolled prove; the marked path (fractalyze/zorch#261) inherits it on
rebase, and the real-shard marked compile/warm number vs SP1 ~81 ms is the
remaining #109 step (needs a GPU window).

- [x] Commit messages follow Commit Message Guideline
- [x] Checked Pull Request Guideline

body:
This task implements the core requirements of the "Iterative Darwin Flow — Architecture Milestone". 

Key improvements:
1. **Dynamic Expansion Control**: The branching width (population size) and iteration limits are now dynamically calculated based on the user-defined expansion setting in the ChatSession. Low expansion (1-3) results in 2 branches and 2 iterations, while High expansion (8-10) scales up to 4 branches and 10 iterations.
2. **Multi-Lineage Survival**: Transitioned the Darwin loop from a single-winner model to a multi-lineage evolutionary system. Now, both the winning variant (ACTIVE) and high-scoring alternatives (KEPT) survive and serve as ancestors for the next generation.
3. **Lineage Preservation**: Updated the export system to include a 'lineage_preservation.md' file. This document captures rejected engineering philosophies and failure fingerprints, ensuring that future iterations do not rediscover already rejected or failing ideas.
4. **Enhanced Spawner Prompting**: Refactored the DarwinVariantSpawner to handle multiple ancestors in the lineage context, forcing the LLM to consider and cross-pollinate established successful theories.

These changes transform the Darwin Engine into a true evolutionary search system as defined in the architectural vision.

- AC: Safe read-only RPC methods should be covered or explicitly omitted — satisfied by exposing `events.relation_evidence` and `sources.status.view` as typed tools.

**`tests/test_anga_variant_feeds.py`** (new) — 10 tests:

"Send a friend a link." Builds on the Phase 1 tenant core (#13) to make the web voice client multi-user and invite-only.

## What's here
- **`server.py`** serves the **guest** agent (account-free toolset), not the owner agent. Both `/live-token` and `/agent` are **invite-gated** by a per-friend token (`friends.json`: token → user_id) — unknown token → **403**, so strangers can't run up your Gemini/Claude bill. `/agent` sets the tenant context for the request → **isolated per-user memory + guest mode + a per-friend thread** (`guest-<uid>`), always reset in a `finally`.
- **Guest Live prompt** advertises only memory/web/weather (no email/calendar), so the front model sets the right expectations.
- **`index.html`** reads the invite token from `?t=` and passes it through; clean "invalid invite" message.
- **`add_friend.py`** generates a token + prints the invite link (reuses a friend's token so their memory persists). `friends.json` gitignored; `friends.example.json` shipped.

## Safety
- Invite-only; each friend isolated (own memory collection, own thread, restricted tools); owner data never exposed.
- 4 new tests prove the gating + that a valid token routes into an isolated guest context (right user, `guest-<uid>` thread, context cleaned up after). 216 pass.

After this: **Phase 3** — host on a ~$5 VPS / the Pi with a stable HTTPS domain. **Phase 4** — per-friend cost caps.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
[StableHLO] Fix mutation of `inputs` in `stablehlo.scatter` op interpreter

The `inputs` operand of the `stablehlo.scatter` op was getting modified by the interpreter. This is wrong behavior because SSA values are immutable.

The reason this was happening was because both `results` and `inputs` were pointing to the same data within the interpreter and thus `inputs` was getting modified when `results` was computed.

We fix that by introducing a new `clone()` function for Tensor's and using it to initialize `results`.

- `components/pr-lifecycle/test/ai/miniforge/pr_lifecycle/monitor_loop_test.clj:144` — Inner testing block label says 'heartbeat fires even when poll-pr-for-new-comments returns zero comments' but the assertion only checks that every iter-events entry has a nat-int? :iteration — which was already confirmed by the count and sequential assertions above. The label describes a causal claim; the assertion doesn't demonstrate it. The no-new-comments stub is wired globally for all runs in this test via run-with-stubs, so the causal relationship is real, but the assertion doesn't express it.
- `components/pr-lifecycle/test/ai/miniforge/pr_lifecycle/monitor_loop_test.clj:126` — testing label 'finalize-loop-iteration! emits ...' names a private implementation function. Tests should express the observable contract, not the implementation path. The label ties the test to the internal function name, which will silently mis-document if the function is renamed.
- `components/pr-lifecycle/test/ai/miniforge/pr_lifecycle/monitor_loop_test.clj:72` — ok docstring says 'dag/err? treats as success' but the map shape uses :ok? true, not an :error or :err? key. dag/err? typically tests for error presence; the described predicate doesn't match the key in use. Minor but misleading for anyone reading the stub to understand what the SUT expects.
- `components/pr-lifecycle/test/ai/miniforge/pr_lifecycle/monitor_loop_test.clj:77` — make-test-monitor docstring states ':event-bus is required for emission assertions' but structurally it defaults to nil when called with {} or no args. The zero-arity call path (make-test-monitor) would silently produce a monitor with :event-bus nil, not an error. The docstring overstates the constraint.
- `components/pr-lifecycle/test/ai/miniforge/pr_lifecycle/monitor_loop_test.clj:141` — Assertion (= [1 2 3] (mapv :iteration iter-events)) hardcodes the literal sequence rather than deriving it from n-iters. If n-iters changes, the expected-vector must be updated separately.
