author: paljort
body:
### What is in this PR
This PR refactors the Local Baserow Get Row service type to conditionally return `None` for the data, when a row isn't found. Previously, we would always raise an error. Now, based on the dispatch context, we either raise or return `None`.

We also updated the sample data logic in the Automations frontend, specifically the concept around knowing if "a node is tested". We previously just checked if `sample.data` is falsey, and if so, consider the node as not tested. Now that a Read a Row node can have `sample.data = null`, we check the envelope/wrapper instead. Here is how the sample data looks when a row is not found:
```python
{"data": null, "status": 200, "output_uid": ""}
```

So, to know whether a node is tested or not, we now check if `getSampleData()` itself returns `null`, as opposed to an object where the `data` field is `null`.

The main benefit of this change is to allow Automation uses to be able to decide what to do when a Read a row node doesn't find a row; they can use a Router node to take the next step. Previously, the workflow would just error and stop.

[This community member](https://community.baserow.io/t/the-best-method-logic-to-use-when-updating-rows-in-one-db-from-another/11695/13) would benefit immediately from this change.

Closes https://github.com/baserow/baserow/issues/4512

### How to test this PR
In `develop`, create a Read a row node that doesn't match any rows (an invalid row ID or a filter that forces no match), then test that node. You'll see the node errors, and if you test the workflow, it stops at this node.

In this branch, you can create a Router node that has a branch with this condition `is_empty(get('previous_node.42.id'))`. If you test the node, you'll see that this branch is reached when a row is not found, and no error is thrown.

author: ziatdinovmax
body:
## Summary

Two small, independent UI fixes:

1. **Silence the Streamlit deprecation warnings.** `st.components.v1.html` is deprecated in Streamlit 1.58 and printed repeated console warnings on every rerun. Migrated the affected calls to `st.html`.

2. **Fix the mode-selector buttons becoming a cramped/truncated mess when the window is resized narrow.** The `Mission Control / Analyze / Plan` buttons used to shrink until their labels truncated (e.g. `Analyze` → `Analy`) and the icon button collided with its neighbours. They now keep full labels and stay clean at every width.

Both are scoped to the UI layer; no agent or analysis behavior changes.

---

## Technical details

### 1. Migrate `st.components.v1.html` → `st.html`
`scilink/ui/theme.py` (3 calls), `scilink/ui/components/sidebar.py` (1 call)

- The deprecation message suggests `st.iframe`, but that takes a URL/Path — it cannot render the raw `<script>` HTML these call sites inject, so it is **not** a valid replacement here. These calls use `components.html` purely to run JS that restyles widgets (theme) or paints a shutdown screen (sidebar) by reaching the app DOM via `window.parent.document`.
- Correct replacement: `st.html(body, unsafe_allow_javascript=True)`, which inserts the HTML inline and executes its JS. `st.html` is not iframed, so `window.parent` resolves to the app window and the existing `window.parent.document` references keep working. Dropped the now-invalid `height=` argument and the `components` import.
- **Verified** headlessly with `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`: `inject_theme()` runs to completion in both light and dark branches plus the collision-JS slot, with no exceptions, and the emitted `st.html` elements carry their `<script>` payloads intact.

### 2. Mode-selector responsive layout
`scilink/ui/app.py`, `scilink/ui/theme.py`

- **Cause:** the buttons sat in the center column of `st.columns([1, 2, 1])` and were further inset by 1.5-unit padding columns, leaving the three buttons ~25% of the page width split three ways. A prior `flex-wrap: nowrap` rule stopped them wrapping to a second row but made them shrink-and-truncate at narrow widths / high display scaling.
- **Fix:**
  - `app.py`: dropped the padding columns — one equal column per mode (`st.columns(len(_modes))`).
  - `theme.py` (light + dark blocks): each mode button now sizes to its label (`min-width: max-content`, `white-space: nowrap`, no ellipsis); the row is centered with `flex-wrap: wrap` + `gap`. A button can no longer be narrower than its text, so truncation is impossible — worst case the row wraps to a centered second line.
- **Verified** with Playwright at 1440 / 1100 / 820 / 600 / 480 px: `truncated=False` for every button at every width (programmatic `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` check), full labels, single clean centered row throughout — including 480px, the original failure width.

author: reaandrew
body:
## What

Adds **`loadr-plugin-rabbitmq`**, a runtime-loadable native protocol plugin that load-tests RabbitMQ over **AMQP 0.9.1** using the pure-Rust [`lapin`](https://github.com/amqp-rs/lapin) client. `lapin` pulls **no C / system-lib dependencies**, so the cdylib cross-compiles to all five release targets (linux gnu x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64, windows-msvc); TLS (`amqps://`) is wired to **rustls only** — never OpenSSL/`native-tls`.

Modelled exactly on `loadr-plugin-mongo` / `loadr-plugin-postgres`: synchronous `FfiProtocol::execute(&self, json) -> json` on a single shared instance, owning its own multi-thread tokio runtime and an internal per-URI connection + channel pool reused across all VUs.

## Contract

- **Schemes** (plugin.toml): `["amqp", "amqps", "rabbitmq"]`
- **Request** (`plugin:` block): `{ operation: publish|get, exchange?, routing_key?, queue?, body?, declare_queue?, ack? }`
- **Response**: `{ ok, latency_ms, msgs, error }`
- **Metrics** (derived from the plugin name): `rabbitmq_reqs` / `rabbitmq_req_duration` / `rabbitmq_msgs`
- **URL**: `amqp://user:pass@host:5672/%2f`

## Changes

- `plugins/loadr-plugin-rabbitmq/` — the cdylib (`publish = false`, workspace member)
- `crates/loadr-core` (flow.rs) — surface `extras.msgs` as `<family>_msgs` for plugin protocols (mirrors the existing `docs`/`rows` mappings)
- `examples/harness/docker-compose.yml` — `rabbitmq:3.13-management` service; the `loadr` user, `/` vhost and the `loadr.work` queue are pre-declared from `definitions.json`; readiness via `rabbitmq-diagnostics ping`
- `examples/32-rabbitmq.yaml` — publish + get workload
- `scripts/run-examples.sh` — build+install the plugin, gate on rabbitmq readiness, repoint `amqp://` URLs at the local broker
- `docs/src/plugins/rabbitmq.md` + SUMMARY nav
- `site/videos/20-rabbitmq-plugin.tape` — vhs demo recipe
- `deny.toml` — ignore `RUSTSEC-2024-0384` (unmaintained `instant`, transitive via lapin's built-in async-io reactor; `loadr-plugin-rabbitmq` only, advisory-only, no upgrade path)

## Tests

- Unit tests (scheme/alias/option parsing, response shapes) + a gated integration test (`LOADR_TEST_AMQP_URL`) that does a real publish/get/empty-get round-trip.
- Validated locally against the harness broker: 17/17 plugin tests pass, full `cargo test --workspace --locked` green, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo deny check` all clean.

author: darrencjh8
body:
## Problem (fixes #45)

The expense tracker's LLM called `notify_user` → POST `/api/notify` → Gateway webhook wakes orchestrator agent → agent also calls `notify_user` via plugin → POST `/api/notify` again → **every email produced two Telegram notifications**.

## Fix

Remove `notify_user` from the LLM tool surface. The Gateway orchestrator agent's natural response IS the notification.

### Two-layer design

| Layer | `notify_user` | Who calls it |
|-------|:---:|--------------|
| LLM Tools (TOOLS array, prompts) | ❌ Removed | LLM uses `log_decision` + `mark_email_read` |
| Internal handler (`_handle_notify_user`) | ✅ Preserved | Statement processor error recovery |

### Changes (22 files, +222 / −248)

**Source:**
- `prompts.js` — Removed all `notify_user` from system prompt rules, workflow, few-shot examples, account/payee matching
- `tools.js` — Removed `notify_user` from TOOLS array; kept `_handle_notify_user`, `NotificationCooldown`, config properties for internal use
- `index.js` — Removed `notify_user` from `toolNames`
- `statement/prompts.js` — Replaced "NOTIFICATION RULES" with "RESPONSE GUIDELINES", removed `notify_user` from LLM instructions

**Gateway:**
- Plugin: `budget_notify_user` → no-op returning `"ok"` with zero HTTP calls
- Contract: `budget_notify_user` kept in manifest for compliance
- SKILL.md: Removed `budget_notify_user` from tool table and workflows

**Tests (4 new):**
- `notify_user` absent from `getToolSchemas()` ✅
- `_handle_notify_user` handler exists for internal use ✅
- System prompt does not reference `notify_user` ✅
- `budget_notify_user` no-op returns `"ok"` without HTTP call ✅

**Memory test**: Replaced `vi.mock` with prototype mock (400x faster — 118s → 290ms)

**Specs/docs**: Updated all references, tool counts, diagrams, and data flows across 7 files

### Test Results: 346/346 ✅
- Expense-tracker: 290 tests (14 files)
- Gateway plugin: 56 tests (1 file)

### Preserved (not modified)
- Gateway webhook `/api/notify` — KTMB, portfolio-tracker, full-deploy still depend on it
- Statement processor's internal `notify_user` calls
- Portfolio-tracker's `notify_user`

author: mike-north
body:
Slice of #23. Implements the iOS approver's push-driven inbox lifecycle (#142): an APNs wakeup fetches the pending envelope(s) from the relay, runs them through the core `prepare()`, refreshes the inbox, and reconciles notifications.

## What this adds

- **`PushInboxCoordinator`** (`@MainActor`) — the heart of the slice:
  1. **APNs wakeup** → `handleWakeup(requestId:)`. The push carries a **request id only** — never human-shown context (`docs/contract.md` §Push) — so the id is used purely as a refresh signal; the coordinator never trusts it as request data.
  2. **Fetch** the relay-visible envelopes via the `RelayInboxFetching` seam (`GET /{account}/devices/{device}/inbox`, the HTTP polling counterpart to the presence socket).
  3. **Prepare + refresh** by handing the envelopes to `ApprovalInboxStore.sync`, which runs each through the core `prepare()` (decrypt + WYSIWYS hash + attestation verification in `allw-core`).
  4. **Reconcile notifications** — present a notification for every still-pending request; clear notifications for ids that resolved, expired, or became unverifiable. `didResolve(requestId:)` clears immediately after a local decision.
- **`RelayInboxClient`** — the `RelayInboxFetching` seam, a wire decoder (`RelayInboxDecoder`) mapping the relay's snake_case envelope JSON to `ApprovalEnvelope`, and a `URLSession`-backed `UrlSessionRelayInboxClient`.
- **Push-token registration** — `HexApnsTokenRegistrar` hex-encodes the raw APNs token to the 64-char form the relay accepts and forwards it to the relay's `push_tokens` registration.

## Thin-shell / contract discipline

No crypto reimplemented. The relay body is opaque `context_ciphertext` (zero-knowledge invariant); all decrypt/hash/verify stays in `allw-core` via `prepare()`.

## Fail-closed coverage

- A relay **fetch error** throws `PushInboxError.fetchFailed` and leaves the existing inbox **and** notifications untouched — a network blip never wipes a real pending approval or renders an approved-looking row.
- A **tampered/malformed** relay response (e.g. an envelope missing its ciphertext, or a non-JSON body) fails the whole batch closed in `RelayInboxDecoder`.
- An **unverifiable origin** decrypts to a deny-only `.unverified` row and is never presented as a fresh actionable approval.

## Tests

`PushInboxCoordinatorTests` covers the happy path (fetch → prepare → refresh → present), notification reconciliation (resolved / expired / immediate-clear-on-decide), the fail-closed paths above, and the hex-encoded APNs token. Fixed clocks throughout (no `Date.now`).

## Local vs CI validation

- **Local (this PR, standalone `swiftc`):** the coordinator, decoder, and reconciliation logic against injected fakes; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, and broad `prettier --check` all green.
- **CI macOS `native-bindings` job only:** the real `UNUserNotificationCenter` notification surface, the `URLSession`-backed `UrlSessionRelayInboxClient`, the generated UniFFI binding wiring, and APNs delivery.

## Sibling awareness (#143, Live Activity)

Edits are confined to the APNs/fetch/inbox-refresh path. New files: `PushInboxCoordinator.swift`, `RelayInboxClient.swift`, `PushInboxCoordinatorTests.swift`. Shared file touched: `Tests/AllwIOSApproverTests/ApprovalInboxStoreTests.swift` (one line in the `@main` runner to invoke the new suite) and `README.md` (new section). No Live-Activity files touched. `PushInboxCoordinator.handleWakeup`/`refresh` return the current `[ApprovalListItem]`, which the Live-Activity layer can consume.

Refs #142

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

Two unrelated things ride on this branch.

**1. Narrow two over-firing deny rules** (`.claude/settings.json`, mirrored in `user-config/settings.json`'s sandbox `denyRead`). The curated deny list is a speed bump for accidents (SECURITY.md layer 5), so a rule earns its keep only when it blocks a realistic mistake without taxing everyday work. These two failed that test:

- `Read(**/.env.*)` → enumerated secret-bearing names (`.env.local`, `.env.*.local`, `.env.{development,production,test,staging}`). A blanket `**/.env.*` also blocked the conventionally **non-secret** templates (`.env.example`/`.sample`/`.template`) that an agent reads constantly to learn a project's expected variables. Those are now readable.
- `Bash(*git remote add *)` → **dropped**; `git remote set-url` stays denied. The real boundary on a push to the *wrong* repo is the **credential**, not egress: squid deliberately allows the `git-receive-pack` POST to github.com, but the auto-minted GitHub App token is workspace-repo-scoped, so a cross-repo push 401s at GitHub's own auth (and a non-allowlisted host fails earlier at DNS). So denying `git remote add` only taxed the everyday `git remote add upstream …` without adding protection. `set-url` stays as a cheap defense-in-depth speed bump.

Rationale is reconciled in `.claude/dev-notes` (the doctrine previously *claimed* `**/.env*` was excluded while the config blocked it). `.claude/hooks/deny-rules.test.mjs` round-trip cases are updated to match, including assertions that the freed templates are now allowed. Residual (documented): a secret hidden behind a non-enumerated suffix (`.env.vault`, `.env.dev`) is readable, and under a *broad* credential (`CLAUDE_GH_TOKEN_REPOS`, a PAT in `~/.git-credentials`) `git remote add` becomes a cross-repo exfil path — both accepted because the deny list is a speed bump, not the wall (the sandbox/firewall/credential scope/secret scrubbing are unchanged).

**2. CLI UX polish** (`bin/claude-guard{,-audit,-panic,-remote,-loosen-firewall}`, `scripts/gen-cli-docs.mjs`, `packaging/homebrew/claude-guard.rb`, tests):

- Actionable next-step hints on Docker/permission failure paths.
- Consistent "outgoing-traffic" terminology in `claude-guard-audit` (and `test_audit_reconcile.py` updated to match the renamed output).
- A `-h/--help` usage path for `claude-guard-remote`.
- **Fixed:** `claude-guard panic --help` printed only its one-line description because the `# Options:` block sat below `set -euo pipefail`, where the `usage()` awk stops. Moved the Options into the contiguous header so `--help` lists all flags; the test now asserts each flag appears and that nothing below `set -euo pipefail` leaks.
- A doc-reference line in the usage block (kept in sync between the generated docs and the wrapper).
- A Homebrew formula that also symlinks `claude` → the guard, with updated caveats explaining the override and the `--dangerously-use-original-claude` escape hatch.

## Security boundary impact

The deny-rule change loosens two **layer-5 deny rules**, which SECURITY.md already classes explicitly as a speed bump, *not* a boundary. The hard boundaries (VM/sandbox, default-deny firewall, workspace-scoped credential, secret scrubbing) are unchanged. SECURITY.md needs no edit — it describes the deny list generically and does not enumerate these specific rules, and the "not a boundary" framing still holds.

## How it was tested

- `node --test .claude/hooks/deny-rules.test.mjs` — 406 pass (round-trip cases synced; freed-template behavior asserted).
- `pytest tests/test_audit_reconcile.py tests/test_guard_panic_coverage.py tests/test_claude_panic.py tests/test_homebrew_formula.py tests/test_claude_remote.py tests/test_claude_audit.py` — all pass.
- `claude-guard-panic --help` verified to list every flag.
- `pre-commit` ran on each commit (commit-msg + fragment-name + CLI-docs regen).

## Checklist

- [x] Commits use Conventional Commits
- [x] User-facing change? Added `changelog.d/deny-rule-narrowing.changed.md` and `changelog.d/panic-help-flags.fixed.md`
- [x] Tests added/updated and not skipped or weakened
- [x] README/SECURITY.md touched only if required (not required here)
- [x] `[monitor-eval]` not added (monitor/eval harness unchanged)

## Lessons Learned

- When a deny/allow list has a **round-trip test that asserts its cases exactly cover the live config**, editing the config without updating the test is a silent CI break — the test is the SSOT contract, not optional. Search for such a round-trip before landing any rule change.
- A `--help` that shells out to an **awk/sed scan of the file's leading comment block stops at the first non-comment line** — so any flag documentation placed *after* `set -euo pipefail` (or the first code line) is silently dropped. Keep the whole usage block contiguous above the first executable line, and have the test assert a real flag appears, not just the program name.

body:
## 문제 (회귀)

"롤렉스 순위", "헬스뷰티 순위" 같은 검색이 **"자료에 없음"**으로 실패. (PR #7쯤엔 되던 것)

## 진단 (실측)

두 데이터 PDF가 **영어 내용**이라 한국어 질문이 못 찾음:
- `Jewelry_Watches_2026Q1.pdf`, `Health_Beauty_2026Q1.pdf` → `"rolex"`, `"Health & Beauty top searched keywords"` 등 영어
- 한국어 질문 "헬스뷰티 순위" → **sparse(트라이그램) 매칭 0**, dense는 한국어로 "순위·카테고리"를 떠드는 `1주차강의 ppt`에 밀림 → **top20에도 안 잡힘**
- 실측: 질문에 영어를 섞으면(`"헬스뷰티 순위 Health Beauty ranking"`) 영어 문서가 **즉시 top으로** 올라옴

## 수정

재작성 프롬프트가 **영어 키워드도 추가**하도록 (`헬스뷰티 → Health Beauty`, `롤렉스 → rolex`, `순위 → ranking`):
- sparse 검색어에 영어가 들어가 **영어 데이터 문서를 매칭**
- dense는 원질문(한국어) 유지 → **한국어 문서 검색은 안 깨짐** (embed-rewrite는 소명 검색을 오염시켜서 탈락시킴)
- 재작성은 캐시라 **결정적** 유지
- 캐시 키에 프롬프트 버전 `v2` 접두사 → 프롬프트 바뀌면 옛 캐시 자동 무효화 (배포 순서 무관)

## 검증 (로컬, 3회 반복)

| 질문 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 헬스뷰티 순위 | ✅ 실제 H&B 순위(dyson airwrap...) 답변, 결정적 |
| 롤렉스 순위 | ✅ rolex 1위... 답변, 결정적 |
| 소명하는 방법 | ✅ 그대로 (안 깨짐) |
| 사업자등록증 발급 | ✅ 그대로 |

tsc 0, Vitest 24/24, next build OK.

## 배포 후

- 재배포되면 새 재작성(영어 포함)이 `v2:` 캐시에 쌓이며, 옛 `v1` 캐시는 자동 무시됨 → 수동 캐시 클리어 불필요
- 영어 데이터 PDF가 더 늘면 동일 방식으로 자동 처리됨

author: kerbowa
body:
gfx1250 WMMA instructions can set matrix_a_reuse / matrix_b_reuse bits that keep the A or B source operand in a high-temporality state in the VALU source-operand cache, so a later WMMA reusing the same registers hits in the cache instead of re-reading the register file.

Add a late, post-RA peephole in the existing pre-emit peephole pass that scans each basic block and, for every WMMA, sets the A/B reuse bit when one of the next few WMMAs reuses the same physical registers as its A or B operand and those registers are not redefined in between.

Stale sticky entries in the cache are cleared when a register is used in an instruction without a reuse bit being set. Therefore, the final WMMA use of the same source should not set the bit.

author: mike-north
body:
**Refs #135** (post-v1, P2, area:policy; CEO roadmap Decision 8). Part of epic #136.

Design-first deliverable: a new `docs/decision-flywheel.md` defining the **only sanctioned data egress** from a user's device — recognized-tool tallies. No egress mechanism and no registry engine are built here; this PR is the design.

## What this defines

### Aggregate-only, recognized-only — three composing fail-closed gates
1. **Aggregate-only** — what may leave is a histogram (`{ tool_identity, decision_class, count }`) over a coarse window, **never** per-event records, timestamps, or ordering. `tool_identity` is structure-only function identity (program name, or MCP `(server, tool)`), never args/params/env/paths/raw — consistent with the structure-not-data invariant (contract Invariant 2, #131).
2. **Recognized-only** — a tally entry exists **only for a recognized tool**. Unrecognized-tool counts are excluded **entirely** — not bucketed, not summed into an `\"other\"` total, cardinality not reported. A device that only ran unrecognized tools emits a tally indistinguishable from one that ran nothing. (An `\"other\": N` bucket would leak existence + cardinality — exactly the private signal recognized-only exists to keep on-device.)
3. **Consent** — explicit, fail-closed. **Default = nothing leaves.**

### On-device aggregation
Runs in the audited core (same place that enforces structure-not-data), reads from the ephemeral decision history (#134, sibling — cross-referenced, not redefined here), drops unrecognized identities **before** bucketing, and is idempotent w.r.t. #134's consume-and-destroy.

### Bounded AWAY from the deferred capability tier (hard constraint)
The recognized-tool registry is part of the deferred **semantic / T3** tier (policy-seam.md; AgentRC / Arc Flow). This design depends on it through a single narrow seam — `is_recognized(tool_identity) -> bool`, structure-in / boolean-out — and ships a **`false`-returning stub** in v1. Consequence by construction: every tally is empty and egress is **inert** until T3 lands. **No capability inference, schema DB, or classification pipeline is built.**

### Transport + consent (the carried open question — for sign-off)
Presented as a **recommendation + options**, not baked in. Fail-closed default: nothing leaves.
- **Recommended (A):** explicit opt-in, inspectable, revocable; aggregate channel over the existing zero-knowledge relay (a tally is strictly *less* than the per-request function identity the relay already sees at the default tier, collapsed to frequency). Build only after the T3 registry exists.
- **Options B–D** in the doc: local-only / never-egress (most conservative); dedicated telemetry endpoint; user-exported/user-pushed.

## Files
- `docs/decision-flywheel.md` (new) — the design.
- `README.md` — docs index entry.
- `docs/policy-seam.md`, `docs/threat-model.md` — cross-references (registry → T3 seam; residual-risk row for the sanctioned egress).

## Validation
- `pnpm exec prettier --check \"**/*.{ts,js,mjs,json,md}\"` — passes.
- `git diff --stat` — docs + README only (no code).

## Sign-off ask
The transport + consent decision (Options A–D) is a privacy/CEO call carried open in #136. This PR does **not** unilaterally pick one — it recommends A, defaults to fail-closed (nothing leaves), and surfaces the choice for sign-off.

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

Two docs deliverables, both treating the platform as the current/complete system (no phase or version framing):

**1. Refreshed the capability showcase with measured, reproducible evidence.**
The persona chapters show kseal *doing the job*; they were missing the hard numbers that make the claims defensible. Added a new `docs/showcase/evidence-and-backtesting.md` that captures real, regenerable evidence:
- **Device hot-path latency** (Criterion, `cargo bench -p kseal-core`): `core_new` ≈129 ns, `policy_evaluate` ≈49 ns, `request_proof_generate`/`verify` ≈333/444 ns, `config_verify_and_decode_ed25519` ≈49 µs, `batch_and_compress_10` ≈33 µs — i.e. core init is ~5 orders of magnitude under the <40 ms startup budget, and a per-request proof is a single sub-µs HMAC.
- **Correctness suites that gate each claim**: Go server **23/23 packages pass**, Rust trust core **78 tests pass**, plus the e2e invariant tests (`e2e_trust_flow` replay/sequence/nonce/token/key all DENY; `privacy_contract` schema is non-PII; fleet `BaselineLearnThenSurge`; canary controller rolls back above threshold and not below min-samples).
- **The FitPulse surge back-test** and the **cost model** (≈$585/mo blended data-plane infra at 100M MAU; KMS ≈$0 per token because signing is in-process).

Each of `01`–`05` now has a short **"Back-tested evidence"** section tying that story to the tests/benchmarks behind it, and `competitive-matrix.md` gained an honesty note (kseal column = code that ships + a test that gates it; competitor columns = public positioning, not a bake-off) plus an economics axis.

**2. New build-along series `docs/build-guide/` (10 chapters)** for technical *and* product readers — how you'd rebuild a system like this and *why* each call was made vs the incumbents. Every chapter follows the same shape (the decision → the options → what we built, with real repo files cited → the business read):

| # | Chapter |
|---|---|

body:
## What

Completes the **read side** of ADR-0028. Status *writes* already funnel through the typed `RunStatus` verbs; the read path was still stringly-typed — callers re-derived the state machine by matching raw strings (`"parked"`, `"running"`, `"completed"`…). This types the read return value so the enum is the whole read+write interface, and the terminal/parked groupings live **once** on the type.

## Changes

- **`RunStatus` (lifecycle.rs)** gains `from_str` (inherent `Option`, mirroring `EntityType::from_str`), `is_terminal()`, `is_parked()` — the string↔enum mapping and the groupings now live in exactly one place.
- **`db::run_status` → `Option<RunStatus>`** and **`RunSnapshot.status` → `RunStatus`**, parsed at the DB edge. An unknown stored string surfaces as a loud `sqlx::Error::Decode` (never a silent `None`), mirroring the existing `entity_type_by_id` precedent; the absent-row `None` stays distinct.
- **4 production read-side matchers** migrated to compiler-checked variants / classifiers: `runs/cancel.rs` (`is_terminal()`), `runs/subscribe.rs` ×2 (typed variants; unknown-run now modeled as `Option<RunStatus>` instead of the `String::new()` sentinel), `decide.rs::run_is_parked` (`is_parked()`).
- 7 in-crate **test** assertions adjusted minimally (`.as_deref()` → `.map(db::RunStatus::as_str)`); the `force_run_status`/`run_status_of` test helpers (own raw SQL) untouched.

## Constraints honored

- **ADR-0028:** no FSM/legality layer added — transition legality stays in the SQL guard; this adds only the read return type + classifiers. The rejected `transition(from,event)`/`can_transition()` layer is *not* introduced.
- **ADR-0029:** "type at the seam, close drift by construction." The **wire stays a String** — `SubscribeResult.status` / `RunCancelResult.outcome` unchanged; `.as_str()` is pushed to the send boundary. `packages/protocol` untouched.

## Verification

- `pnpm check` (workspace tsc + cargo check), full `cargo test` (282 unit + all integration), `pnpm -r test` (368 vitest), biome — all green.
- New unit test for the classifiers + a test for the Decode-on-unknown arm (both seams).

body:
🚨 **Severity**: CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability**: The `@flowiseai/nodevm` sandbox configuration object did not explicitly block or sanitize access to native Node globals like `fetch`, `global`, and `globalThis`. Even though other built-ins like `process` and `fs` were explicitly blocked, an attacker could access the remaining globals to break out of the VM environment context or perform unauthorized network requests from the context of the backend server.
🎯 **Impact**: Allowed Remote Code Execution (RCE) via sandbox escapes, or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) allowing malicious scripts to probe internal networks or exfiltrate credentials.
🔧 **Fix**: Updated `createCodeExecutionSandbox` in `packages/components/src/utils.ts` to strictly set `fetch`, `global`, and `globalThis` to `undefined` on the `sandbox` object, explicitly mapping them to `undefined` before they are injected into the VM configuration alongside the secure wrappers.
✅ **Verification**: Code review confirmed the sandbox changes map correctly; no valid sandbox operation requires the raw `global` or native `fetch` components since `node-fetch` and `axios` are mocked with secure wrappers in `executeJavaScriptCode`.

author: adlai88
body:
## Problem

We're a registered Polymarket builder (code `0xed9222…97f8`, profile "Simmer.Markets", 0% maker/taker fee) and **attribution works** — but only on **server-signed (managed-wallet)** flow, which carries the code via the server's `POLY_BUILDER_CODE` env.

**External/self-custody operators sign orders client-side with this SDK and the server only relays the pre-signed order — it can't retrofit the builder code.** The SDK defaulted `builder` to zero bytes32 unless the operator set `POLY_BUILDER_CODE` (which isn't surfaced to them), so that cohort shipped **unattributed**.

Measured 2026-06-16: **~53% of strict real volume ($54.6K of $103K / 30d) is external/local-signed** — i.e. roughly half our volume earns us no builder credit. Polymarket's per-builder time-series confirms our attributed volume tracks the overall volume cliff (peak ~$1.2M/wk Feb → ~$32K/wk now), with the external cohort missing.

## Fix

Default the V2 `builder` field to a new `SIMMER_BUILDER_CODE` constant instead of zero. Precedence is unchanged in order, only the fallback changes:

`explicit builder_code arg > POLY_BUILDER_CODE env > SIMMER_BUILDER_CODE (new)`

- The 3 resolution sites (EOA + DW/OWS V2 paths) repointed; `metadata` still defaults to zero.
- The builder code is a **public** on-chain attribution identifier (serialized in every order, shown on the public leaderboard + builder dashboard) — safe to hardcode in the open-source SDK. Not a secret.
- **No user cost:** Simmer's builder profile is Maker 0% / Taker 0% (confirmed in the builder dashboard).
- **Opt-out preserved:** operators pass `builder_code=ZERO_BYTES32` or set their own `POLY_BUILDER_CODE` to attribute elsewhere / not at all.

## Tests

`tests/test_polymarket_v2.py`: default == `SIMMER_BUILDER_CODE`; explicit arg beats env; env beats Simmer default; explicit zero opts out. Full signing suite green (69 passed).

## Rollout caveat

Orders are signed **client-side**, so this only takes effect as operators **upgrade** the installed SDK — recovery is gradual, not instant. New installs get it immediately. There is no server-side lever for already-installed operators (by custody design the server never signs their orders).

## Verification after merge/publish

Watch Simmer's attributed volume on `data-api.polymarket.com/v1/builders/volume?timePeriod=WEEK` (filter our builderCode) rise toward our real volume as operators upgrade.

author: arsfeld
body:
## What

Fixes inflated playback progress in the Flutter player. During HLS transcode, a few seconds of playback could show as **~30% watched** on episode/home cards, and items would flip to "watched" far too early.

## Root cause

The HLS transcoder serves a **live/growing playlist** (`lib/mydia/streaming/ffmpeg_hls_transcoder.ex:557`: `-hls_list_size 0`, no `-hls_playlist_type`), so `player.state.duration` is the *partial, still-growing* length while transcoding — not the full media duration. The transcoder runs faster than realtime, so the available length races ahead of playback. `ProgressService` synced `position / player.state.duration`, giving `≈ 1/transcode_speed` (a 3× transcode → ~33%). That inflated value was persisted (cards read it) and also tripped `isWatched()` at the 90% threshold.

The player already has a `DurationOverride` carrying the true full duration (used by the seekbar) — `ProgressService` just wasn't using it.

### Evidence

Verified against the live DB: an in-progress episode at ~30 min showed `position=1787s, duration=3452s, 51.8%` — correct once transcoding completes. The bug only bites in the early window before the transcoder finishes, where a short watch persists an inflated value.

## Change

- New `ProgressService.resolveSync()` resolves duration via `DurationOverride.getDuration()` (true full duration) instead of the raw player duration. Both sync paths and `isWatched()` route through it.
- Unit test reproducing the transcode case (12s watched, partial=120s, override=3452s → synced duration is 3452, not 120).

## Tests

`./dev flutter test test/core/player/` → **51 passed** (5 new + 46 existing). Analyzer clean.

## Not included (follow-ups)

- **Resume seek lands too far forward** — separate, unconfirmed. Likely the resume seek clamping to the live edge because the freshly-restarted from-0 transcode hasn't produced the target segments yet (no `-ss` resume-offset support on the backend). Needs live reproduction before fixing.
- **"Start over / Resume" dialog UX** — deferred; a `DurationOverride`-aware resume prompt is a separate phase.

author: perezjuanj
body:
Closes #34. Builds on the merged Wave 1 lanes (A/B/C/E/D) and stays strictly in its lane — touches only step accounting.

## What
The ring's onboard step counter (0x10/0x87 descriptor `[4:6]`, 16-bit big-endian, `DeviceStatus.steps` — §5.4 🟢) is a *since-handoff* delta, not a daily total: the official app sums it in local memory and periodically resets the ring's counter; with the official app not running it keeps climbing (it does NOT reset at midnight on its own). This lane reconstructs a usable per-day total from that counter and fixes the three bugs in #34:

1. **Cross-session delta persistence.** The old in-memory `lastRawSteps` baseline was lost on reconnect/app-restart, so the next reading rebased to the current counter and silently dropped every step taken while disconnected. The last raw value **and its day** are now persisted in `UserDefaults` (`steps.lastRawValue` / `steps.lastRawDay`), read on every frame, so a reconnect computes the TRUE delta `v - persistedRaw` and credits the gap.
2. **Reset vs. climb disambiguation.** A pure, unit-tested `StepAccumulator` decides: `newRaw < previousRaw` ⇒ reset (credit `newRaw`), else monotonic delta. A **mid-day** reset is anomalous (handoff/reboot/16-bit wrap) and logged `.notice`; a reset **across midnight** is the official app's expected daily reset and logged `.debug`. Never silently miscounts.
3. **Midnight display bleed.** The live display total is re-read from the **sample-day** `StoredDaily` row instead of an in-memory carry-over, so an in-session midnight rollover starts fresh with no prior-day bleed.

No SwiftData migration (`StoredDaily` unchanged). Step state lives in `UserDefaults`, not `LocalStore`, to avoid a migration and per-day-row collision.

## Files
- `ios/OpenRingKit/Sources/OpenRingKit/StepAccumulator.swift` — pure reset/midnight fold (new)
- `ios/OpenRingKit/Tests/OpenRingKitTests/StepAccumulatorTests.swift` — 9 cases (new)
- `ios/OpenRingConn/BLE/RingSession.swift` — thin caller: persist raw+day across sessions, sample-time stamping, reset logging
- `ios/OpenRingConn/Store/LocalStore.swift` — `addDailySteps(_:day:)` doc + sample-day stamping

## Tests / checks
- `cd ios/OpenRingKit && swift build && swift test` → **107 pass, 0 failures** (9 `StepAccumulatorTests`: climb, no-movement, no-baseline, mid-day reset+anomaly, midnight reset not-anomalous, midnight incremental climb, 16-bit wraparound, reset-flag-never-on-climb, end-to-end day sum = 2000). RingKitVerify ground-truth step vectors still pass.
- Changed app files parse-check clean (`swiftc -parse`, iphoneos). Device build is the orchestrator's gate.

## Deferred (protocol-blocked, honest)
The ideal fix — read the ring's authoritative daily/lifetime total from the `0x4c` activity payload `[15:22]` — is deferred as gated on captures #13/#9 and is **not** implemented here. No fabricated protocol values: every byte/opcode reference matches the pre-existing, ground-truthed `DeviceStatus.swift`.

## Adversarial review
Peer review verdict: **approve** (no mustFix), acceptance + fabrication checks passed, 107 tests run on the branch. This fixup commit addresses the top shouldConsider item — a comment clarifying that on the live path `sampleDate ≈ now` (sample-time == ingest-time), so a future reader doesn't assume measurement-time back-stamping (impossible without per-step timestamps the ring doesn't expose). Comment-only; no behavior change.

author: chrshnv
body:
## What

The `...core.beans` tests in `sbs/axelix-spring-boot-3-starter` each built their own Spring `TestContext`. This makes the two **non-endpoint** beans tests share a single cached context:

- `DefaultBeanMetaInfoExtractorTest`
- `QualifiersPersistencePostProcessorTest`

They now extend a new abstract `AbstractSharedBeansContextTest`. The base pins `Main` via `@SpringBootTest(classes = Main.class)` and contributes the union of both tests' fixtures via `@Import`, so Spring reuses one `ApplicationContext` for both.

`AxelixBeansEndpointTest` (the endpoint test) is intentionally left on its own context.

## Why `Main` is pinned in `classes`

Leaving the configuration to Spring Boot's auto-detection produced divergent, non-shareable merged configurations across the two subclasses (and, in one attempt, dropped the auto-detected `Main` so the embedded `DataSource` was missing). Pinning `Main` explicitly via the `classes` attribute makes both subclasses resolve an identical, deterministic context — which is what lets them share the cache — while keeping auto-configuration (e.g. the embedded `DataSource`) active. `QualifiersPersistencePostProcessor` is not imported separately; it is already provided by `DefaultBeanAnalyzerTestConfig` as a static `@Bean`.

author: maccman
body:
## What

Adds a **"Convert to bullet"** action to the Tasks page (Plan 18 follow-up). Select one or more tasks and either click the **"Convert to bullet (N)"** toolbar button (next to *Schedule*) or press **⌘⇧K** — each selected task's checkbox is dropped, turning `- [ ] buy milk` into `- buy milk`. The rows leave the Tasks view immediately and the lines remain in their notes as ordinary bullets. Works on checked/archived rows too.

## Why

This is the V2 port of V1's Tasks-page "Convert to checklist" button.

V1 used a `kind: task | checklist` attribute (both render as checkboxes; checklists just don't aggregate into Tasks). V2 has no per-item task/checklist distinction — **every GFM checkbox is a task** — and [Plan 18](docs/plans/18-tasks.md) deliberately rejected per-item opt-out as "invented syntax", mapping checklists to a note-level `checklist: true` flag that was ultimately **dropped** and never built.

Rather than resurrect that flag (which would convert a task's *entire note* — a footgun for daily notes with many tasks), this demotes the selected task(s) to a plain bullet. That is per-item (matching V1's granularity), pure standard markdown (no invented syntax), and naturally removes them from the view because a checkbox is the only thing the projection treats as a task.

## How

Mirrors the existing toggle/edit/delete chain end-to-end:

- **Core** — `taskLineToBullet(source, task)` in `markdown/edit.ts`: strips the 3-char marker + following horizontal whitespace, keeping the bullet/indent/content; guarded by `locateTaskMarker`/`TaskStaleError` like its siblings. Exported through both `@reflect/core` barrels.
- **Session** — `commitTaskToBullet` on `NoteSession` (thin `commitBodyEdit` wrapper) so an open note edits its live buffer.
- **Bridge** — `convertTaskToBullet` in `lib/note-task.ts` (session-or-disk via `applyTaskChange`, serialized per path, `raw`-guarded).
- **Action** — `convertMutation` + `convertToBullet` in `use-task-actions.ts`: optimistic `withoutTasks` on both lists, mirroring `deleteMutation`'s struck-row/`recently-completed` handling.
- **UI** — "Convert to bullet (N)" toolbar button (`List` icon) shown when a selection exists; **⌘⇧K** screen-level chord in `use-task-keyboard.ts` (V1's `Mod+Shift+K`), fires only with a selection.

No schema/migration/Rust changes.

## Reviewer notes

- Adding `commitTaskToBullet` to the `NoteSession` interface required updating the 4 fake-session test objects (document-binding/move-note/open-documents/rename-coordinator).
- Tests added at every layer: core primitive (`edit.test.ts`), bridge (`note-task.test.ts`), session (`note-session.test.ts`), keyboard (`use-task-keyboard.test.ts`), and a screen integration test for both the button and ⌘⇧K (`tasks-screen.test.tsx`).
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` 0 errors (the 4 warnings are pre-existing React-Compiler notices in untouched files); all targeted tests pass.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches note markdown writes and the live session buffer (same paths as task edit/delete); behavior is guarded by `TaskStaleError` and mirrors proven task mutations, but multi-note batch converts can still affect user data.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **Convert to bullet** on the Tasks page so selected checkbox lines lose their `[ ]`/`[x]` marker and stay in the note as plain list items, which removes them from the Tasks projection.
> 
> The change is wired like existing task writes: core `taskLineToBullet`, `commitTaskToBullet` on open notes, `convertTaskToBullet` on disk/session, and optimistic cache updates in `use-task-actions`. The toolbar shows **Convert to bullet (N)** when rows are selected; **⌘⇧K** works at the screen level and inside the inline editor.

author: acoshift
body:
Follow-up to #9 (the cache-egress PromQL fix). #9 stops the bleeding going forward; this adds the tool to recover the days already lost.

## Why the data loss is wider than "cache_egress was missing"

`syncProjectUsageDate` accumulates all resources into one request and submits it **once at the end** (`SetProjectUsage`). But it `return`s on the first Prometheus error, and the cache-egress query runs *before* that submit. So while cache-egress was failing, for every project with **≥1 routed domain** the **entire** daily `project_usages` row was dropped — `cpu_usage`, `cpu`, `memory`, `egress`, `waf_egress`, `cache_egress`, `disk`, `replica`. Projects with no domains took the no-error `"0"` branch and were unaffected.

Normal runs only ever recompute today (and yesterday before 5am), so the outage days never self-heal.

## What this adds

A one-shot **backfill mode**. Set `BACKFILL_FROM` / `BACKFILL_TO` (UTC `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive) and the binary re-runs project-usage collection for that window, then exits — no periodic loops.

Idempotent: `SetProjectUsage` upserts on `(project, location, date, name)`, so re-running rewrites identical values for unaffected projects/days and never double-counts. Safe to re-run.

## Billing-correctness fix for historical days

`rangeSeconds` — the multiplier applied to averaged cpu/disk/replica gauges — was `max(now, et) - t`. For an already-finished day, `now` is far past the day end `et`, so this inflates to **multiple days** and would over-bill on backfill. Extracted into `billingRangeSeconds` (live behavior byte-for-byte unchanged) and `Backfill` passes `now = et`, pinning each completed day to exactly one day (86400s). Unit-tested (`TestBillingRangeSeconds`), including the over-count case that motivates `now = et`.

## Operator runbook

1. Deploy an image containing **both** #9 (the fix) and this commit. (#9 alone stops new loss; backfill needs the fix or it re-errors and aborts.)
2. Run a one-shot job **per location** with the live env plus:
   ```
   BACKFILL_FROM=2026-06-12   # cache_egress shipped in #6 on 2026-06-12 (outage start)
   BACKFILL_TO=2026-06-15     # through yesterday; today is covered by live runs
   ```
3. Spot-check a couple of domain-having projects' `project_usages` rows against Prometheus for those dates.

**Bounds & caveats**
- Recoverability is limited by Prometheus retention (~10 days). 2026-06-12 is inside the window; don't expect to recover anything older than retention.
- `p.Domains` is current route state, so backfilled `cache_egress` attribution uses today's domain→project mapping (a domain that moved/was deleted since is approximate). All other resources are exact. Same caveat already documented for the feature.
- Only `project_usages` is backfilled. Deployment-level usage was on a separate, unaffected path and uses non-idempotent inserts, so it's intentionally excluded.

## Tests
`TestBillingRangeSeconds` + existing suite green; `go vet` clean.

author: jphein
body:
Closes #30.

Restores the dynamic Open Graph / Twitter social-card route that was stubbed to a static fallback when `@vercel/og` + wasm (~2.2 MiB) exceeded the Workers **FREE** 3 MiB bundle cap. Now on Workers **PAID** (10 MiB).

**Bundle size after: ~2.85 MiB / 10 MiB gzipped** (`Total Upload 11484 KiB / gzip 2923 KiB`) — 28% of budget.

## What it does
Per-page branded social cards rendered with `next/og` (satori + resvg-wasm), in the TechEmpower earth-tone design system: cream gradient background, teal→amber→coral accent rail, a "rising bars" logo mark, the **TechEMPOWER.org** wordmark, the page title in **Fraunces**, and a **DM Sans** eyebrow + domain pill. Spanish diacritics render correctly (the font subset covers Latin-1 + Latin-Ext-A).

The card is rendered **purely from a `?title=` query param** — no Notion fetch on the request path — so it deliberately avoids re-introducing the heavy recordMap render behind the earlier CPU 503s (#…). `PageHead`/`feed` pass the page title through `lib/get-social-image-url.ts`.

## Two notable implementation decisions (please review)
1. **App Router route handler, not `pages/api`.** `@opennextjs/cloudflare` only makes `@vercel/og` work on workerd by swapping its Node build for the Edge/wasm build at build time, and that AST patch only matches the dynamic `index.node.js` import an **App Router** handler emits. A `pages/api` route statically inlines `@vercel/og`'s Node build, which then crashes on Workers doing `readFileSync('/Geist-Regular.ttf')`. This adds a single `app/` route handler alongside the existing Pages Router (hybrid is supported).
2. **`build` → `next build --webpack`.** Same root cause: under Turbopack (Next 16.2's default) the OpenNext og patch is skipped and the Node `@vercel/og` build is inlined → runtime crash. Webpack is OpenNext's supported path. `next dev` still uses Turbopack. (Master #54 already removed the `lqip-modern`→`sharp` dead path, so the webpack build is clean.)

## Brand fonts
`lib/fonts/{fraunces-600,dmsans-700,dmsans-500}.ts` are instanced + subset static slices of the Google Fonts variable TTFs (~45 KB each), decoded via `atob` → ArrayBuffer (edge + node safe).

## Validation
- `pnpm test` (eslint + prettier) ✓
- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓
- `pnpm cf:build` ✓ — `ƒ /api/social-image`, worker saved
- Rendered locally via `pnpm cf:preview` + curl: HTTP 200 `image/png` 1200×630 for page-title, site-level (homepage), and Spanish-accented titles.

body:
## Scope
The public/visitor profile now renders FROM the owner's saved `profile_widgets` — its widget set, position order, and per-kind content (platform / template / composed) — instead of rendering every platform card directly. A widget the owner hid (`is_enabled = false`) is omitted for visitors. This is the visibility payoff for personalization phase 2: what the owner arranges is finally what a visitor sees. Decision: **only-widgets** (a public profile with no widget rows shows the neutral empty state — the same the owner sees on their own screen; there is no auto-provisioning, so no "all cards minus disabled" fallback).

## Type
feat

## Changeset
1. Public read of `profile_widgets`: `fetchPublicWidgets(userId)` on the data source + repository (no auth gate; same soft DTO mapping/error handling as the owner read) and a `publicProfileWidgets(userId)` provider folding it. The contract is the already-documented public-readable surface in `docs/integration/personalization.md`.
2. `PublicProfileWidgetsView` (new, `profile/presentation`): reads the public widgets, filters to enabled, sorts by `position`, and renders each widget through the SAME owner card views — read-only (no options menu, no add/reorder).
3. Card-source seam: an optional `CardSource` on `TemplateCardView` / `ComposedCardView` (default → `ownerCardProvider`, so owner behavior + tests are unchanged); the visitor injects `publicOwnerCard(userId, …)`. New `publicOwnerCard(userId, platform)` provider folds the existing `CardsRepository.fetchPublicCard`.
4. Cross-feature seam: the router injects a `PublicWidgetsBuilder` into `PublicProfileScreen`, which delegates its body to it; `PublicProfileScreen.cardBuilder` (now dead) is removed. `feed` imports no `profile/presentation` / `profile/data` — only `profile/domain`.
5. Dead-code sweep: removed the now-unused `publicCard` provider from `feed`.

author: wangjohn
body:
## Summary

[#1427](https://github.com/assembledhq/143/pull/1427) ("Session Transcript Refactor") replaced the session thread UI with a brand-new 977-line `ThreadTranscriptWindow` (custom message/tool bubbles, `react-virtual`, a search box). This **reverts that UI** while **keeping the faster/cleaner backend**: the original `ChatTimeline` (and its existing tool-call / user / assistant components) renders again, but it's now sourced from the single `/transcript` window endpoint instead of the old two-query `/messages` + `/logs` coupling.

The seam that makes this clean: `/transcript` entries embed the full `message`/`log`/`human_input` records, so a small adapter flattens them into the `{messages, logs}` shape `buildTimeline()` already consumes.

## Why
The new rendering changed a large part of the chat UI. We want the original components back, without giving up the single-query, indexed transcript backend that was the point of the refactor.

## Changes

**Frontend**
- `lib/timeline.ts`: add `flattenTranscriptWindows()` — unwraps `/transcript` turns into `{messages, logs, humanInputs}` (id-deduped), reusing the existing `buildTimeline()`.
- `ChatPanel` (`session-detail-content.tsx`): one `/transcript` infinite query feeds `ChatTimeline`; replaces `threadMessagesQuery` + `threadLogsQuery`. Rewired all five cache-coupled sites: query, scroll-to-latest, load-newer, warm-start prefetch, and optimistic send (now reconciles via transcript cache-patch + invalidation, no flicker).
- Removed `ThreadTranscriptWindow` (+ test), the transcript **search** UI, the `@tanstack/react-virtual` dependency, and dead message-window helpers/types/api methods (`getThreadMessageWindow`/`getThreadLogs`, `ThreadMessageWindow*` types).
- **Jump to latest**: kept right-aligned (as in the old UI; the new one centered it) and added a bounded `requestAnimationFrame` settle-loop so it reaches the true bottom even as lazy markdown/code/images expand after the first scroll.
- Fix: `revertThread` now invalidates `threadTranscript` (previously the removed `threadMessages` query), so the revert patch actually refreshes.

**Backend**
- Removed the now-unused `/transcript/search` endpoint (handler, service, store method, models, tests). **Kept** the `/transcript` window endpoint, store, and migration `000190`.

**Tests**
- Migrated the session-detail page tests from `/messages`+`/logs` mocks to `/transcript` (shared `makeTranscriptWindow` helper); collapsed the obsolete parallel-logs tests into a single-fetch render test; added `flattenTranscriptWindows` unit tests.

## Reviewer notes
- Optimistic message send no longer patches a flat message window; it patches the newest transcript page then invalidates. Behavior is covered by the migrated `page-agent-tabs`/`page-transcript` tests.
- jsdom can't assert true-bottom scroll pixels, so the Jump-to-latest settle behavior is best confirmed once manually in the running app.
- Backend `/messages` and `/logs` endpoints are intentionally left in place (public API surface); only their dead frontend wrappers were removed.

## Verification
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` ✅, `eslint . --max-warnings=0` ✅, full suite green (one unrelated `settings/evals/new` contention-timeout that passes in isolation).
- Backend: `go build ./...` ✅, `go vet` ✅, `handlers`/`services/thread`/`db`/`models` tests ✅.

body:
## Why
The embedded RADIUS server (#276) is opt-in, and the app container only exposes HTTP behind Nginx — so RADIUS UDP never reached it. This wires deployment so a normal deploy-on-merge brings it up (you asked for exactly this).

## Changes
- **`docker-compose.prod.yml`**: publish **UDP 1812/1813** on the `app` service and pass `RADIUS_SERVER_ENABLED` (**default `true` in prod**, overridable with `RADIUS_SERVER_ENABLED=false` in `.env.prod`) + `RADIUS_AUTH_PORT` / `RADIUS_ACCT_PORT` / `RADIUS_SERVER_SECRET`. Nginx proxies HTTP only, so RADIUS UDP is published directly. ⚠️ Fixed host ports → keep `app` at `replicas:1` (or front RADIUS with a UDP LB) if you scale the app tier.
- **`docker-compose.yml`** (dev): publish the UDP ports + env, **default `false`**.
- **`Dockerfile`**: `EXPOSE 1812/udp 1813/udp` (documentation).
- **`.env.prod.example` / `.env.example`**: document `RADIUS_SERVER_*` (prod=true, dev=false).
- **`charts/fireisp/values.yaml`**: add the `RADIUS_SERVER_*` toggle (default false). Exposing it on Kubernetes also needs UDP ports added to the Service — left as a documented follow-up (the chart Service is HTTP/TCP only today; `helm` isn't available here to lint template changes).

## After merge + deploy
`GET /api/v1/radius/server-status` will report `running:true` on the demo, and the listener will be reachable on UDP 1812/1813 (you've already opened the firewall for the RouterOS + my test IP). I'll then run the live RADIUS auth/accounting test against the demo.

## Verification
- All compose + `values.yaml` validated with js-yaml; `secretsAudit` + `setupSecrets` tests green.
- **No application code changed** — deploy/config only.

author: copilot
body:
The in-revision Redis sidecar acts as the Celery **broker** (db0), result backend (db1), and ops/durable cache (db2), but was started with `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`. For a broker this is an anti-pattern: under memory pressure Redis evicts arbitrary keys — including broker queue lists, unacked-task hashes, and durable OpenAPI runtime config — so enqueued BLAST/ACR/AKS jobs are accepted by the API, silently dropped, and never reach a terminal state. This is the observed "queuing doesn't work" symptom.

### Changes

- **`infra/modules/containerAppControl.bicep`** — Redis `--maxmemory-policy` switched from `allkeys-lru` to `noeviction`. The `--maxmemory 384mb` cap is intentionally kept: with `noeviction` a memory-pressure write fails loudly (and surfaces on the sidecar metrics card) instead of dropping queued work or growing until OOM. Memory stays bounded in practice — the result backend honours `CELERY_RESULT_EXPIRES` and the ops caches set per-key TTLs.

```diff
   '--maxmemory', '384mb'
-  '--maxmemory-policy', 'allkeys-lru'
+  '--maxmemory-policy', 'noeviction'
```

- **`api/tests/test_redis_broker_eviction_policy.py`** — new regression guard: fails if the Redis sidecar ever uses an `allkeys-*` / `volatile-*` policy, or drops the `--maxmemory` cap.

- **`docs/features_change/2026-06/2026-06-16-redis-broker-noeviction.md`** — change note covering root cause and rationale.

### Notes / out of scope

Worker resourcing (worker sidecar runs prefork pools totalling ~8 processes on 1 vCPU) is a tuning trade-off rather than a defect and is left untouched here; the decisive cause of dropped jobs was the broker eviction policy. Happy to follow up on concurrency/CPU tuning separately if desired.

author: vaibhavatlan
body:
## Problem

A required status check only clears a merge when it reports a **conclusion**. A job skipped via a job-level `if:` reports `skipped` — which a required check does **not** count as success — so it stays pending and **blocks the PR and the merge queue**.

Two required checks (`Integration Tests`, `Trivy Code Scan`) used `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'` at the **job** level, and `Conventional Commits` was skipped on fork PRs. Separately, the `code` paths-filter included `.github/**`, so any workflow-only edit triggered the full unit + integration matrix.

## Changes (single file: `.github/workflows/pull_request.yaml`)

**1. Replace the one `code` filter bucket with two scoped buckets in the `changes` job:**

| Bucket | Globs | Drives |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk` | `application_sdk/**`, `tests/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.github/actions/{unit-tests,setup-deps}/**`, `!**/*.md` | unit, integration, docstr, e2e |
| `scan` | `application_sdk/**`, `contract-toolkit/**`, `tests/**`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Trivy code scan |

`sdk` drops `.github/**` (workflow-meta) and `.security/**`, and never included `contract-toolkit/` or `docs/` — so workflow-only / toolkit-only / docs-only PRs no longer run the test matrix. It keeps the two `.github/actions/*` test-harness dirs so changing *how* tests run still re-runs them. The trailing `!**/*.md` (last-match-wins in `dorny/paths-filter`) excludes markdown anywhere, so a markdown-only edit *inside* a code dir (e.g. `application_sdk/README.md`) no longer triggers the suite — while `scan` deliberately keeps a wide net so Trivy still catches secrets committed in markdown.

**2. Make `Integration Tests` and `Trivy Code Scan` always-run + short-circuit:** drop the job-level `if:`; the job always starts, a first step no-ops when the bucket is unchanged, and every real step is gated on `sdk`/`scan`. Job names are unchanged → **no branch-ruleset edit needed.**

**3. Make `Conventional Commits` always conclude:** drop the job-level `if:`; the validation step runs only on non-fork PRs (the action needs `ORG_PAT_GITHUB`), and a no-op step reports success on fork PRs / `merge_group`. PR-title content is still enforced by `Validate PR title`.

**4. Mechanical:** `unit` and `docstr` now gate on `sdk`; the e2e jobs (`build-sdk-base-image`, `connector-tests`) gate on `sdk == 'true' || container == 'true'`.

## Effect

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| docs-only / workflow-only / toolkit-only PR | required checks skipped → can block; matrix ran on `.github` edits | `Integration Tests` + `Trivy Code Scan` go ✅ in seconds; matrix correctly skipped |
| markdown-only edit inside a code dir (e.g. `application_sdk/README.md`) | ran the full unit + integration matrix | matrix skipped (Trivy still scans, for secrets) |
| fork PR | `Conventional Commits` skipped → blocked | ✅ concludes |
| real SDK PR | full tests run | full tests run (unchanged) |
| merge queue | a skipped required check hangs pending | every required check always concludes |

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean (only pre-existing shellcheck warnings); `pre-commit` passes.
- This PR touches only `.github/`, so its own run should show `Integration Tests` + `Trivy Code Scan` green in seconds and the unit matrix skipped while `Unit Tests Gate` stays green.
- Negation-pattern (`!**/*.md`) behaviour is worth eyeballing once with a markdown-only test PR.
- To confirm in the queue: `dorny/paths-filter` on `merge_group` diffs the queued ref against the default branch (same setup conformance already uses).

满分化 **T2 廉价收割**：把安全纵深两项 ★4→★5。两项均**模型无关 + 确定性**（无模型 key，CI 可单测），承接 Stream PI 分层防御。设计 `docs/research/2026-06-16-7.3-7.4-input-dlp-harvest-design.md`。

现 spotlight 只裹**已知不可信通道**（tool/RAG/memory），治不了 red-team 实测的**内联注入**（指令藏在 user 消息里）——`RunRequest.input` 单串无指令/数据边界。

- `RunRequest.untrusted_content: list[str]`（≤16 段/每段 ≤8192，向后兼容）：业务系统结构化传待处理数据（工单/邮件/文档）

body:
## Summary

Replaces the default development-only secret-store runtime path with an OS-backed credential-store path for normal development and production-style local startup.

## Changes

- Adds `@napi-rs/keyring@1.3.0` for Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, and Linux Secret Service/libsecret support behind the existing `OsCredentialAdapter` boundary.
- Adds a runtime secret-store factory with health detection, degraded diagnostics, and a fail-closed unavailable-store implementation.
- Wires Twitch OAuth and EventSub token access through the runtime secret-store selection.
- Keeps fake/in-memory stores available only through explicit test injection seams.
- Adds restart-style smoke coverage, unavailable credential-store coverage, redaction checks, and dev/prod parity coverage.
- Updates OpenSpec artifacts, the MVP runbook, and the MVP final-review note for the resolved secret-store gap.
- Commits the `.codegraph/` directory marker while leaving the machine-local CodeGraph database ignored.

## Why

Twitch access and refresh tokens are real secrets. The previous runtime wiring used `DevSecretStore({ mode: "development" })`, so connected tokens were lost across restart and the local runtime had no durable credential-store decision. This change gives normal development and production-style local startup the same secure behavior.

## User Impact

Stream Jams now stores real Twitch token material in the OS credential store when available. If credential storage is unavailable, the local app still starts, diagnostics report a non-secret `runtime-secret-store` provider error, and Twitch OAuth/token operations fail closed without falling back to plaintext storage.

author: lalonchera22
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses multiple security vulnerabilities and concurrency issues across authentication, API rate limiting, subscription contracts, and payment processing. Key improvements include fixing RLS policies to properly separate read/write access, implementing atomic rate limiting to prevent race conditions, securing the subscription contract against arbitrary pricing, and hardening JWT verification.

## Key Changes

### Database & Authentication (supabase/schema.sql)
- **Fixed RLS policies for users table**: Replaced conflicting SELECT policies with explicit public read access and separated write operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) with proper ownership checks using `WITH CHECK` clause
- **Implemented atomic rate limiting**: Added `check_and_log_api_usage()` function using PostgreSQL advisory locks to serialize concurrent requests per API key, eliminating the race condition where multiple requests could read the same counter and bypass the limit
- **Automated nonce cleanup**: Wrapped `cleanup_expired_nonces()` scheduling in an idempotent `DO` block to prevent auth_nonces table from growing indefinitely

### Smart Contracts (contracts/ContenlineSubscription.sol)
- **Added Plan registry**: Creators now register plans onchain with fixed price and duration; subscribers cannot specify arbitrary amounts
- **New `setPlan()` function**: Allows creators to define/update their subscription plans with price, duration, and active status
- **Modified `subscribe()` signature**: Removed `durationDays` and `amount` parameters; now reads these from the registered plan, preventing attackers from subscribing with amount=1
- **Added PlanSet event**: Emits when a creator registers or updates a plan

### API Rate Limiting (lib/validateApiKey.ts)
- **Switched to atomic RPC call**: Now uses the new `check_and_log_api_usage()` function instead of separate SELECT + INSERT operations
- **Added graceful fallback**: If the function doesn't exist (during deployment), falls back to non-atomic checking but still enforces the limit
- **Removed redundant logging**: Logging is now handled atomically within the SQL function

### Edge Function Optimization (supabase/functions/sync-subscriptions/index.ts)
- **Implemented pagination**: Processes subscriptions in batches of 100 to avoid memory/CPU limits in Edge Functions
- **Added time-based filtering**: Prioritizes subscriptions expiring within the next 2 hours for revalidation
- **Improved type safety**: Added explicit `Sub` type definition

### Checkout API Security (app/api/v1/checkout/route.ts)
- **Added category whitelist**: Only allows 'onchain', 'course', 'service' categories; prevents developers from forcing different fee structures
- **Added null check**: Validates that API key has an associated user before creating payment session, preventing RLS violations

### Contract Whitelist Validation (lib/contracts.ts)
- **Explicit error handling**: Throws a clear 500 error if contract whitelist is empty (misconfiguration) instead of silently rejecting with 400
- **Improved error message**: Guides developers to configure required environment variables

### JWT Verification Hardening (lib/jwt.ts)
- **Fixed timing attack vulnerability**: Added length check before `timingSafeEqual()` to prevent TypeError from leaking information about signature validity
- **Proper error handling**: Returns null for invalid signatures of any length, treating them uniformly as authentication failures

### Configuration & Documentation (next.config.js)
- **Added CSP security notes**: Documented why 'unsafe-eval' is required (WalletConnect/RainbowKit) and marked TODO for future nonce-based CSP migration to eliminate 'unsafe-inline'

### Tests (test/contracts.test.ts)
- **Updated subscription test**: Now calls `setPlan()` before `subscribe()` to match new contract flow
- **Added plan validation test**: Verifies that subscriptions to non-existent or inactive plans are rejected

## Notable Implementation Details
- The advisory lock in `check_and_log_api_usage()` uses `hashtext()` to convert UUID to a stable integer for locking, ensuring all concurrent requests for the same key are serialized
- The subscription sync function uses `lt('expires_at', horizon)` to prioritize expiring subscriptions, reducing unnecessary blockchain calls
- JWT verification now safely handles malformed signatures without information leak

author: whiterabbit404x
body:
## Summary
Wrap detection, alert, and detection-alert linking operations in per-event savepoints to gracefully handle recoverable SQL errors (FK violations, constraint errors, etc.) without dead-lettering the monitoring target. When these errors occur, the affected operation is skipped and processing continues, allowing the target to remain healthy and retry on the next cycle.

## Key Changes

### monitoring_runner.py
- Wrapped `_create_detection()` call in `connection.transaction()` savepoint; catches and logs FK/constraint errors, sets `detection_id = None`, and continues
- Wrapped `_upsert_alert()` call in savepoint; catches and logs errors, sets `alert_id = None`, and continues  
- Wrapped detection-alert linking UPDATE in savepoint; catches and logs errors without failing the entire event
- Added warning-level logging for each recoverable error with target_id, monitoring_run_id, and truncated error message for debugging

### repair_target_cursor.py
- Added new `--clear-dead-letter` flag to `--mode reset` to atomically clear dead-letter state, lease fields, and delivery_attempts when resetting cursor
- Added standalone `--mode clear-dead-letter` command for clearing dead-letter state without cursor changes
- Updated `cmd_reset()` to support `block=0` (null cursor for fresh backfill) and optional dead-letter clearing
- Updated `monitor_checkpoint` handling: delete row when `block=0`, update when `block > 0`
- Enhanced docstring with usage examples for dead-letter recovery workflows

### migrations/0112_reset_e785_cursor_for_live_tail.sql
- New migration to recover a specific Base target (e7851a52) that was stuck in dead-letter state with stale cursor
- Clears dead-letter state, lease fields, and nulls cursor/checkpoint to force fresh live-tail scan
- Workspace-scoped and idempotent

### test_base_monitoring_cursor_and_alert_bugs.py
- Added comprehensive test `test_detection_insert_failure_does_not_dead_letter()` verifying:
  - Detection INSERT FK error is caught by savepoint and doesn't raise
  - Alert INSERT error is caught and doesn't raise
  - Target UPDATE (lease clear) still executes after recoverable failures
  - Savepoint context manager is properly invoked
  - Process completes normally without dead-lettering the target

### conftest.py
- Added mock exception types to `_Status.psycopg.errors` for test compatibility (DeadlockDetected, ForeignKeyViolation, IntegrityError, UndefinedTable, UndefinedColumn)

### test_base_polling_chain_selection.py
- Updated `_process()` mock function signatures to accept `**kwargs` for forward compatibility with new monitoring_runner parameters

## Implementation Details

**Savepoint Strategy:**
Each detection/alert operation is wrapped in its own `connection.transaction()` savepoint. If an exception occurs, the savepoint rolls back that operation only, leaving the connection healthy for subsequent operations (e.g., target lease clear, checkpoint update).

**Error Handling:**
Errors are logged at WARNING level with truncated error messages (300 chars for detection/alert, 200 chars for linking) to aid debugging without exposing sensitive data. The target is NOT dead-lettered; it remains eligible for the next monitoring cycle.

**Cursor Repair:**
The new `--clear-dead-letter` flag enables operators to recover stuck targets by atomically clearing dead-letter state and optionally resetting the cursor in a single command, reducing manual intervention steps.

**Workspace Scope:**
All changes respect workspace-scoped data isolation. The migration is workspace-scoped and idempotent.

author: mperkins0155
body:
## What

Fixes three Windows-only bugs that prevented the `tinyagi` CLI from running on native Windows (non-WSL).

### 1. Doubled drive letter → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`
`new URL('.', import.meta.url).pathname` returns `/C:/Users/...` on Windows. Passing that to `path.resolve` makes Node treat the leading `/` as the current drive root and prepend it, producing `C:\C:\Users\...`:

```
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\C:\Users\...\packages\cli\dist\version.js'
```

Fixed by using `fileURLToPath()` (correct on all platforms) in:
- `packages/cli/bin/tinyagi.mjs` (`REPO_ROOT`)
- `packages/cli/lib/defaults.mjs` (`SCRIPT_DIR`)

### 2. False "Missing prerequisites: node, npm"
`commandExists()` ran the POSIX shell builtin `command -v` via `cmd.exe`, which has no such command, so every check failed even with Node/npm installed. Now uses `where` on `win32`, `command -v` elsewhere (`packages/cli/src/install.ts`).

## Testing

Verified on Windows 11, Node v25:
- `npm run build` — clean
- `tinyagi version` / `install` (detects existing build) / `agent list` / `provider list` / `status`
- daemon `start`/`stop` — API server on `localhost:3777`, SQLite queue + heartbeat, clean shutdown

No behavior change on macOS/Linux (`fileURLToPath` and the `command -v` branch are unchanged there).

author: jfolcini
body:
From the backlog. Closes #704.

## Bug
A single `is_foreground` flag was flipped on every `WindowEvent::Focused(false)`, but it gates two opposing regimes: maintenance jobs (`wal_checkpoint_truncate`, `op_log_compact`, `tombstone_purge`, `loro_snapshot_if_dirty`) run when `!foreground`, while the sync daemon's periodic resync + materializer metrics pause when `backgrounded`. So plain focus-loss (clicking another window while the app stays on-screen) fired backgrounded-only maintenance mid-edit and starved periodic sync.

## Fix
`derive_app_state(WindowStateFlags) -> AppState`: `Background` iff `os_suspended || !visible || minimized`; `focused` is deliberately unused — focus-loss alone never backgrounds. Desktop `Focused(false)` now queries live `is_visible()`/`is_minimized()` to detect a real minimize/hide; mobile `Suspended`/`Resumed` map directly (`#[cfg(mobile)]`). `apply_state` routes the enum to the existing mark methods, so the decision lives in one tested place.

## Verification
9 unit tests incl. the core case (focus-lost-but-visible → Foreground). Reviewer ran the full Rust suite (**4186 passed**) + clippy clean; verdict SOUND. The benign Linux/GTK signal-ordering nuance is documented (self-correcting, conservative; mobile uses the authoritative `Suspended` event).

author: usirin
body:
Fixes #382

Records **ADR 0071** — the decision on how to make the control-plane boundary (ADR 0053/0065) binding at the GitHub level, since today it is honor-system: `main`'s ruleset requires **0 approvals + 0 checks**, so nothing at the platform blocks a hand-merge of a control-plane PR or a no-PASS merge. Only `ship-it`'s self-restraint upholds it.

## The decision

Two complementary GitHub mechanisms, each closing the half of the gap it actually fits:

1. **Required status checks back the gate suite.** A `required_status_checks` rule on `main` for the ADR-0061 gating set (`lint / format / typecheck`, `unit tests`, `validate skill frontmatter`, `integration tests`, `produce run-evidence bundle`, `scan changed files for leaks`); `deploy (web)` excluded as informational. A no-green-CI `gh pr merge` becomes platform-blocked. Required *checks* (not *reviews*) for the general lane preserves the solo-operator autonomous lane (an operator cannot self-approve — ADR 0048/0055).
2. **A human-only CODEOWNERS holds the control plane.** `require_code_owner_review` + a checked-in `CODEOWNERS` over `.claude/**`/`.github/**` and the gate-critical skills, owned by a **human-only** identity. This resolves the **ADR-0055 wrinkle**: ACL `write+` (agent-inclusive) decides whose *verdict marker* counts; CODEOWNERS (human-only) decides whose *approval* unblocks a *control-plane* merge — two different authz questions, deliberately disjoint, so an agent approval cannot satisfy the human-merge gate.

Ruleset-as-code over click-ops (ADR 0062). Status quo (honor-system + discipline) and required-approvals-on-all-PRs are considered and rejected in the ADR.

## Scope

- `.decisions/0071-enforce-control-plane-at-github.md` (new), `index.md` row.
- Cross-linked from ADR 0053 and ADR 0065 (acceptance criteria).
- This ADR **records and recommends**; it does **not** change any repo setting. Enacting the ruleset + CODEOWNERS is an outward-facing human governance action, filed as follow-up **#402** (`status:needs-triage`, milestone "Pipeline hardening").

This PR is **non-control-plane** (touches only `.decisions/**`) → auto-ships on a `review-doc` PASS.

author: dhokanson-armoryworks
body:
## What

Phase 2 of the schema-ownership move (`docs/DESIGN.md`): build `forge-db` as a declarative
Postgres DB-project. Seeds the desired-state `schema/` tree from the merged squash baseline
(forge-api `a8260a75`, deployed) and adds the C# `Forge.Db` harness that reconciles a live
Postgres to it via **Atlas**.

## Contents

- **`schema/`** — 293 tables, 865 indexes, 2 functions, 2 triggers, 1 extension, **one object
  per file** (dacpac-style). Split from a canonical `pg_dump --schema-only` of a throwaway DB
  built by running the squashed migrations. Lossless: per-statement counts match the dump exactly.
- **`src/Forge.Db/`** — harness with verbs `baseline` (the splitter) / `plan` / `verify` /
  `apply`. Deploy gates: block-destructive-by-default (`--allow-destructive`), non-dev requires
  `--yes` + `--backup-taken`; every `apply` captures the plan to `history/` (audit-only).
- **`atlas.hcl`**, per-dir READMEs (INPUT vs OUTPUT), `tests/` (7 unit tests).

## The §9 safeguard (why `verify` is two checks)

The Atlas free tier **refuses to process** extensions, functions, and triggers
(*"available to logged-in users only"*). So the harness hands Atlas only
tables/indexes/constraints, pre-seeds extensions into the dev DB, and verifies
**extensions + functions + triggers** itself via `pg_extension`/`pg_proc`/`pg_trigger`.
A trigger-drop regression proves the point: **Atlas reports "synced" while `verify` correctly
fails** (DESIGN §9 #1). Atlas `--exclude` must be schema-qualified (`public.__EFMigrationsHistory`).

## Verification

- `verify` against a scratch DB built from the squash → **zero diff** (atlas + explicit check). ✅
- Trigger-drop break test → `verify` fails as designed; restore → passes. ✅
- `dotnet test` → 7/7 green; `dotnet build -warnaserror` clean. ✅

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- forge-api §5 lean-EF refactor (shed ~277 `*Configuration.cs` → attributes) + one-directional
  drift-check CI.
- Owner-gated **no-op `apply` handoff** to the live install (deploy hold stands).

author: aldrin-isaac
body:
Slice 1.C wired the L2c session-key endpoints at \`c.newtronBase()\` — \`/newtron/v1/auth/login\` + \`/newtron/v1/auth/logout\`. **Live newtron returns 404 on those URLs**; the actual routes are \`/newt-server/v1/auth/login\` + \`/newt-server/v1/auth/logout\`. The misplacement was inherited from the upstream-doc draft (the doc-refresh PR #158 corrected the doc; this PR catches up the code).

Architecturally this makes sense: **L2c is a transport-level concern** (a session-key middleware on the newt-server outer listener), not a newtron-engine concern. A bearer minted at `/newt-server/v1/auth/login` authenticates against every engine mounted on the same newt-server — `newtron/v1/*`, `newtlab/v1/*`, `newtrun/v1/*`.

## Symptom pre-fix

- Newtcon's auth-gate POSTs to `/api/auth/login` → handler forwards to `/newtron/v1/auth/login` → **404** → operator sees `"POST /api/auth/login: not found"` with `kind: precondition_failure`.
- Logout silently called the wrong URL too (newtron 401'd it — looked like "logout failed" in audit log).
- All four auth-arc PRs (#152–#155) had this bug; it was invisible because the dev newtron we live-smoked against had L2c disabled (every login attempt 404'd for "L2c not enabled" rather than "wrong path").

## Code change

| Function | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `Login()` | `c.newtronBase() + "/auth/login"` | `c.newtServerBase() + "/auth/login"` |
| `Logout()` | `c.newtronBase() + "/auth/logout"` | `c.newtServerBase() + "/auth/logout"` |

Plus a clarifying comment on `Login()` explaining the layering.

## Tests

- `internal/newtronc/auth_test.go` — httptest mock URLs updated to `/newt-server/v1/auth/{login,logout}`.
- `internal/handlers/auth_test.go` — `TestAuthLogout_WithCookie`'s mock upstream URL updated likewise.

**All 161 backend + 107 frontend tests pass. Build clean.**

## Live verification (against dev newtron with `--auth-pam-service=newtron-test --enforce-authorization`)

```
POST /api/auth/login {alice/YourPaSsWoRd}
  → 200 + Set-Cookie: newtcon_session=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
  → {"user":"alice","expires_at":"2026-06-16T06:40:39..."}

GET /api/networks (with cookie)
  → 200 {"networks":[{"id":"1node-vs-auth",...}]}

GET /api/networks/1node-vs-auth/authorization (with cookie)
  → 200 with the real grant table (7 user_groups, 25+ permissions)
```

Bearer flows: cookie → store → context → newtronc transport → newt-server outer middleware → newtron engine.

Commit `d589e85` ("refactor: streamline web source syncing and cleanup") deleted **21 files** and reverted **6 more**, erasing the contents of PRs **#2–#7**. Four later PRs (#9–#12) were merged *on top of* that broken state, so `main` carried the destruction but also genuine newer work.

This PR (1) reconciles all of that into one branch and (2) adds the **Tier A parity features** from the SiteGist vs SiteGPT audit.

---

## Part 1 — Reconcile (restore wiped work)

1. **Branched off `main`** → PRs #9–#12 preserved.

## Part 2 — Tier A parity features (vs SiteGPT)

**1. Real multilingual (95+ languages)**
- `app/lib/language.server.ts`: dependency-free language detection (Unicode script ranges + Latin stop-word heuristic).
- `streamRAG` injects a **LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT** so the LLM answers in the user's detected language and translates non-matching context. Per-bot override via `settings.language` (`"auto"` = mirror visitor). Detection lives inside `streamRAG`, so all 5 call sites get it for free.

**3. Real sentiment analysis** (was faked from thumbs feedback)

- `Message.sentiment` + `AnalyticsSnapshot.{positive,neutral,negative}Count` (additive idempotent migration).
