author: yuvalof
body:
Local patches on top of upstream, carried by this fork.

- **Context-aware Exec** — `Conn.ExecContext` / `Stmt.ExecContext` run the statement in a goroutine and `SQLCancel` it on context cancellation, so writes honour deadlines. Upstream only made reads (`QueryContext`) cancellable.
- **Connection validation** — `Conn.IsValid` (driver.Validator) drops a connection from the pool once a statement was cancelled mid-execution, since its state is then uncertain.
- **Described-parameter binding** — `intParamBinding` / `stringParamBinding` honour the column's described SQL type/precision/scale instead of guessing from the Go value, fixing SQLSTATE 22003 ("Numeric value out of range") and 22001 ("String data, right truncated") on wide DECIMAL/NUMERIC params.
- **Fractional-second truncation** — `truncateFraction` rounds a timestamp's sub-second part to the declared scale, avoiding SQLSTATE 22008 ("Datetime field overflow").
- **DatabaseTypeName** — `SQLTypeCode` + `ColumnTypeDatabaseTypeName` surface a column's ODBC SQL type via `database/sql` (so DATE vs TIMESTAMP is distinguishable).

Unit tests added for the parameter-binding and fraction logic (no DB needed).

author: fakoli
body:
## Summary

`Character::resolve_const` matched velocity members **only** in their dotted, axis-suffixed form (e.g. `velocity.walk.fwd.x`). Standard MUGEN content — including the shipped `assets/trainingdummy` `[Statedef 20]` walk — uses the **bare** form `const(velocity.walk.fwd)` (no `.x`). The bare member matched no arm and fell through to `Value::DEFAULT` (0), so `VelSet x = const(velocity.walk.fwd)` set x-velocity 0: the character correctly entered walk state 20 on held forward/back but `pos.x` never changed — it "walked in place". This broke walking/running and jump x-velocity for **every** character using the standard bare const.

The fix adds bare-form aliases in `resolve_const` (crates/fp-character/src/lib.rs) so each bare velocity member returns the same value as its existing `.x` arm. Walk/run/jump x-velocities are authored x-first in MUGEN (walk is x-only), so the bare form aliases `.x`. The change is minimal — each existing `.x` arm gains an `|| m.eq_ignore_ascii_case("<bare>")` clause; no `.x`/`.y` arm changes value.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Bare members resolve to the correct non-zero float** — `velocity.walk.fwd/back`, `velocity.run.fwd/back`, `velocity.jump.fwd/back/neu`, `velocity.airjump.fwd/back/neu` each alias their `.x` arm. Verified by `const_bare_velocity_members_alias_x_component` (each bare value `==` its `.x` value and `!= DEFAULT`).
2. **No regression on `.x`/`.y` arms** — only `||` clauses were added to existing arms; the existing `const_resolves_velocity_members` suite (and all 789 lib tests) stay green.
3. **Behavioral test** — `training_dummy_walks_forward_and_back_via_const_velocity` loads the shipped (non-asset-gated) Training Dummy, drives it through the executor with `holdfwd` held for 30 ticks, asserts it enters walk **state 20** AND `pos.x` **strictly increases**, then `holdback` **decreases** `pos.x`. It also asserts `const(velocity.walk.fwd) == 2.4` for the dummy (`[Velocity] walk.fwd = 2.4`). This test fails on pre-fix code (x-velocity 0 → pos.x stays 0).
4. **Clippy clean** — `cargo clippy -p fp-character --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

Two stale unit tests that asserted the bare forms default to 0 (`const_partial_and_prefix_members_default`, `const_unknown_movement_velocity_members_are_safe_default`) were updated.

## Test + clippy output

```
$ cargo test -p fp-character
test tests::const_bare_velocity_members_alias_x_component ... ok
test tests::training_dummy_walks_forward_and_back_via_const_velocity ... ok
test result: ok. 789 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored   (training_dummy.rs integration target)

$ cargo clippy -p fp-character --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 8.85s   (no warnings)
```

Note: one run surfaced a flaky failure in the pre-existing `loader::tests::ac2_genuine_malformed_component_still_warns` (a `tracing` thread-local-subscriber race under parallel tests); it passes deterministically across repeated runs and is unrelated to this change (which touches no tracing/global state).

author: vilfredsikker
body:
## What & why

Questions previously doubled as both *questions* and *notes*. This PR adds a first-class **note**: a private, local-only, actionable item meant to be handed off to a coding agent — distinct from a *question* you want answered. Notes and questions share the desktop **Notes** panel, the yellow accent, and most actions; they differ by intent and one action each.

## Behavior

**Notes** (new, `notes.json`, `n-` id prefix, 📝 icon)
- Private/local-only, like questions (never pushed to GitHub).
- Created from the diff composer (new **Note** kind) and exportable.
- Actions: **Validate** (AI), resolve, delete, reply, **promote to comment**.

**Questions** (changed)
- The AI action is now **Elaborate** (answer/expand) instead of *Validate*.
- New **Promote to note** action.

**Notes panel**
- New `All | Notes | Questions` sub-tabs; threads render inline via `InlineThread`.

## Implementation

**Engine (`er-engine`)**
- `ErNotes` → `notes.json`; notes reuse the `ReviewQuestion` shape.
- `AiState.notes`, `CommentType::Note`, `CommentRef::Note`, `HintType::Note`. Notes flow through the comment index, every `comments_for_*` query, navigation, relocation/staleness, and `find_comment` alongside questions.
- `submit_note` + `n-` handling in edit/reply/update/delete/resolve paths; loader reads `notes.json`.

**Desktop backend**
- Snapshot builds note threads (`kind: "note"`), counts, replies, and inline threads.
- Commands: `add_note`, `promote_to_note`, `elaborate_with_ai`; `promote_to_comment`/`resolve_thread`/`reply_to_thread`/`ask_ai` handle notes. New `ELABORATE_CARD_AI_PROMPT`. Export gains `include_notes`.

**Desktop UI**
- Notes panel sub-tabs; `InlineThread` note styling/actions; question footer shows **Elaborate** + **Promote to note**; `DiffComposer` Note kind; export view Notes toggle. Notes reuse the question yellow with a distinct note icon.

**TUI** renders notes (yellow + 📝) in the panel and inline.

## Testing

- `cargo build --workspace --exclude er-desktop` ✓ (engine + TUI)
- `cargo test -p er-engine` — 653 pass; new `ErNotes`/`CommentRef::Note` tests pass. One pre-existing failure (`raw_diff_for_arena_uses_branch_view_not_head`) is environmental — the sandbox git wrapper breaks branch detection in the test's temp repo ("Failed to determine current branch"); unrelated to this change.

author: richardwooding
body:
**Phase 0** of #443 (continues #450, #451). The type-ref coverage half.

## Problem
`tsTypeRefQuery` had no entry for JavaScript or Ruby, so type *usages* in those languages never counted as references and the types read as dead:
- JS: a class used only via `new Foo()` → `Foo` never referenced.
- Ruby: a class used only as a superclass (`class X < Base`) or constant receiver (`Helper.go`) → `Base` / `Helper` never referenced.

## Change
- **javascript**: `(new_expression constructor: (identifier) @typeref)`
- **typescript**: also capture `new_expression` (class-via-`new`), alongside its existing type-annotation refs
- **ruby**: `(superclass (constant) @typeref)` + `(call receiver: (constant) @typeref)`

typerefs merge into `references` (`source_symbols_treesitter.go:450`), so this feeds `dead_code` / `who_calls` directly.

### Verified
- JS `new Widget()` → `refs=[Widget]` (was `[]`)
- Ruby `class Widget < Base; Helper.go` → `refs=[go Base Helper]` (was `[go]`)

## Deliberately omitted
**Perl / R / MATLAB** get no typeref query (documented in the map): they have no static type-annotation syntax, and their packages / S4 classes / classdefs are referenced through the ordinary call path already captured by `tsRefQuery` — so there's no type-only-usage gap to close.

Regression cases added to `TestExtractTreeSitterTypeRefs` for js + ruby.

## Phase 0 status (#444)
With this + #450 (benchmark) + #451 (refExtractionLangs + Perl method calls), Phase 0 is complete: a regression-gated cross-language benchmark, `dead_code`/`test_gaps` enabled for all 17 wired languages, and the reference/type-ref under-extraction gaps (Perl method calls, JS/Ruby type usage) closed.

body:
Closes #1321.

## TLDR
Adds persisted app-managed local signer slots for app-owned keys. These signers are hidden from user account projections, cannot become active, and can sign by explicit `signer_pubkey`.

## Overview
- Added `SignerSource::AppManagedLocalNsec` and actor-side app-managed signer tracking.
- Filtered app-managed signers out of `SessionState.accounts` and rejected `SwitchActive` for their pubkeys.
- Persisted a hidden local-signer roster through the existing keyring capability and restored it before active-session restore.
- Added `nmp_app_register_agent_nsec` to the FFI surface and `NmpCore.h` for registering hidden app-managed nsecs.
- Updated publish/action comments, e2e selector coverage, builder/product/FFI docs, and the Blossom ADR text to use the new registration path.

## Subjective Decisions
- Kept this PR scoped to local app-managed signers. I initially considered hidden remote signer variants, but removed that surface because #1321 is about persisted local app-owned keys and remote hidden persistence would need its own complete roster contract.
- Preserved `nmp_app_signin_nsec(make_active=0)` as a visible secondary account import. Hidden app-owned keys now use `nmp_app_register_agent_nsec` so account UI and active-account policy remain unambiguous.
- The app-managed restore test drains its normalization writes, and adjacent restore tests now drain their existing restore writes too, so the shared mock keyring cannot leak background writes across serial tests.

## Validation

author: mtalvi
body:
Related Ticket:
[APPENG-5427](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/APPENG-5427)
## Problem

Running `deploy-with-custom-image.sh` on a fresh cluster fails `test_get_pod_logs` because the edge namespace has no pods:

```
FAILED tests/mcp_servers/test_openshift_tools.py::test_get_pod_logs
  AssertionError: No running pods found in namespace
```

`helm-install` sets up RBAC for the edge namespace but never deploys a workload into it. CI handled this with inline `oc` commands in the GitHub Action, but the local deploy script didn't -- so anyone deploying locally on a fresh cluster hit this failure.

## Changes

- **`Makefile`**: Add `make deploy-edge-workload` target that creates the namespace, deploys a dummy `edge-worker` pod (`registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10`), and waits for it to be available. Idempotent and image is configurable via `EDGE_WORKLOAD_IMAGE`.
- **`scripts/local/deploy-with-custom-image.sh`**: Add `EDGE_NAMESPACE` support (defaults to `$NAMESPACE`), call `make deploy-edge-workload` after helm-install, and forward `EDGE_NAMESPACE` to both `helm-install` and `integration-tests`.
- **`.github/actions/kind/action.yaml`**: Replace inline `oc` commands with `make deploy-edge-workload` so CI and local use the same code path.

author: amir-hdri
body:
🎯 **What:** Fixed an insecure fallback configuration in `SecretManager.js` where a random master key was dynamically generated if `process.env.MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` was missing.

⚠️ **Risk:** Generating a random encryption key on the fly in production environments violates fail-safe default principles. Since the dynamically generated key only exists in memory, any payload encrypted during the application's runtime becomes undecryptable when the server restarts or scales out to a new instance. This leads to data loss for persistent encrypted data, and bypasses critical security safeguards enforcing properly deployed configuration.

🛡️ **Solution:** Removed the fallback random key generation entirely. The application now throws a FATAL ERROR if `process.env.MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not defined during `SecretManager` initialization. This ensures operators must define explicit secrets before the service can boot. Test assertions have been updated to properly mock environment variables and verify this error-throwing behavior.

## Problem

Python's `logging` module requires explicit configuration to emit output — without it, all `logger.debug()` and `logger.error()` calls are silently dropped, making it impossible to diagnose where `parse_kwork()` hangs in Railway logs.

## Solution

Replaced all debug and error instrumentation with `print()` statements tagged `[DEBUG]` and `[ERROR]`, which write directly to stdout and are captured by Railway's log collector. The core parsing logic was extracted into `_parse_kwork_inner()`, and `parse_kwork()` now wraps it with `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=120)` plus a `try/except` block so timeout and unexpected errors are both surfaced as visible `[ERROR]` lines.

author: mmakevic-amd
body:
📝 Summary of Changes
This PR fixes `TritonEmitterTest.ScaledDotIsSupportedByReferencePlatform` subtest from `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests:fusion_emitter_device_test`.

It also adds `CUBLASLT_FISSION` to the list of disabled backends when `xla_gpu_experimental_disable_binary_libraries` is set.

XLA does not set scales for BF16 type https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/111f921748b0643e70693b6b2a53a0d76b2af37a/xla/codegen/xtile/codegen/dot_algorithms.cc#L78-L120

and it also skips ScaledDotRewriter for Triton https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/81ef88c292f808f640a7d73103a47e939e3250da/xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler.cc#L700-L702

So it emits a `dot_scaled` with no scales, which explains the accuracy issues. This PR modifies `ScaledDot` function so that for bf16 it converts scale to operand type, broadcasts + reshapes it to operand shape, multiplies, then emits a plain `stablehlo.dot_general` via `EmitStableHloDotAndAdd`. This follows the logic from `ScaledDotRewriter::RewriteComputation` (https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/9e1e4f3a8d7db8c626cd4079058353ce87d4f941/xla/backends/gpu/transforms/scaled_dot_rewriter.cc#L166-L192)


🎯 Justification
Test started falling on ROCm after https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/80931bbe05b8e6e9dbb6dc8fbd8416f4131db0bd enforced Triton backend via:
```

author: daniakash
body:
## Summary

Fourth PR in the acpx-ai-harness series (after #45, #46, #47). Closes out the host-side session lifecycle so a session can survive process boundaries: a host can park its runtime mid-turn (or between turns), persist the returned lifecycle state, and a future process can reattach and keep going.

After this PR, every `HarnessV1Session` method has a real implementation except `doCompact` (which permanently throws since acpx auto-compacts internally). \`doStart\` chooses between ATTACH and RERUN based on the resume payload; the methods that emit lifecycle state surface the bridge coords so the framework can persist them.

## What this PR ships

**doSuspendTurn / doDetach.** Both call \`channel.suspend()\` at the slice boundary to drain buffered events and capture the \`lastSeenEventId\` cursor, then return a lifecycle state pointing at the live bridge (\`{ bridge: { port, token, sandboxId, lastSeenEventId } }\`). The bridge process keeps running so a follow-up \`doStart({ resumeFrom })\` or \`doStart({ continueFrom })\` can reattach. The only difference between the two is the state \`type\`: suspend returns \`continue-turn\` (mid-turn), detach returns \`resume-session\` (between turns).

**doStop.** Sends \`{ type: 'detach' }\` to the bridge and awaits the \`bridge-detach\` reply that carries an adapter-defined payload. Then races a 5s timeout against \`proc.wait()\` and kills the process. Returns the adapter payload as the lifecycle state's \`data\`. The detach-reply machinery is extracted into \`host-detach.ts\` so it can be unit-tested in isolation.

**doStart 3-rung dispatcher.** Replaces the resume/continue rejection from #47:

  - **ATTACH** — \`pickResumeCoords()\` walks \`continueFrom\` then \`resumeFrom\` (continueFrom wins when both are present, since mid-turn intent is the more specific signal). When coords are found, \`tryAttachToExistingBridge()\` seeds a \`SandboxChannel\` with the saved port/token/lastSeenEventId, calls \`channel.open({ resume: true })\`, and on success returns the open channel. On any failure (sandbox id changed, WS unreachable, auth rejected), the attempt is silently swallowed.
  - **RERUN** — the existing fresh-spawn path. acpx persists session state to disk via \`stateDir + sessionKey\`, so even when the in-sandbox bridge is gone for good, the fresh bridge can pick up the persisted session on the first prompt.

**doContinueTurn.** Drives the in-flight turn after \`doStart({ continueFrom })\`. On ATTACH, it just subscribes via \`wirePromptControl\` and resolves \`done\` when the bridge emits its finish event. On RERUN, it sends a \`Continue.\` nudge prompt with \`continue: true\` so acpx loads the persisted session and re-drives a turn — lossy in the sense that events from the prior process's turn tail aren't recovered, but that's the unavoidable trade-off when the bridge process is gone.

**Refactors.** \`createSession\` extracted into \`host-create-session.ts\` so the session factory and its lifecycle methods are testable without going through \`doStart\` (and so \`host-session.ts\` stays under the 300-line budget). \`awaitProcExit\` moved into \`host-session-utils.ts\` and tolerates an undefined \`proc\` so the ATTACH path (where the host doesn't own the bridge process) shares the same shutdown helper.

\`session.isResume\` now reflects whether \`doStart\` was given a resume payload. \`respawnStrategy\` (\`'fresh' | 'attach' | 'rerun'\`) is threaded through \`createSession\` so \`doContinueTurn\` knows which branch to take.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bun run lint\` exit 0
- [x] \`bun run typecheck\` clean across all six workspace packages
- [x] \`bun run build\` still emits all four expected artifacts (\`dist/index.js\`, \`dist/index.d.ts\`, \`dist/bridge/index.js\`, \`dist/bridge/package.json\`)
- [x] Harness unit suite: **95 tests across 10 files** (was 79 before this PR, +16 across attach decoder, createSession lifecycle methods, doContinueTurn ATTACH/RERUN dispatch, doDestroy idempotency, doCompact rejection, isResume flag passthrough)
- [x] Provider and acpx-test-helpers suites unchanged

## What this PR doesn't ship yet

- **Host AI SDK tool routing** — still warned-but-not-forwarded (the \`unsupported-tool\` CallWarning from PR #46 still fires on \`start.tools\`). Lands when an HTTP MCP server inside the bridge gets built.
- **End-to-end tests** — against a real harness sandbox provider. The unit tests cover the lifecycle wiring; e2e tests prove the whole thing works against real codex / claude-code / gemini binaries.
- **README expansion** — consumer examples + sandbox setup notes.

## Summary

- **New decision type `redact`**: Cedar policies can emit `@decision("redact") @redact_fields("field1,field2")` to allow a tool call but strip sensitive fields from parameters before execution — preventing PII/secrets from reaching tools that don't need them.
- **Severity order**: `quarantine > require_approval > redact > allow` — a `require_approval` annotation on any matched policy beats `redact`, and `quarantine` beats both.
- **Audit trail**: `AseEvent` gains `redacted_fields: Vec<String>` so every SOC event records which fields were stripped (empty for all non-redact decisions).
- **Python SDK**: `protect_tool` (sync + async) handles `redact` by replacing listed kwargs with `"[REDACTED]"` before calling the tool; non-kwarg positional args are passed through unchanged.
- **Example policy** added to both `policies.cedar` files: `secrets/rotate_credential` → redact `api_key,password,secret,token`.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gateway/src/events.rs` | `AseEvent.redacted_fields: Vec<String>` with `#[serde(default)]` |
| `gateway/src/models.rs` | `AuthorizeResponse.redacted_fields` (`skip_serializing_if = Vec::is_empty`) |
| `gateway/src/policy.rs` | `redact` escalation + `@redact_fields` parsing + `AuthorizeDecision.redacted_fields` |
| `gateway/src/routes.rs` | Thread `redacted_fields` through; clear on route-layer override; 2 new tests |
| `gateway/src/policy.rs` | 2 new policy tests (basic annotation + require_approval beats redact) |
| `policies.cedar` + `gateway/policies.cedar` | Example `@decision("redact")` canary policy (kept in sync) |
| `gateway/src/{baseline,correlate,detect,events,ingest,main,rule_dsl}.rs` | `redacted_fields: vec![]` added to all ~16 AseEvent construction sites |
| `sdk-python/aegisagent/decorator.py` | `redact` branch in sync + async `protect_tool` |
| `sdk-python/tests/test_sdk.py` | 3 new `TestRedactDecision` tests |

author: thekevinbot
body:
## Summary

Implements slice 1/4 of the **e2e attestation nudge** (#17): the `testing-conventions e2e attest '<command>'` command (#67). The nudge gets agents to run e2e tests locally — `attest` records that a run happened against the current commit. The companion CI-side `e2e verify` (#68) and the remaining slices (#69 docs, #71 dogfood) follow.

## What `e2e attest` does

`testing-conventions e2e attest '<command>'`:
- Runs `<command>` (the e2e suite) via the shell, streaming its output.
- Writes `e2e-attestation.json` recording the command, a timestamp, the exit code, and **the commit SHA it was run against** (HEAD).
- Commits that file as its own commit on top — the attestation names the code commit beneath it, since a commit can't contain its own SHA.
- Writes/commits **regardless of the command's exit code** (force a *run*, not a *pass*); exits `0` once recorded.

Library API: `testing_conventions::e2e::{attest, Attestation, ATTESTATION_PATH}`. Purely additive — a new `e2e` command group and module; nothing existing changes.

## Tests (red → green)

- `58352e1` — red integration + e2e tests + a compiling stub.
- `c276b82` — the implementation (turns them green) + docs.

`tests/e2e_attest.rs` (4 integration) and `tests/e2e_attest_e2e.rs` (2 binary) build throwaway git repos and assert `attest` names HEAD, writes the file, commits it on top, force-runs on a failing command, and errors outside a git repo.

## Notes

- Rebased onto current `main`; `CHANGELOG.md` / `MIGRATIONS.md` / `docs/reference/index.md` updated (changelog gate satisfied).
- The branch carries both the red and the green commit. Per AGENTS.md the red tests are normally witnessed red *on CI* first; here the prior session witnessed them red locally (GitHub access was down at the time), so this PR opens already green — surfaced here for transparency.

Closes #67.

body:
Introduces **The Necromancer's March**, a third sibling game that thematically inverts the Light-Bringer premise. Instead of carrying light to cleanse cities, the player is a necromancer marching on villages to raise skeleton hordes and overrun their defenders.

## Changes

- **New game module** (`necro.ts` / `necro.html`): Real-time "commander" gameplay where the player moves via joystick/WASD, raises skeletons from graves (costing souls), commands auto-targeting minions, and razes houses to heal the horde and summon bone-totems. Victory condition is defeating all knights; defeat is losing all health.

- **Documentation updates** (README.md):
  - Reordered game links to feature The Necromancer's March as the second spinoff (after The Burning Vigil)
  - Added full game description section explaining the inversion mechanic, commander-style controls, skeleton economy, house-razing layer, and legacy tracking (villages overrun, best clear time, houses razed)
  - Updated tech section to list `necro.ts`, `necro.html`, `necro.webmanifest`, and `necro-test.mjs`
  - Updated service worker and manifest references to account for three games instead of two
  - Updated deployment docs to note compilation of `necro.ts → necro.js`

- **Art prompts** (new directory `art/prompts/necro/`): Four self-contained Gemini generation prompts for village establishing cards:
  - `village-hollowmere.txt` — the first march, sparse and drowsy
  - `village-aubers.txt` — fortified chantry-town, hardest village
  - `village-barrows.txt` — burial mounds with thick watch
  - `village-fen.txt` — lawless marsh with gibbet, few defenders

The game shares the world, cities (re-themed as villages), and the procedural SVG art system with the other games, ensuring it is fully playable before any PNG assets exist.

## Summary
Adds a client-side **configuration generator** to the docs site: a decision-tree wizard that emits copy/paste-able Claude config JSON, `.env`, `docker run`, `docker-compose.yml`, or a systemd unit for the user's exact deployment. Everything runs in the browser (nothing is sent anywhere); non-secret answers are encoded in the URL for shareable configs, and secret fields are quarantined from the URL with `<YOUR_…>` placeholders in the output.

## What's here
- **Page + assets:** `docs/configuration-generator.md` + `docs/javascripts/config-wizard/{wizard-spec.json, wizard.js, generators.js}` + `docs/stylesheets/config-wizard.css`. Vanilla JS, no build step. The single `wizard-spec.json` is the only source of questions/var-mappings; the JS are pure renderer/transformers.
- **Drift control (the load-bearing part):** `tests/test_config_wizard_spec.py` AST-extracts the canonical env-var inventory from the codebase (the `env()` helper family incl. the `env as _env` alias, full-literal and f-string `os.environ.get`, plus the upstream `ServerConfig` source via `inspect.getsourcefile`) and enforces two-way containment against the spec. Adding a config var without wiring the wizard fails CI; a small documented allowlist covers vars deliberately not surfaced. The generator's hardcoded var names are gated too.
- **Browser smoke test:** `tests/test_config_wizard_smoke.py` (Playwright, `browser`-marked) drives the built page through a local + a server/OIDC path; wired into `docs.yml`. It skips cleanly in the main test lane (no built site).
- **Docs:** linked from `configuration.md`, `index.md`, and `README.md`.

author: abdul-rahman-0x
body:
### Overview
This pull request transitions the billing infrastructure from basic functionality to production-grade reliability. I identified a critical logic gap where the system could not differentiate between active, canceled, and expired subscription states, leading to inconsistent user redirects and redundant Stripe customer profiles.

### The Problem
Previously, the server actions followed a "happy path" that assumed every checkout was a first-time purchase. This caused two main issues:
1. Data Integrity: Users with existing records were being misdirected back to the dashboard even if they were attempting to upgrade or renew a plan.
2. Stripe Clutter: The system was creating new Stripe Customer IDs for every session instead of maintaining a single source of truth for each user.

### The Solution
I refactored the billing server actions to implement a more defensive and intelligent logic flow:
- **State Awareness:** The system now validates the specific subscription state before initiating the Stripe API call, ensuring users only reach checkout when necessary.
- **Identifier Persistence:** I implemented logic to fetch and reuse existing `stripeCustomerId` records, preventing duplicate profiles in our payment gateway.
- **Stripe Metadata Integration:** Added specific `userId` metadata to the Stripe session objects, ensuring that our backend webhooks can accurately map asynchronous payment events to the correct Neon database records.

This refactor ensures the application can handle real-world user lifecycles—including plan switching and renewals—with absolute type safety and zero data desync.

Closes #8

Closes the Keycloak↔Entra capability-broker wiring (issue #24, waves 1–5 implemented + Phase 5 docs). Replaces the fail-closed stubs and identity placeholders with live, config-gated paths. **Every path fails closed on missing config/mapping.**

## What's here

### Host implementation (T1–T8) — `feat(host)` commit
- **Foundations (T1/T2):** Entra/Keycloak/Dynamics config (tenant+client an inseparable pair); shared `HttpPost`/`GraphHttp` transports; realm JWT signature verifier (jose remote JWKS, signature-only); fail-closed agent-client credential resolver.
- **Agent path (T3):** live Keycloak token endpoint (`client_credentials` → RFC 8693 WIF exchange); config-presence broker gating — un-granted capability refused at the Keycloak hop with **zero Entra egress**.
- **User inbound + exchange (T6/T7):** defensive `teams` claim parse in the pure validator (no Zod); required `authorizeUserRun`; host-side `subjectToken` side-channel threaded run→exchange; real RFC 8693 `exchangeV2` (sub=user, azp=agent), fail-closed on undefined subject token.
- **Hardening (T8):** `AGENT_CLIENT_MAP` (dagId→real client id) replacing the identity placeholder; HITL approver authz at parity with the HTTP path (`aadObjectId`→team, gated by `canAccessDag` before `recordDecision`); **per-team conversation routing** via `HITL_TEAM_CHANNELS` (cards to the team's own channel, default fallback); Dynamics per-org host (fails closed on unset — no `https:///` sentinel).

### Docs — `docs` commit
- **ADR-0062** (team modeling via realm roles) and **ADR-0063** (defensive `teams` parse, no Zod).
- **Phase 5 operator runbook** (`docs/runbooks/entra-fugue-agents-provisioning.md`) — spike gate with mandatory negative controls, Appendix A provisioning, 0-secret/0-cert invariant, agent+user e2e, evidence template.
- team-security living doc + ADR index cross-references; HITL bot provisioning runbook; the spec/architecture/plan-alignment artifacts.

## Verification
- **Tests: 1197 pass / 0 fail; typecheck clean** (host package).
- Each wave passed a multi-agent wave-gate review (spec-check + code-review + silent-failure + test + type-design + comment). Wave 5's per-team-routing finding was fixed and re-reviewed clean.

## Not done in this PR (needs a live tenant)
- **Phase 5 / T9 live verification is PENDING-LIVE-VERIFICATION.** The runbook is ready but spikes #1–#3 and the Appendix A provisioning must be executed by an operator against a real Entra tenant + reachable `fugue-platform` realm. The four spikes are not marked PASS.

## 측정 (사용자 VM probe)
```

HK 신고저: 1회차 0.0s · 2회차 0.0s

## 원인
TW 렌더가 `enrich_for_panel` 에서 **종목당 yfinance 동기 호출**: `_fetch_mcaps`(fast_info+history), `_fetch_display_names`(`.info`), `_fetch_industries` — docstring 에 *"백그라운드 전용 / render 경로 금지"* 라 명시돼 있는데도 렌더에서 콜. 콜드(10분 캐시 만료) 시 ~60종목 × 슬로우 콜 = **8.2s 블록**.

- 렌더 = `_enrich_compute(allow_slow=False)`: persist 시총 + 영구 이름 + 업종 벌크맵 + 번역 캐시**만**(yfinance per-ticker·Flash **0**) → 즉시 반환.

`_backfill_industries` 의 기존 "렌더 경로 .info 금지, 캐시+벌크만" 패턴을 enrich 전체로 확장.

author: rohan919477
body:
## Summary

This PR integrates the backend authentication register API with the Flutter mobile signup flow.

The registration screen now sends real account-creation requests to the Django backend using `POST /api/auth/register/`, replacing the previous mock/delayed signup behavior. The frontend submits the backend-required fields: `username`, `email`, `password1`, and `password2`.

On successful registration, the app shows the email-verification state, matching the backend flow where a verification email is sent after account creation.

---

## Changes Made

### Authentication API Integration

* Added typed register request and response models.
* Connected the signup form to the backend `POST /api/auth/register/` endpoint.
* Replaced mock registration logic with a real API call through the existing auth service layer.
* Added Riverpod-based auth controller handling for registration state.
* Added loading, success, and error handling for the signup flow.
* Replaced unexpected registration response errors with user-friendly `AppException` handling.

### Register Screen Updates

* Converted the register screen to use Riverpod state.
* Added a separate Username field because the backend requires `username`.
* Added reusable username validation for required values, minimum length, and alphanumeric-only usernames.
* Kept full name as frontend/user setup data instead of incorrectly sending it as the backend username.
* Disabled form actions while registration is loading.
* Preserved the email-verification screen after successful account creation.

### Duplicate Account Validation

* Added backend validation for duplicate email addresses and usernames before database constraints are reached.
* Duplicate registration attempts now return a JSON `400 Bad Request` validation response instead of exposing Django’s HTML debug page.
* The Flutter app remains on the signup screen and displays the returned backend validation message in a SnackBar.

### API Configuration Updates

* Updated the auth register endpoint to match the backend route:

  * `POST /api/auth/register/`
* Standardised API URL composition so `/api/` is defined once in the base URL.
* Updated endpoint paths to remain relative to the API base URL, avoiding inconsistent endpoint prefixes in future API integrations.

### Flutter Web CORS Support

* Added `django-cors-headers` to backend dependencies.
* Configured `corsheaders.middleware.CorsMiddleware` before Django’s `CommonMiddleware`.
* Allowed local Flutter Web development origins using `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` with dynamic development ports.
* Restricted CORS handling to `/api/` routes.
* Gated local CORS origin configuration behind `DEBUG`.
* Rebuilt the Docker image to install the new backend dependency.

### Test Updates

* Added a widget test confirming that the Username field is rendered.
* Added unit tests for username validation.
* Updated signup validation tests to account for the new Username field and the longer form layout.
* Added final newlines to affected files to keep diffs clean.

---

## Backend Endpoint Used

```http
POST /api/auth/register/
```

Request body:

```json
{
  "username": "testuser123",
  "email": "testuser123@example.com",
  "password1": "StrongPassword123!",
  "password2": "StrongPassword123!"
}
```

Successful response:

```json
{
  "detail": "Verification e-mail sent."
}
```

Example duplicate-email validation response:

```json
{
  "email": [
    "An account already exists with this email address."
  ]
}
```

---

## Test Plan

* [x] Backend containers run successfully through Docker Compose.
* [x] Swagger returns `201 Created` for `POST /api/auth/register/`.
* [x] Swagger response returns `"Verification e-mail sent."`.
* [x] Flutter signup screen submits to the backend register API.
* [x] Django logs show `POST /api/auth/register/ HTTP/1.1 201`.
* [x] App shows the email-verification screen after successful registration.
* [x] Confirmed Flutter Web CORS preflight allows requests from the local development server.
* [x] Confirmed a valid registration creates a user in the PostgreSQL database.
* [x] Confirmed a valid registration sends an email-verification message.
* [x] Confirmed duplicate email returns a JSON `400` response and displays a clear error SnackBar.
* [x] Confirmed duplicate-email registration remains on the signup screen.
* [x] Confirmed invalid backend password rules return a `400` response and display an error SnackBar.
* [x] Confirmed failed registration does not show the verification state.
* [x] `flutter test` passes.
* [x] `flutter analyze` completes with existing informational findings in unrelated features.

---

## Notes

* Registration now uses the real backend endpoint: `POST /api/auth/register/`.
* The backend returns `"Verification e-mail sent."`, so the app shows the email-verification screen after successful signup.
* Flutter Web requires backend CORS configuration because it runs from a separate local origin, such as `http://localhost:<port>`.
* Local-development CORS origins are enabled only when `DEBUG` is enabled.
* Verification emails may appear in the recipient’s spam folder during local development because the message currently uses the default `example.com` template/domain.
* The backend Docker Compose service name for logs is `web`.

---

## Out of Scope

This PR only covers register/signup integration using `POST /api/auth/register/`.

Login, token storage, refresh-token handling, token verification, authenticated requests, and logout will be implemented in a separate follow-up PR.

---

## Related Issue

author: venosta-web
body:
Closes #478.

## What

Completes the exhaust-fan ownership transfer. The `ExhaustFanController` becomes the **sole owner** of `exhaust_fan_entities`; the `DehumidifierCoordinator` now controls only `dehumidifier_entities`.

Because `ExhaustFanConfig` defaults to `enabled=False`, installs that previously had `control_dehumidifier` on with `exhaust_fan_entities` set would silently stop cycling their exhaust fans. We **do not auto-migrate** (old on/off humidity thresholds carry no speed-band information). Instead a per-growspace HA repair issue directs affected growers to the Exhaust panel so the opt-in is explicit.

## Decisions (ADR-0019)

- **Trigger** (per growspace): `control_dehumidifier` **AND** `exhaust_fan_entities` **AND NOT** `exhaust_fan_config.enabled`. The `NOT enabled` guard is a deliberate refinement over the literal acceptance criteria — a grower already on the new controller isn't nagged.
- **Create-or-clear**: a shared helper raises/deletes the issue, called from `async_setup_entry` and from every service that mutates a trigger input without a full reload (`configure_exhaust_fan`, `set_dehumidifier_control`, `configure_environment`), so the repair self-heals on opt-in.
- **Presentation**: `is_fixable=False`, `IssueSeverity.WARNING`, `issue_id = exhaust_fan_migration_{growspace_id}`.
- **Out of scope** (accepted edge case): a switch-based exhaust fan the dehumidifier last commanded *on* may be left stuck on until the grower enables the new controller — the issue's framed risk is fans *not cycling*.

## Notable fix found in review

`configure_environment` rebuilt `EnvironmentConfig` **without** carrying `exhaust_fan_config`, silently resetting the exhaust controller to `enabled=False` on any environment edit. Now preserved, mirroring how `circulation_fan_config` already falls back to the stored config.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `DehumidifierCoordinator` controls only `dehumidifier_entities`
- [x] Existing dehumidifier tests updated for the narrowed controlled set
- [x] Repair raised for installs with `control_dehumidifier` on + `exhaust_fan_entities` configured (+ controller not yet enabled)
- [x] Repair not raised without that prior configuration
- [x] Tests cover the repair-trigger condition and the dehumidifier behavior change

## Testing

- Full suite: **4520 passed**, 46 snapshots intact
- ruff check + format clean on changed files

## Docs

- New `docs/adr/0019-exhaust-fan-sole-ownership.md`
- `CONTEXT.md`: **Exhaust Ownership** + **Exhaust Migration Repair** glossary terms

> Note: the original issue cited "ADR 0017" for the transfer, but 0017 is the water-aggregation ADR and 0018 never documented the dehumidifier relinquishing exhaust — hence the new ADR-0019.

author: djwaldo
body:
Three improvements to `ts-convert-from-tableau` (**v1.13.0**), learned from a live migration of *Bank Data Dashboard and Story.twb*.

## 1. Migration-scope choice (Step 1.5)
Ask right after auth **what to migrate**:
- **Models + Liveboards** (default) — full flow
- **Tables + Models only** — skip Steps 8–11
- **Liveboards only** — skip Steps 4–7.5; build on an **existing model** the user picks

New **Step 1.5a model picker** mirrors the connection prompt: **G** GUID / **N** name / **F** filter / **L** list-all (slow, warned). Models are found via `--subtype WORKSHEET` filtered to `metadata_header.worksheetVersion == "V2"` — there is **no `MODEL` subtype** in `metadata search` (confirmed against the instance). Steps are annotated with the scopes that run them.

## 2. obj_id read-back fix (Steps 7, 10-pre, 10c)
**The bug we hit:** a requested `obj_id` on a *fresh* model import is **not honored** — ThoughtSpot reassigns `{Name-with-dashes}-{guid8}` (requested `P1UKBankCustomers-bankdemo1` → actual `P1-UK-Bank-Customers-49347340`). Because the liveboard's viz `tables[].obj_id` reused the written value, **all 7 tiles failed to bind** (`"No table with object_id … found"`), forcing a delete + re-import.

**The fix:** read the model's **real** obj_id back (import-response `objId` / `ts metadata search --guid` / export) and use only that for viz `tables[].obj_id` and the cohort `worksheet.obj_id`. Captured once in Step 10-pre alongside the parameter UUIDs.

## 3. Efficiency guidance
New **Efficiency** block + relaxed the "one question at a time" rule: batch independent prompts (mode+scope, the count/bin/cohort decisions, theme+chips), parse the TWB in one pass, and capture obj_id + param UUIDs + resolved column names in a **single** Step 10-pre export. Removing the obj_id failure cycle is the biggest wall-clock win.

## Scope / validation
Tableau-only (it's the liveboard-building, dashboard-bearing skill). The obj_id lesson is generally true and could be promoted to `shared/schemas/ts-model-conversion-invariants.md` for the snowflake/databricks from-* skills as a follow-up. All pre-commit validators pass.

author: butterflyfish
body:
Brings the native Windows terminal panel up to the macOS terminal surface: a
real split-pane subsystem, full right-click parity, and localized menu strings.

## What

**Split panes.** Each terminal tab now owns a *pane tree* (a leaf PTY session or
a horizontal/vertical split) instead of a single session. The focused pane takes
input and the menu's pane actions.
- Split Right / Left / Down / Up (mirrors the macOS surface), Close Pane.
- Click a pane to focus it; the focused pane shows a focus ring.
- Drag the divider between panes to rebalance (live resize cursor; ratio 5–95%);
  each pane's PTY resizes to its rect.
- `exit` removes a pane, its sibling takes the space; the last pane closes the
  tab; the last tab closes the panel.

**Right-click parity** with the macOS terminal context menu: Copy · Paste ·
Split ×4 · New Tab · Close Pane · Change Tab Title · Reset Terminal · Terminal
Read-only (checkmark). Right-clicking focuses the pane under the cursor first.

**i18n.** Added a `terminal.*` section to the i18n catalog (en-US + zh-CN,
regenerated bindings) and routed the menu + panel title through
`lingxia_logic::i18n::t` — previously hardcoded English.

## Commits (each self-contained, CI/clippy/fmt clean)
1. i18n: terminal strings (keys + wiring)
2. split-pane subsystem (model, layout, multi-pane render, menu, poll/resize)
3. left-click pane focus
4. read-only toggle
5. draggable dividers
6. clippy-clean the shell terminal build

## Testing
- `cargo clippy` `-D warnings` clean on the **CI toolchain (1.95.0)** for every
  windows-sdk feature combo: `standard`, `shell-runtime`, and
  `shell-runtime,terminal-runtime`; workspace clippy clean; `cargo fmt` clean.
- The **standalone Windows example app** (`examples/lingxia-showcase/windows`,
  which enables shell+terminal) builds and links with **zero warnings**.
- Note: that example is `exclude`d from the main workspace, so CI's *Windows
  Target* job compiles windows-sdk only with `standard` — the shell/terminal
  paths aren't linted by CI. I validated them with the explicit combo builds
  above (and fixed three pre-existing shell-only clippy lints they surfaced).
- Not exercised: live PTY behavior in the running app (GUI) — to be confirmed by
  manual run; logic is compile- and lint-verified.

## i18n follow-up (out of scope, by layering)
The native file/media dialog titles in `lingxia-platform`
(`windows/file.rs`, `windows/media.rs`: "Select folder/file", "Choose
Images/Videos/Media") are still hardcoded. `lingxia-platform` sits *below* the
i18n string table (`lingxia-logic` depends on `lingxia-platform`), so localizing
them cleanly needs locale plumbing into the platform layer — a separate change,
not folded into this terminal PR.

author: smalluban
body:
When reloading the extension in Chrome, `OptionsObserver` listeners for `terms` and `contextMenu` were resolving via microtasks and calling `chrome.contextMenus.update` before `onInstalled` had finished recreating the menus, causing an uncaught "Cannot find menu item with id ghostery" error.

The fix removes the two `OptionsObserver` listeners entirely and instead moves `contextMenu`/`terms` visibility logic into `updateVisibility`, which is already called on tab activation and page load. The `ID_PARENT` menu is now created with `enabled: false, visible: false` as a safe default, and `updateVisibility` updates it to the correct state on first invocation. This eliminates the race without any silent error swallowing.

author: ventsislavnikolov
body:
## Problem
Production 500s on **every** SSR request:
`{"status":500,"unhandled":true,"message":"HTTPError"}` →
`Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` (confirmed in Vercel runtime logs).

`src/start.ts` registers `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware`, so `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` is imported on every request — but the package was absent from the deployed function bundle.

## Root cause
`vite.config.ts` externalized `/^@sentry\//` via `rollupConfig.external`. Nitro's file-tracer (`nf3`) only traces packages whose imports flow through *its* `resolveId` hook; rolldown strips a `rollupConfig.external` match to a bare specifier first, so Nitro never copied `@sentry` into the lambda's `node_modules`. It resolved locally only because Node ESM walks up to the project-root `node_modules` — the isolated Vercel lambda has no parent to fall back to.

Regression window: v1.10.4 (200) → v1.10.6 (500). `vite.config` is unchanged since scaffold; the trigger is the 2026-06-14 dependency bump — `nitro` is pinned to a moving `nitro-nightly` whose newer trace behavior stopped copying the rollup-externalized package.

## Fix
Drop the manual `rollupConfig.external` and externalize via Nitro's `traceDeps`, which both externalizes the package (OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation stays intact, not inlined) **and** traces it into the function output. Robust against further nitro-nightly drift.

## Verification
- Vercel-preset rebuild: traced deps **6 → 29** — lambda `node_modules` now has `@sentry`, `@opentelemetry`, `import-in-the-middle`, `require-in-the-middle`, still `sharp`.
- `@sentry` remains a bare external in the bundle (not inlined).
- **Isolated** lambda run (copied outside the repo, no parent `node_modules`): `GET /` → **200** (pre-fix: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; Biome clean.

The scheduled **Cert Bot** was failing — not a code bug, a real alert firing: `clearglassinc.github.io`'s TLS cert is at **19 days** (< the 21-day strict threshold), so the bot exits 1. But that certificate is **GitHub-managed and auto-renews** — there's no action a maintainer can take, so failing the build is noise.

### Fix
`scripts/cert_bot.py` now treats platform-managed hosts (`*.github.io`, `*.pages.dev`) as **advisory**:
- still-valid-but-soon → `::warning`, **non-failing**
- actually expired → still `::error` (a real outage)
- domains we control (custom domains) keep **strict** failures unchanged

### Verification
- New behavior simulated: `github.io @ 19d strict → exit 0 (warning)`; `custom domain @ 19d strict → exit 1 (error)`.
- Added 2 unit tests; **full suite 231 passed, 2 skipped**; ruff clean.

All other workflows on `main` are green (CI, Deploy Pages, Policy Gate, Security, IP Protection, Control Surface Feeds, Health Monitor).

## Summary
Adds a minimal HTTP health check server to the monitoring worker process to support Railway's health check requirements. The worker now serves a `/health` endpoint on a configurable port without affecting the main monitoring loop.

## Key Changes
- Import `threading` and `http.server` modules to support HTTP health endpoint
- Add `_start_health_server()` function that:
  - Creates a bare-minimum HTTP server with a single `/health` GET handler
  - Returns `{"status":"ok","service":"monitoring-worker"}` on `/health` requests
  - Suppresses per-request HTTP logs to avoid noise
  - Runs in a daemon thread so it doesn't block the main monitoring loop
- Update `main()` to:
  - Read `PORT` environment variable (defaults to 8000 if not set or invalid)
  - Start the health server early, before the monitoring loop initializes
  - Allows Railway's health check to pass while RPC probes and schema checks run

## Implementation Details
- Health server runs in a daemon thread named `worker-health-server`, leaving the main thread free for the monitoring loop
- Responds with 200 OK + JSON body for `/health`, 404 for other paths
- Logs server startup with host, port, and path for observability
- No changes to existing monitoring logic or configuration validation
- Railway worker service can now be configured with `healthcheckPath=/health` and port exposure via `$PORT` environment variable

author: yzyzieee
body:
## Problem
A classmate uploaded a preprint/author-manuscript with no printed venue or year. Gemini, told to extract metadata, **invented a plausible-but-wrong journal and year** — which then gets published as fact. (The paper is actually findable: ICASSP 2025.)

## Fix
1. **Prompt hardening** — venue, DOI, and year are returned **only if explicitly printed in the document** (publication line, DOI string, copyright/date). Otherwise empty/null. Never infer from the topic, the authors' usual venues, or the reference list. A missing value is correct; an invented one is flagged as a serious error.
2. **Crossref recovery** — when venue/DOI/year is missing, the extract route searches Crossref by title (`query.bibliographic`) and, on a strong **title-overlap match** (overlap coefficient ≥ 0.85 with a ≥4 distinct-token floor), fills **only the missing fields** from the authoritative record (year, venue, DOI, publication type). It never overwrites what was genuinely in the document.
3. **No confident match → stays empty** → the existing required-`year` validation prompts the submitter to add it (and venue can be filled in the review). No fabrication either way.

## Verified
- Live Crossref query for the reported paper recovers **year 2025 / venue "ICASSP 2025…" / conference-paper** (DOI `10.1109/icassp49660.2025.10887958`).
- Title-overlap simulation: both the short and full title variants score ≥ 0.85 and accept the correct record; a bogus query returns 0.286 → rejected (no fabrication).
- `npm run build` compiles + lints.

**Root cause of the cartoon face + robotic voice:** the Anam SDK has one bare dependency, `import … from "buffer"`, which the browser can't resolve natively. **Verified against the live Anam API this session:** `POST /v1/engine/session` returns **200** with persona `{name, avatarId}` (real engine `connect-us.anam.ai` + Cloudflare TURN). Adding a `voiceId` returns **400**, so the persona stays `{name, avatarId}` and the avatar uses its bound voice.

## O que muda

Substitui o modelo de **1 habilidade secreta com 3 níveis** (Bronze/Prata/Ouro) por **3 habilidades distintas por linha evolutiva, todas podendo ficar ativas ao mesmo tempo**. Ser o **Destaque do Dia** desbloqueia a próxima da lista — 1ª vez → habilidade 1, 2ª → 2, 3ª → 3.

`pokemon.secretLevel` (1 habilidade / 3 níveis) → `pokemon.secretCount` (0–3 = quantas das três desbloqueou).

## Mapeamento por linha (de `pokemons-abilities.csv`)

| Linha | 1ª | 2ª | 3ª |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sandshrew | Rollout | Dig | Sand Rush |
| Nidoran♀/♂ | Rivalidade | Hustle | Dig |
| Diglett | Dig | Sand Rush | Dig+ |
| Geodude | Sturdy | Explosion | Rollout |
| Onix | Weak Armor | Sturdy | Rock Head |
| Cubone | Rock Head | Battle Armor | Lightning Rod |
| Rhyhorn | Lightning Rod | Rock Head | Reckless |
| Omanyte | Swift Swim | Shell Armor | Weak Armor |
| Kabuto | Battle Armor | Weak Armor | Swift Swim |
| Aerodactyl | Fly | Rock Head | Fly+ |

## Efeitos (de `secret-abilities.csv`)

- **Ajustados** (agora fixos): Weak Armor (dano ×2 + **+20% velocidade por ponto de HP faltante**), Sturdy (1 HP, **1×/dia**), Shell Armor (**dano vira 1**), Rollout +10%, Battle Armor +30%, Rock Head +50%/−50%, Rivalidade +10% por aliado do mesmo gênero (+10% batalha vs mesmo gênero).
- **Novos**: **Hustle** (+10% batalha / −10% missão), **Explosion** (ao perder, derrota o inimigo e perde metade do HP máx), **Lightning Rod** (contra inimigo Elétrico o portador assume o duelo), **Reckless** (ao perder, retenta sem passar a vez), **Dig+** (um buraco sempre no ginásio), **Fly+** (leva o time inteiro voando).
- **Sem efeito ainda** (sem clima): **Sand Rush** e **Swift Swim** — registradas e exibidas, prontas para os efeitos climáticos futuros.

## Observações do pedido atendidas

- **Dig múltiplo**: `today.digTunnel` → `today.digTunnels`. Cada Pokémon do roster com Dig/Dig+ abre **um túnel de 2 buracos**; vários portadores = vários túneis, podendo sobrepor. Dig+ ancora um buraco no ginásio.
- **Explosion como último Pokémon**: o KO mútuo (último de cada lado) ainda **vence a batalha** → recompensas aplicadas normalmente.

## Verificação

- `tsc -b` limpo; **306 testes passam** (novos para Explosion, Lightning Rod, Reckless, Shell Armor=1, Weak Armor por HP, Dig múltiplo).

🚨 Severity: HIGH

💡 Vulnerability: The `brandName` setting loaded from persistent storage was directly interpolated into the sidebar's `innerHTML` without sanitization, creating a stored DOM XSS vulnerability.

🎯 Impact: An attacker who can modify the `brandName` setting could inject malicious scripts that would execute whenever the sidebar is rendered.

author: lionsr
body:
## Summary

This PR makes the plotting-facing k-space reference helpers depend on the canonical mode convention in `mode_analysis.jl`.

The main changes are:

- move `dispersion.jl` after `mode_analysis.jl` in the package include order;
- compute plotted quasiparticle energies with `mode_energy_Jh` rather than a separate trigonometric expression;
- compute generic plotted ground-state Fourier occupations from the canonical `bogoliubov_angle`;
- make special integer modes (`k=0,N/2`) use the target spin/parity sector when a result file stores `mode_gF`, so APBC even-sector references do not incorrectly occupy a single special mode;
- persist the reference fermionic sector as `RESULT_MODE_GF` for ordinary ED k-space result files, even when `measure_modes=false`, so plotting code can reconstruct the correct fixed-sector reference curve;
- recover spin boundary metadata from both `bc` and `ham_params_bc`, and ignore `mode_gF` when the spin boundary is unknown or open;
- make odd half-integer fixed-parity sectors include one lowest-energy generic quasiparticle in the plotted ground-state reference;
- pass the chain length `N` and stored fermionic sector from plotting call sites that already have them;
- add regression tests comparing the public plotting helpers to the canonical mode-energy and Bogoliubov definitions, including the special-mode, half-grid parity, and k-space metadata cases raised in review.

## Motivation

The previous `compute_ground_state_occupation` formula was an independent source of truth. On the half-integer fermionic grid used by the ED ground-state sector, it reversed the occupation profile relative to the BdG convention used by the ED measurement path. For integer fermion grids, the special modes also require the target parity sector: minimizing each special mode independently can leave the reference curve outside the saved spin/parity sector. For odd fixed-parity half-grid sectors, where no special modes are present, the reference must instead contain the lowest generic quasiparticle.

This PR keeps the older plotting API names, but makes their physical content follow the same convention as the ED and TN mode-observable code. Result files now store the reference sector needed by the plotting scripts, and the plotting loader uses that sector only when it also knows the corresponding spin boundary condition.

Addresses #61.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `julia --project=. test/test_mode_analysis.jl` passed: 139 tests.
- `julia --project=. test/test_cooling_interface.jl` passed: 104 tests.
- `julia --project=. test/test_plot_mode_cooling.jl` passed: 61 tests.
- `julia --project=. test/test_plot_kspace_examples.jl` passed: 1 test.
- `julia --project=. test/runtests.jl` passed: 646 tests.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes ground-state reference physics used in plots and ED/plot parity alignment; risk is mitigated by extensive tests but affects how users interpret k-space cooling curves against references.
> 
> **Overview**
> Plotting and ED k-space paths now share **`mode_analysis.jl`** as the physical source of truth instead of standalone dispersion formulas.
> 
> **`dispersion.jl`** wraps **`mode_energy_Jh`** and Bogoliubov-based ground-state occupations. Sector-aware references use **`spin_bc`** and stored **`gF`**: special modes **`k=0, N/2`** are chosen to match fermion parity, and odd half-integer grids without special modes put a single lowest-energy quasiparticle in the reference curve. Without sector metadata, behavior falls back to the old per-mode special-mode rule.
> 
> **ED outputs** persist **`RESULT_MODE_GF`** (ground-state reference fermionic sector) for ordinary k-space runs, not only when **`measure_modes=true`**. K-space time series reuse that stored **`gF`** via **`_ground_state_reference_gF`**.
> 
> **Plotting** loads **`mode_gF`** from HDF5, resolves spin BC from **`bc`** or **`ham_params_bc`**, and ignores **`mode_gF`** when BC is open/unknown. Evolution scripts pass **`N`**, **`spin_bc`**, and **`gF`** into the occupation helper so reference curves match simulation data.
> 
> Regression tests cover canonical energies/occupations, parity sectors, and result metadata.
>

author: pointpu
body:
## Wave T — timestamp truncate-to-seconds conformance

Bugfix (Round-5, relates #122). Several handlers built proto-response timestamps via `timestamppb.New(t)` **without** `.Truncate(time.Second)`, leaking the DB's microsecond precision. The Kachō api-conventions rule states: *"Timestamps: в proto-ответе truncate до секунд (`CreatedAt.Truncate(time.Second)`); БД хранит микросекунды."* Every offending response timestamp is now routed through the canonical helper `internal/apps/kacho/shared/proto.go` → `shared.TimestampProto(t)` (which does `timestamppb.New(t.Truncate(time.Second))`).

### Sites fixed

**P1 — real microsecond leaks (service did NOT pre-truncate):**
- `internal/handler/mapping.go` — `operationToProto` `CreatedAt` + `ModifiedAt`
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/sa_keys/usecases.go` — `saClientToProto` `CreatedAt`, `ExpiresAt`, `LastUsedAt`
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/internal_authorize/handler.go` — `GetFGAStoreInfo` `ModelCreatedAt`
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/internal_iam/force_logout.go` — `GetJWKSStatus` `CurrentCreatedAt`
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/session_revocations/handler.go` — `toProto` `RevokedAt`/`TtlExpiresAt` + `IsRevoked` `RevokedAt`

**P2 — already pre-truncated upstream; routed through the helper for uniformity / defense-in-depth:**
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/authorize/handler.go` — `Check`/`BatchCheck`/`WhoAmI` `CheckedAt`
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/conditions/handler.go` — `Evaluate` `EvaluatedAt` + `ConditionToProto` `CreatedAt`
- `internal/apps/kacho/api/internal_authorize/handler.go` — `ReloadModel` `ReloadedAt` (simplified; already truncated inline — no behavior change)

Repo-wide grep for `timestamppb.New(` confirms every other proto-response site already truncates (`.Truncate(1_000_000_000)` = `time.Second` in `dto/toproto/*` and `cluster/handler.go`, or `.Truncate(time.Second)` in the helpers). No extra leaking sites found. Request-passthrough (`ttl` in session_revocations Revoke) and the audit `timestamppb.Now()` in sa_keys are intentionally untouched.

### TDD — RED → GREEN (strict, ban #12)

Failing tests written and run FIRST, confirming sub-second leaked, then fixed → GREEN:

| Test | RED (before) | GREEN (after) |
|---|---|---|
| `handler.TestOperationToProto_TruncatesTimestampsToSeconds` | `CreatedAt sub-second leaked: nanos=123456789` | pass |
| `sa_keys.TestSAClientToProto_TruncatesTimestampsToSeconds` | `CreatedAt sub-second leaked: nanos=123456789` | pass |
| `session_revocations.TestToProto_TruncatesTimestampsToSeconds` | `RevokedAt sub-second leaked, was 123456789` | pass |
| `session_revocations.TestIsRevoked_TruncatesRevokedAtToSeconds` | `RevokedAt sub-second leaked in IsRevoked, was 123456789` | pass |
| `conditions.TestConditionToProto_TruncatesCreatedAtToSeconds` | `CreatedAt sub-second leaked: nanos=123456789` | pass |
| `internal_iam.TestGetJWKSStatus_TruncatesCurrentCreatedAtToSeconds` | `CurrentCreatedAt sub-second leaked, was 123456789` | pass |
| `internal_authorize.TestGetFGAStoreInfo_TruncatesModelCreatedAtToSeconds` | `ModelCreatedAt sub-second leaked, was 123456789` | pass |

Plus a P2 conformance regression guard added to the existing `authorize.TestHandler_Check_AllowedHappyPath` (asserts `CheckedAt.Nanosecond()==0`). The conditions `Evaluate` and authorize `Check`/`WhoAmI` `CheckedAt` are pre-truncated in the service, so a handler-level RED isn't achievable there; the helper-routing is a uniformity change and `ConditionToProto`/`saClientToProto`/`operationToProto`/`toProto` cover the genuinely-leaking mapping paths.

### Verification (local)
- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `gofmt -l <changed files>` — empty
- `go test -short ./...` — 31 packages ok, 0 fail
- `gosec -severity high` on changed packages — 0 findings

### Newman
Not required for a precision/conformance fix: the change is sub-second timestamp precision, which is not asserted by any black-box Newman case (no observable behavior change beyond dropping fractional seconds).

author: pon4ik7
body:
## Problem

Closing an incident did not render in chat — neither via the **Close** button nor the `/incident close` command — even though the incident was correctly closed in the database. The bot logged:

```
telegram: Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unclosed start tag at byte offset 133 (400)
```

## Root cause

`response.IncidentClosed` is sent with `telebot.ModeHTML`. For an incident closed within a minute, `formatDuration` returns `"<1m"`. The raw `<` is interpreted by Telegram as the start of an HTML tag, so the whole message is rejected with HTTP 400. Because both close paths send this summary, neither renders the close. In the button path the send error also propagates up and skips the card edit, so the card stays `ACTIVE`.

## Fix

Escape the duration value before embedding it in the HTML message, the same way `Title` and other dynamic fields are already escaped. `formatDuration` itself is unchanged (still returns `"<1m"`), so its unit test stays valid.

## Tests

- `TestIncidentClosedSubMinuteIsHTMLSafe` — renders a sub-minute close and asserts the output contains `<1m` and no raw `<1m`.

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, and `go test ./...` all pass. Verified locally by rebuilding the stack.

Question shape: "which earns more cash, rounds 20-40 or 40-60?" — ranks the total cash of **two or
more** round ranges. The §7.5 comparison member of the BUG-0009 "grounded values, wrong assembly"
class: each per-round figure is grounded, but a model can mis-state *which range earns more / by how
much*, and the value-only faithfulness guard can't catch a mis-ranking. Fully deterministic ⇒ ships
under Q-0048 (no prod-check), like the sibling cost builders.

- `btd6_data_service.compare_round_ranges(ranges, *, roundset="default")` — prices each inclusive
  range once via the existing `round_cash` (the same owner the round-cash workflow uses, so per-round
  figures never drift), dedups normalized ranges, ranks **descending**, fails closed (<2 distinct
  priceable ranges), ABR-aware.
- `btd6_context_service.deterministic_round_range_comparison_reply` — fires on an earning noun
  (`cash`/`money`/`income`/`earn`) + a comparison signal (`more`/`vs`/`or`/`compare`…) + **≥2** parsed
  round ranges (a round token required before each range's first anchor, so crosspath codes like
  `5-0-0` are never mis-read as ranges); ABR cue → the ABR round set. Appended to the
  `deterministic_btd6_list_reply` dispatcher.
- Non-overlap with the single-range round-cash workflow is structural: this floor requires ≥2 ranges
  **and** short-circuits before that workflow ever runs.

## Slice 2 — floor-builder exclusivity invariant (promotes the #950 Q-0089 idea)

The dispatcher now fans out to **6** narrow builders; their non-overlap was argued in prose. Extracted
the builder tuple to a module-level `_BTD6_LIST_BUILDERS` (behaviour identical) and added
`tests/unit/invariants/test_btd6_floor_builder_exclusivity.py` — runs **every** builder against a
curated corpus and asserts **exactly one** fires per should-fire phrase (the expected one, and the
dispatcher serves it) and **zero** on should-defer phrases; a coverage test fails if a builder is
added without a corpus phrase. Makes the mutual-exclusion contract executable.

## Checks

`check_quality --full` GREEN (**10022 passed**, +36 new); `check_architecture --mode strict` 0
errors; mypy clean. De-staled the §7.5 plan + current-state ledger (ratchet held at 20 by archiving
#905).

## Status

Born-red card flipped `complete`. Self-merge candidate on green (Q-0113) — contained, additive,
deterministic, fails closed, reuses a proven seam (same risk class as #924/#926/#946/#950).

Greptile Summary

 This PR introduces structured, retryable cleanup failure handling for worker teardown across `stop_worker`, `notify(completed)`, and `notify(split_request)`. Failed cleanups are made visible as blocked tasks via a tamper-resistant, base64-encoded JSON marker embedded in the task body, separate from the free-form `reason` field. - **Cleanup marker system**: Embeds a `` HTML comment in the task body during atomic status transitions, decoded by `cleanupIntentFromTask` to drive retry routing in `stop_worker`, `notify`, and `split_task`. - **Three retryable paths**: `stop_worker` resumes any pending intent; `notify(split_request)` and `split_task` each have a fast-path that skips child-task creation on retry; the rollback in `notify(split_request)` now includes `body`. - **Regression coverage**: New tests cover stop_worker cleanup failure, spoofed cleanup reasons, notify(completed) and notify(split_request) cleanup failures, and stop_worker-as-retry finalizer.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — all three cleanup paths handle failure atomically and the body-marker approach correctly survives concurrent retries and update_task calls. The ledger mutex ensures the updater callback is called exactly once, making closure-variable mutation in handleStopWorker safe. Previously flagged rollback-missing-body and stale-preflight issues are both resolved in this version. All three cleanup intents are correctly finalized by finishPendingCleanup. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | server/internal/mcp/handlers.go | Core cleanup machinery added: workerCleanupOps abstraction, cleanupPendingMarker embed/strip helpers, and markCleanupPending/finishPendingCleanup lifecycle; previously flagged rollback-missing-body and stale-preflight issues are resolved. | | server/internal/mcp/handlers_test.go | Adds four targeted regression tests for cleanup failure visibility and retry paths, plus a successfulCleanupOps() helper used across existing tests. |

The atomic update immediately before `AddAll` wrote `bodyWithCleanupPending(…, cleanupIntentSplitRequest, reason)` into the body, and that marker survives the rollback. The task goes back to `"in_progress"` with a `split_request` cleanup marker still embedded in its body. When the worker retries `notify(split_request)`, `cleanupIntentFromTask` finds the stale marker and immediately enters the cleanup retry path, killing the still-running worker's tmux window and worktree. `finishPendingCleanup` then fails because the task is `"in_progress"` rather than `"blocked"`, leaving the task permanently stuck — worker dead, status never advancing. author: agtilden
body:
## Summary

Makes the controller device a **selectable Play-to target** ("This device") instead of scattering "play here" buttons through the menus and results. Picking **This device** in the Play-to dropdown routes now-playing, the queue, transport, and volume to an in-browser `<audio>` player; every existing play affordance (Play all / Play next / a track's play / the queue) just works against it.

It's an **independent** renderer (a browser can't join a Sonos group). Switching the dropdown to a Sonos zone behaves exactly as before and **does not stop** the device audio — you can play on the device and control a Sonos zone at the same time. The dropdown shows a playing indicator on "This device" so you can see it's still going.

## What's included
- **`localPlayer.tsx`** — `LocalPlayerProvider` / `useLocalPlayer()` exposes a full target API (now-playing, queue, active index, position/duration, volume, transport, enqueue) backing an `<audio>` engine + MediaSession (lock-screen controls).
- **`App.tsx`** — a synthetic `This device` `GroupOption` in both Play-to dropdowns; in device mode the now-playing card, queue, transport, and volume bind to the local player, and enqueue actions route to it. **Sonos-only controls are hidden in device mode**: repeat/shuffle/crossfade/sleep, the multi-zone room-volume popover, and save-queue.
- **`GroupDropdown` / `groupPalette`** — the device option renders with a phone icon (no color chip) and is excluded from the group editor.
- Plays `/api/stream/<sourceId>/<trackId>` **same-origin**; no bridge/protocol changes.

## Notes / scope
- The `LibraryView` "Play to" picker doesn't yet list the device target (its own dropdown is Sonos-only) — a small follow-up if wanted.
- Not synchronized with Sonos (by design).

## Test plan
- `apps/web` builds, lints clean, component test passes (providers wrap the render).
- **Needs live verification**: pick a source, choose "This device", Play all → audio plays in the browser with the normal now-playing/queue/transport/volume; switch to a Sonos zone and confirm the device keeps playing and the dropdown shows its indicator; mobile lock-screen shows controls.

body:
## 🐛 症状
foreground 自律起動（ArcSphere3D 等）で supervisor が **「🚀 start」をログした直後に何も起動せず凍結**。画面は tail -f が残るだけで進まない。

- 📄 state.json は `status:"running"` / `last_reason:""` のまま固まる
- 🚫 cron-launcher へ到達した形跡（headless 起動ログ）が無い
- ❌ claude の出力・エラーも一切無し（＝セッション起動前に死亡）

## 🔍 根本原因
`sup__throttle_apply`（PR-C の throttle 配線で追加）が `printf '%s %s'` と **末尾改行なし**で出力していた。これを `sup__loop` の

```bash
read -r _dcap _scap < <(sup__throttle_apply ...)
```

で受けると、`read` は改行に出会わず **EOF を直撃 → 代入は成功するが終了ステータス 1** を返す。`autonomy.sh __run` の `set -euo pipefail` 配下ではこの status 1 が `sup__loop` を**初回ループで即死**させ、cron-launcher 呼び出し前に supervisor プロセスごと落ちていた。

再現（最小）:
```bash
set -euo pipefail; read -r a b < <(printf '%s %s' 480 300); echo done
# → "done" は出力されず exit 1
```

## 🛠️ 修正（二層）
1. **根本**: `sup__throttle_apply` の printf に `\n` を付与（呼び出し側 read を正常に改行終端）
2. **防御**: read 行に `|| true` を付与し、将来同型の EOF status1 でも supervisor を落とさない

## ✅ 回帰テスト
bats の `run` は対象関数へ `set -e` を**伝播しない**ため、既存 `run sup__loop` テストは本バグを取りこぼしていた。本番と同一の `set -euo pipefail` 環境を明示再現する回帰テストを追加:

- 🎯 cron-launcher 到達の決定的証拠（`sessmin` ファイル生成）を検証
- 🎯 終端 status（`daily-cap`）に到達＝running 凍結でないことを検証

## 🧪 検証
- ✅ `npm test`（node 38 + bats 397、新テスト 362 含む）全緑・失敗 0
- ✅ `npm run lint`（shellcheck -S error）無警告

## 影響範囲
- 認証・認可・DB スキーマ・本番デプロイ **非該当**（supervisor の起動信頼性バグ修正のみ）

author: billdenney
body:
## Summary

Builds on PR #57 (heartbeat write-back), PR #59 (three-layer
heartbeat), and the 2026-06-13 audit fix (`start_new_session=True`
+ process-group signalling — commit 244aff4). Those landed Bugs
1-4 of the 2026-06 zombie-consolidated triage; this PR closes the
remaining two narrow paths so a power outage or cap-kill leaves
zero stranded subprocesses.

**Coordination note** — the two prior task IDs (`task_beafc943`,
`task_bf03e163`) created the local branches
`fix/three-layer-heartbeat` (already merged as PR #59) and
`fix/terminate-uses-process-group` (an empty label at the same
SHA as `main`, no commits ever pushed). That work was actually
landed via the 2026-06-13 audit MR. I started fresh on
`fix/zombie-consolidated` off `origin/main` per the prompt's
fallback guidance. The empty `fix/terminate-uses-process-group`
branch is safe to delete locally.

## What this PR adds

### `_terminate` post-kill verify (`runner/dispatcher.py`)

After the SIGTERM → 5s wait → SIGKILL escalation we now run a
second `process.wait(timeout=2)` and log ERROR if the subprocess
still has not reaped. The function returns either way so the
dispatcher's drain block keeps its own final wait. Same
polling-based shape applied to `_terminate_by_pid` for the
adopted-worker path.

Why: a SIGKILL'd process in `TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE` (D-state)
silently returned and the dispatcher proceeded to finalize —
telling the supervisor the cap-kill worked when it had not.

### Supervisor-side post-kill pid sanity check (`runner/orchestrator.py`)

`_reap_finished` now reads the just-written run record's pid and
probes `os.kill(pid, 0)`. If the pid is still alive the slot is
**held** (not freed), a one-shot `subprocess_leak_detected`
event + `critical`-level notification fire, and an ERROR log
names the leak. Re-checks on subsequent ticks stay silent
(deduped via `DispatchSlot.subprocess_leak_notified_at`) until
the kernel finally releases the pid, at which point the slot
frees normally and the queue can resume dispatching to that
account.

Defence in depth: catches any future code path that forgets to
kill, or any kernel state the dispatcher's SIGKILL escalation
cannot break.

### Schema: `RunRecord.pid`

New optional `int | None = None` field carrying the OS pid of the
subprocess each run spawned. Survives dispatch finalization
(unlike `TaskState.pid`, which is cleared) so the orchestrator's
post-tick probe has something to consult. Defaults to None →
state YAMLs from prior releases round-trip unchanged and the
post-tick reap silently skips the probe.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` — 1414 passed (baseline 1402 + 12 new)
- [x] `ruff check src/ tests/` — clean
- [x] `ruff format --check src/ tests/` — clean
- [x] `mypy src/` — clean
- [x] `test_dispatcher_terminate.py` — new `_FakeProcessVerify`
      asserts wait ordering `[5, 2]` and the D-state ERROR log
- [x] `test_dispatcher_linux_user.py` — pid wired through to the
      RunRecord (`outcome.run_record.pid == 4242`)
- [x] `test_orchestrator_helpers.py` — five new cases: alive-pid
      holds the slot + fires both callbacks; dead-pid frees;
      legacy run records (pid=None) free; already-notified leaks
      re-check silently; leak that finally clears frees the slot
- [x] `test_schema.py` — `RunRecord.pid` defaults to None,
      accepts a positive int, rejects 0
- [ ] Manual: misbehaving fixture task with
      `max_duration_s_per_task=10` that ignores SIGTERM; expect
      `_terminate` to ERROR-log the leak, orchestrator to hold
      the slot, slot to free once operator SIGKILLs the
      subprocess. (Operator-side validation — not in CI.)

## Files changed

- `src/claude_task_runner/runner/dispatcher.py` — `_terminate`
  + `_terminate_by_pid` post-kill verify; `_build_run_record`
  takes pid kwarg; owned-path passes `process.pid`,
  adopted-path passes `prior.pid`
- `src/claude_task_runner/queue/schema.py` — `RunRecord.pid`
- `src/claude_task_runner/runner/in_flight.py` —
  `DispatchSlot.subprocess_leak_notified_at`

  `notify_callback` + `event_callback`

  existing callbacks into `tick_dispatch`
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` `### Fixed` + `### Added`
- Tests as listed above

author: jamiestamp
body:
Only apply access limiting default at instantiation
Introduce a default nil value for the access_limiting enum to match how the access_limited boolean worked.

Flow:
- Instantiate a new document from its class
- Have access_limited/access_limiting set to nil
- Replace the nil value with the default set by the document's class
- Ignore any attempts to set the default where a valid value has been set

This allows `set_access_limited` to determine it should assign a default and the value set by a user will be honoured when the form is submitted and the record is first saved.

As per the old behaviour, this will only apply when the document is first created (before being persisted to the DB). It will not apply when creating a new edition on a published document. Instead a new edition will have access limiting disabled.

Model test in unit/app/models/publication_test.rb updated to mimic a newly instantiated model to replicate what would be used on the form fields.

Two follow-up fixes after the initial CLI-tools launch:

## 1. Prefix copied `curl` commands with `https://`
`curl ippollo.com` hits HTTP first and 301-redirects to HTTPS, which curl
won't follow without `-L` — so the copied commands appeared to "just
redirect." The CLI card now renders `curl https://ippollo.com/...` so every
copied command works as-is.

## 2. Add labeled `ipv4` / `ipv6` fields to `/json`
`/json` now returns `ipv4` and `ipv6` alongside `ip`. A single connection
only exposes the family you connected over, so on the apex only that family
is populated (the other is `null`) — this is a TCP/IP limit, same as
ifconfig.co. The family-pinned subdomains make each explicit:

- `https://ipv4.ippollo.com/json` → `ipv4` populated
- `https://ipv6.ippollo.com/json` → `ipv6` populated

No build/config changes; the edge function stays additive and the static
