author: poisonchihuahua
body:
## 概要

nginx リバースプロキシを追加し、Docker 構成を単一オリジン(`https://localhost`)へ集約しました。プロキシが HTTPS を終端し、`/api`・`/swagger` を backend、それ以外を frontend へ振り分け（HTTP は HTTPS へリダイレクト）、同一オリジン化により CORS が不要になり httpOnly Cookie も `SameSite=Strict` のまま安全に送受信できます。backend には `ForwardedHeaders` を追加し、`X-Forwarded-For`/`Proto` から実クライアント IP（レート制限キー）と HTTPS 判定（Cookie の `Secure` 属性）を復元、backend/frontend はホスト非公開にしてプロキシ経由のみに集約しました。証明書は起動時に自己署名を自動生成し、`proxy/setup-trusted-cert.sh`（mkcert）でブラウザ警告の出ない「信頼される証明書」へ差し替え可能です。証明書・鍵は `.gitignore` に追加し、README に Docker/TLS の手順を記載しています。

## 検証

`docker compose up --build` で全経路 200、HTTP→HTTPS リダイレクト、ログイン時の Cookie への `Secure` 付与、mkcert 証明書のシステム信頼ストア検証(`-k` 無しで成功)、backend テスト 52/52 合格を確認済みです。

author: sutanunandigrami
body:
## Summary
- `BrowserPool` (`src/endless_library/scrapers/annas_browser_pool.py`): lazy-spawn process-wide singleton holding `(Playwright, Browser)`. Recycle after 50 uses, atexit-registered shutdown, lazy patchright import so tests can inject a fake launcher.
- `AnnasArchivePatchright.resolve_cdn` now acquires from the pool instead of `with sync_playwright()`. Per-call context still created/closed locally; only the browser is reused.
- 11 new unit tests against a mock launcher.

## Why
Step 3 of 9 in the resilience/speed program. Patchright launch was the most-cited "obviously expensive" thing in the code — but measured cost is ~600ms, not the ~5s I'd estimated. Pooling still removes it from the per-call hot path and is the right infrastructure for PR #41 (parallel browser contexts).

## Aborted detour: context-pooling
I tried pooling the BrowserContext too, on the theory that cached `__ddg*` cookies would let later resolves skip the warmup goto entirely (~10s saved per cache-miss book). Bench reality: success rate dropped from 100% to 80% (book 3 of 5 came back with "no partner URL found"). Best theory: annas reads enough session signals off the shared context that repeated slow_download requests aren't served the inline partner URL. **Reverted to browser-only pooling.** Documented in the commit body.

## Measured (5-book in-container bench)

| | mean | p50 | p95 | min | success |
|--|--|--|--|--|--|
| Baseline (PR #37) | 32116 ms | 34096 | 61090 | 8477 | 5/5 |
| PR #38 hot cache | 24861 ms | 26476 | 44739 | 1512 | 5/5 |
| **PR #39 (this)** | **18320 ms** | **1784** | 61350 | 1292 | **5/5** |

### Micro-bench (pool spawn vs reuse, no annas hit)
```
first acquire (spawn):  596 ms
second acquire (reuse):   0 ms
   -> ~600 ms saved per cache-miss resolve
```

## Honest caveat
The 32 → 18 ms wallclock drop is **dominated by annas-side variance, not by the pool**: on the bench run for this PR, 3 of 5 books served the partner URL inline (cookie-replay HIT), versus 1 of 5 on PR #38's bench. Same code, same fixture, different day — that's the natural variance from a 5-book sample against a free-tier resource.

The pool itself contributes only the ~600 ms savings per cache-miss — a real but small fraction of the observable change. The architecture is still load-bearing for PR #41.

- [x] `ruff format --check` — passed
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_annas_browser_pool.py` — 11/11 passed
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_annas_ddg_cookies.py` — 17/17 passed
- [x] In-container bench — 5/5 success, mean 18.3s

A user who never discovers reordering keeps the default, so the default *is* the designed layout. MAIA is a primary interaction surface, not just a tool; it belongs near the top.

## How
`DEFAULT_PERSONAL_NAV_ORDER` is used **only when the person hasn't reordered** (empty localStorage). Their saved order always wins; fully reorderable from the default. Slugs not listed fall back to definition order at the end.

## Boundary
Nav only — **no schema, no API**; floor / four questions / pulse untouched. This is the agreed "tiny follow-up," after which navigation goes quiet and it's back to observation.

## Classification
- [x] **Class C — Routine Improvement**

author: klowe001
body:
**This is the commit that missed the #257 merge.** #257 merged the Bun-toolchain removal (which fixed `npm: not found`), but closed before this `.npmrc` was pushed — so `main-agent` has no `.npmrc` and the deploy now fails at the install step:

```
--> npm install
npm error code ERESOLVE
npm error peerOptional esbuild@"^0.27.0 || ^0.28.0" from vite@8.0.16
npm error Found: esbuild@0.25.11
```

## Why

With Bun removed, Replit's install phase runs `npm install`, which **re-resolves** peers and chokes on Vite 8's optional `esbuild ^0.27||^0.28` peer vs the `0.25.x` that tsx/others pull. (`npm ci` — our build command — installs from the lockfile and doesn't re-resolve, but Replit's `npm install` runs first.)

## Fix

`.npmrc` with `legacy-peer-deps=true`, so every npm invocation (Replit's `npm install` included) tolerates the optional-peer mismatch — matching how the lockfile was generated.

## Verified locally
- `npm install` with `.npmrc` → resolves, no ERESOLVE ✓
- `npm ci` exits 0; full `npm run build` passes ✓

After merge: **redeploy.**

body:
Fixes #126.

The reusable workflow's `integration-lint` job is hardcoded to `matrix: language: [python]`, gated on `contains(…, 'python')`, and **drops `--config`**. So a consumer's **TypeScript** (`no-first-party-mock`, #43/#75) and **Rust** (`no-first-party-double`, #44) integration tests go unchecked, and a #102 waiver in a non-default config path is ignored. The `detect` step also doesn't scan Rust today.

## Plan (red → green, per `AGENTS.md`)

This PR opens with the **red commit only** — self-test fixtures and jobs, no workflow logic change yet — so CI shows the gap before the fix lands.

### On red/green for this change

Adding the TS/Rust arms is *additive* (like #58, which wired the Python arm with no red test): a clean `uses:` job can't prove an additive check runs, and a violating `uses:` job can't stay green afterward. But the current job also **omits `--config`**, so it ignores the consumer's `config` input — a real bug that *is* red→green testable via Python (the already-wired arm). That's the witnessed red:

- **`integration-lint-config-waiver`** (`uses:`) — a clean Python suite whose integration test trips `no-constant-patch`, lifted by a `[[python.exempt]]` entry in a *non-default* config path (#102). The `uses:` call **fails on today's workflow** (the job doesn't forward `--config`, so the waiver is ignored) and passes once it does.

The new arms are covered by clean/violating fixtures:

- **`integration-lint-rust`** (`uses:`) — a clean Rust crate must pass the reusable workflow once the rust arm is wired, with rust staying *out* of the coverage matrix it doesn't support. (Green no-op against today's workflow.)
- **`integration-lint-new-arms-trip`** — drives the published command directly (a `uses:` call can't assert a failure, as the existing `packaging-red`/`below-floor` jobs do) to assert the non-zero exit on a rust `#[double]` and a typescript first-party `vi.mock`, plus a clean pass.

Expected on this commit: the **Testing Conventions (self-test)** run goes red on `integration-lint-config-waiver` and stays green everywhere else.

## Then (green commit, once red is witnessed on CI)

- `detect`: emit a second output `integration_lint_languages` that also covers Rust (`Cargo.toml` / `*.rs`), kept separate so the coverage/colocated matrix (no rust arm) is unchanged.
- `integration-lint`: fan out over `integration_lint_languages` (python, typescript, rust) and forward `--config`.
- Workflow header comment + `docs/guide/ci.md`. (No CHANGELOG/MIGRATIONS — workflow-only.)

author: dutiona
body:
## What

Adds `.claude/skills/release-checklist/SKILL.md` (#553) — the in-repo, execute-with-gates release procedure that promotes a built `memory-engine` into its durable home `~/.local/opt/memory-engine/{bin,data}` (the only artifacts the harness consumes — never a `target/` dev build).

## The 5 gated steps (STOP on any failure)

1. **Build** optimized `memory-engine-cli` + `memory-engine-mcp` (release, never debug).
2. **Quality gate** (blocks promote): `cargo test --workspace` (incl. migration test) + `+nightly fmt --check` + `clippy --workspace --all-targets` + version-bump check.
3. **Back up** the live DB → timestamped `data/backups/` (the gate's own copy, before any mutation).
4. **Migrate + verify** — *irreversible, needs explicit "go"*: `migrate --check` dry-run → `migrate` → `schema` verify (`schema_version == CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, exit 0). **On failure → restore backup + ABORT** (old binaries keep serving the old, intact DB).
5. **Promote** — *irreversible, needs explicit "go"*: atomic `mv` into `bin/` + `RELEASE` manifest (version, git sha, schema_version, date) + `stats` smoke.

Migration is ordered **before** promoting the new binaries, so the harness never starts a new binary against an un-migrated DB. Uses the `migrate`/`schema` CLI from #552.

A `.gitignore` exception (`.claude/*` + `!.claude/skills/`) tracks in-repo skills while keeping local Claude config ignored.

## Verification

This is an operational doc (no code/tests). The CLI commands it invokes (`migrate`/`migrate --check`/`schema`/`stats`, `--format` as a global flag) match the `#552` CLI surface. The release gate is intended to be exercised at first install (Stream-B P3).

Closes #553.

(The 75→120 job-cap probe was reverted — it proved the cap was never the cause.)
- **Quarantined the post-bundle-stall specs** (preview-runtime / runtime / preview-shadcn, 6) → **#1242**.

## Part 2 — reality-check the 28 surfaced failures (built + ran locally, 1 worker)
**Stale tests — fixed (23):** Model-v2 node ids `module:`→`subdomain:` (11) + deployable multi-select testid `modules`→`contexts`; LikeC4 "Generated" explorer split; example fixtures renamed/removed (`/Acme/` disambiguation ×4; deleted "Fullstack .NET (Banking)" re-pointed ×4); `__loomSetSource` seam for the enum-picker spec; workspace-history mobile ready-wait.

- **#161** — palette "add workflow" emitted `workflow X() { }` (workflows take no `()`), so the parse-guarded add was silently dropped. Removed the `()`.

author: miyasaki09
body:
## Voir d'un coup d'œil ce qu'on peut cuisiner avec le stock

Chaque déjeuner/dîner du planning affiche une **pastille** indiquant si on a tout en stock pour le faire :

| Pastille | Sens |
|---|---|
| 🟢 ✓ | Tout en stock |
| 🟠 ~ (n/m) | Partiel — il manque des ingrédients |
| 🔴 ✕ | Rien en stock |
| ⚪ ? | Recette non détaillée (impossible à évaluer) |

Jamais la couleur seule : glyphe + `aria-label` + infobulle listant les ingrédients manquants (accessibilité WCAG 1.4.1).

### Backend — déterministe, **zéro appel IA**
- **`lib/stockCoverage.js`** (pur, 24 tests) : agrégation du stock par canonique (conversion d'unités via `convertWithMeta`), matching de fiche par nom, couverture avec **tolérance 15 %** (règle métier « faisable si manque < 15 % »). Les **staples** (épices, huiles, sucre, sel, poivre, eau) n'influencent pas la couleur.
- **`GET /api/planning/[importId]/stock-coverage`** : pour chaque plat, résout les ingrédients — batch (texte) → fiche générée liée (`generated_recipe_ingredients`) ou sa JSONB → parse de la description — puis compare au stock actuel. Dédup par signature de plat, une requête par table, résultat mappé par `meal.id`.

### Frontend
- **`StockDot`** (composant accessible) + **`useStockCoverage`** (hook)
- **WeekGrid** : pastille par cellule, **toggle Afficher/Masquer**, légende, résumé « N prêts · N partiels »
- **WeeklyPlanView** et **TodayMeals** : pastille également

### Limite assumée (documentée)
Couverture évaluée **indépendamment par recette** : le stock n'est pas réservé d'un repas à l'autre de la semaine (deux repas demandant le même ingrédient le voient chacun comme disponible). Une évolution future pourrait faire une allocation cumulative sur la semaine.

Build ✅ · 144 tests ✅

- Fixes correctness gaps found by code review: `lognormal` systematics now fail loudly instead of silently falling back to `absolute`; the prior-correlation PD-regularization now warns only on genuine negative eigenvalues.
- Adds a quadratic fast-path + Newton polish to the minimizer (`Combiner._minimize`): when the chi2 is an exact quadratic form (symmetric responses, all-absolute, no Pearson), the minimum is reached via a single linear solve instead of iterative L-BFGS-B; the general path keeps L-BFGS-B with a guarded Newton-correction polish on top. Fuses `fun`/`jac` into one `jax.value_and_grad` dispatch. `corrV2` wall-clock: ~84s -> ~22-27s.
- Adds `ndf`/`chi2_per_ndf`/`p_value` goodness-of-fit fields to `CombinationResult`, printed as a new `[goodness of fit]` section.
- Adds `--no-impacts`/`--impacts-only` CLI flags to skip or narrow the (often dominant-cost) uncertainty-impact computation.
- Implements the correlation scan (`-s` in the original C++ tool) as `Combiner.scan_correlations()` / CLI `--scan`, writing both text and structured (`--export`) output.
- Adds `--verbose`, printing per-phase timing checkpoints (parse, setup+prior, chi2 build, minimize, post-fit, impacts, total) to stderr to help users decide when the flags above are worth using.
- Documents why the Python port's output intentionally keeps `[impact table]`/`[merged impacts]`/`[covariance matrix for merged impacts]` sections that the C++ reference omits on some setups.
- Commits the reference C++ Convino setup configs (`ConvinoSetups/`) used for validation, and ignores `documentation.pdf`.

## Test plan
- [x] Full fast test suite passes (`python -m unittest test.test_correlation_scan test.test_export test.test_formatter test.test_goodness_of_fit test.test_impacts_options test.test_lognormal_unsupported test.test_minimize_nonlinear test.test_output_path test.test_pd_regularization_warning test.test_regression test.test_verbose`)
- [x] Slow suite passes (`CONVINO_SLOW_TESTS=1 python -m unittest test.test_regression`), including the `corrV2` golden, confirming no numeric regressions from the minimizer changes
- [x] CLI smoke-tested `--verbose` manually (stderr gets timing lines, stdout unaffected)

author: izagood
body:
## 문제

Windows에서 앱을 백그라운드로 돌릴 때 콘솔 창(cmd 창)이 주기적으로 떴다 꺼졌다 하며 깜빡인다.

## 원인

GUI 앱이 `std::process::Command`로 콘솔 자식 프로세스(`git`, `claude` CLI)를 spawn할 때 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` 플래그가 없으면 Windows에서 콘솔 창이 잠깐 뜬다.

- `src-tauri/src/main.rs`의 `windows_subsystem = "windows"`는 **앱 자신의 창**에만 적용되고, 자식 프로세스에는 영향이 없다.
- `SyncBar.tsx`의 `STATUS_POLL_MS = 15_000`으로 **15초마다** git status를 폴링하고, auto-sync 타이머까지 더해져 깜빡임이 반복된다.
- macOS/Linux엔 콘솔 창 개념이 없어 Windows 전용 증상이다.

## 수정

spawn 직전 `Command`에 `creation_flags(0x0800_0000)`(`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`)을 거는 플랫폼 전용 헬퍼 `suppress_console_window`를 추가하고, 생산 경로의 모든 spawn에 적용:

- `crates/synapse-core/src/git.rs` — `run_command`(모든 git 호출 funnel), `git_available`
- `src-tauri/src/agent.rs` — claude CLI spawn

다른 OS에선 no-op. 테스트 코드(`#[cfg(test)]`)의 spawn은 사용자 영향이 없어 제외했다.

## 테스트 / 검증

- 이 변경은 Windows 콘솔 창 억제라는 **플랫폼 전용 네이티브 글루**라 Linux CI 러너에서 의미 있는 단위 테스트가 불가능하다 (CLAUDE.md 컨벤션에 따라 사유 명시).
- 기존 `run_command_passes_output_within_timeout` 테스트가 `run_command`(→ `suppress_console_window` no-op) 경로를 이미 검증하므로 명령 실행이 깨지지 않음은 보장된다.
- `cargo fmt --check` 로컬 통과 (synapse-core, src-tauri). cargo test/clippy는 C 컴파일러 부재로 로컬 실행 불가 → CI에 위임.
- **수동 검증 방법**: Windows에서 빌드 후 auto-sync를 켠 워크스페이스로 앱 실행 → 15초마다 콘솔 창이 더 이상 깜빡이지 않는지 확인.

author: andy-grigg
body:
The upgrade to pytest 9.1 seems to have broken CI. Specifically, pytest seems to now evaluate command line arguments before setting the test path from a pyproject.toml file.

As a result, it parses the `--mi-version` custom argument before loading the test directory, and so the custom argument hasn't been registered.

The most expedient fix is to provide the path exactly. I can't see anything in the changelog either confirming that this an expected change or even changing something in a similar area which could indicate this is a side effect. Either way, the fact that it worked was maybe accidental anyway - it's not unreasonable that pytest might check args before checking config.

author: skatti97
body:
Adds 7 new KPIs to the `QOE_AGGREGATE` event and bumps `qoeAggregateVersion` to `1.1.0` for cross-platform parity with video-agent-android.

| KPI | Type | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| `avgDownloadRate` | Long (bps) | Mean network download throughput across distinct samples |
| `minDownloadRate` | Long (bps) | Lowest download throughput observed (omitted when no sample) |
| `maxDownloadRate` | Long (bps) | Highest download throughput observed (omitted when no sample) |
| `totalSwitchUps` | Long | Count of CONTENT_RENDITION_CHANGE events where quality went up |
| `totalSwitchDowns` | Long | Count of CONTENT_RENDITION_CHANGE events where quality went down |
| `totalPauseTime` | Long (ms) | Total time the user spent paused this session |
| `totalRenditions` | Long | Distinct video renditions (W×H pairs) observed this session |


## How it's wired

All 7 KPIs live entirely on `NRQoEAggregator` — no new tracker-side state. The aggregator observes the assembled attribute dict that already flows through `processAction:`, mirroring the existing pattern for totalRebufferingTime.

**Three design choices worth knowing:**

1. **avgDownloadRate skips consecutive duplicate samples.** AVPlayer's `accessLog.events.lastObject` returns the same entry between real network events, so naïve every-event observation would bias the mean toward whichever rate was sticky during the longest idle window. The aggregator only accumulates on change — true mean over distinct download events.

2. **totalPauseTime consumes `timeSincePaused` from the existing timeSince table** instead of running its own clock. Mid-pause harvest still reports correctly via an open-segment snapshot in generateAggregateAttributes — written to a local var, never back into `self.totalPauseTime`, so the matching RESUME doesn't double-count.

3. **totalRenditions keys on width × height, not bitrate.** Pixel-area keying is robust to streams that label distinct resolution variants with the same bitrate. Initial rendition is seeded at CONTENT_START because `NRTrackerAVPlayer.checkRenditionChange` (lines 351-354) silently stamps the first observation without firing CONTENT_RENDITION_CHANGE.

**Auto-wired:**
- Dirty check iterates NRVAAllKPIKeys(), so adding entries there picks up new KPIs for duplicate suppression with zero comparator changes.
- buildQoeEvent does addEntriesFromDictionary, so any new KPI reaches the wire automatically.
- [aggregator reset] is already called on sendEnd, so per-view reset works for free.


## Test plan

- [x] Unit: 61/61 passing (was 31; +30 new)
- [x] Spec-required cases for totalPauseTime: closed-only, mid-pause snapshot, no-double-count after resume
- [x] Distinct-count / dedup / seed-from-start / invalid-rejected for totalRenditions
- [x] Consecutive-duplicate skip + non-consecutive accept for avgDownloadRate
- [x] Reset coverage — every new accumulator clears on [aggregator reset]
- [x] New keys present in NRVA_DEBUG_LOG at harvest time
- [x] Manual: launch Examples/iOS/SimplePlayerWithAds, pause + resume + change quality, confirm all 7 KPIs surface in the QOE_AGGREGATE event
- [x] NRQL parity check against Android sample app for the same scenario

author: blahmonkey
body:
**NOTE:** The author must always **first review the PR themselves**, before requesting review from others, that means carefully having reviewed the full diff in GitHub.

## What does this PR change?

Fixes a restart-durability bug found while validating the position-recovery fix: after live fee-bearing trading, restarting the process crash-looped the Nexus instance during state recovery.

### Root cause

`CapitalController.order_fill` releases a terminal fill's working aggregate via the proportional-fee Decimal division in `TrackedOrder.remaining_total`, which can leave `working_order_notional` at a sub-ULP negative residue (observed: `-1E-27`), with a mirror `fee_reserve = +1E-27`. `CapitalState.__post_init__` rejects any negative aggregate, so `deserialize_state` raised `Malformed WAL codec payload` → `StartupError` in `_recover_state` → the instance crash-looped on boot. The residue was latent until the Praxis fee fix made `actual_fees` non-zero (at `fee_rate=0` the reserve/release netted to exactly zero).

### Fix

- **Mutation site** (`order_fill`): snap `working_order_notional`, `fee_reserve`, and `per_strategy_deployed` residues within `SUB_ULP_TOLERANCE` to zero. The `fee_reserve` snap previously handled only tiny negatives; `_adjust_strategy_deployed` now treats sub-tolerance magnitudes as zero rather than logging a false underflow (genuine underflows beyond tolerance still warn).
- **Recovery shim** (`wal_codec._decode_capital_state`): snap sub-tolerance *negative* persisted aggregates to zero before constructing `CapitalState`, so snapshots already carrying a residue boot. The domain invariant stays strict — only sub-`SUB_ULP_TOLERANCE` negatives are snapped; meaningful negatives still raise.
- `SUB_ULP_TOLERANCE` is now a single source in `capital_state` (was forked into the codec).

TD-096 records a follow-up: collapse the two-step terminal residual release in `order_fill` into one exact decrement. The shipped position-recovery fix (Praxis 0.83.0 / Nexus 0.64.0) is independent and unaffected — this bug is upstream of reconcile.

## Tests

Added codec tests asserting a sub-ULP negative residue decodes to zero and a meaningful negative still raises. `ruff` + `mypy` clean, **1,449 tests pass**. Bumps 0.64.0 → 0.65.0.

author: bedahovorka
body:
## Problem

`docker compose up --build -d` was failing after the kDisco 0.5.0 upgrade.

### Root causes

1. **BuildKit registry cache import failure** — `docker-compose.yml` contained `cache_from` entries for local-only image tags (`interlocksim:latest`, `interlocksim-text:latest`). BuildKit treated them as registry references and failed with `insufficient_scope`.

2. **Committed binary artifacts** — `docker-kdisco/` contained pre-built kDisco `.klib`, `.jar`, `.module`, and `.pom` files checked into Git. This bloats the repository and violates the project policy of keeping binary artifacts out of the codebase.

3. **Native runtime failures in fast-sim**
   - Missing `libgcc` on the Alpine runtime image caused exception-unwinding symbols to fail at startup.
   - The native binary has absolute build-tree resource roots baked in; these directories were not present in the runtime image, so `Resources.read()` could not locate `vyhybna.xml`.

## Changes

- Removed invalid `cache_from` blocks from `docker-compose.yml`.
- Deleted the entire `docker-kdisco/` directory from the repository.
- Updated `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.fast-sim` to fetch kDisco from GitHub Packages via `GITHUB_ACTOR`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` instead of copying pre-staged local artifacts.
- Added `GITHUB_ACTOR`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` build args to the `fast-sim` service in `docker-compose.yml` so the native image can authenticate to GitHub Packages.
- Added `/docker-kdisco/` to `.gitignore` and `docker-kdisco/` to `.dockerignore` to prevent accidental re-introduction.
- Removed the obsolete `docker-kdisco` seeding steps from `gradle-java21.yml` and `sonarqube.yml` GitHub Actions workflows.
- Updated the README dependency note to reference GitHub Packages only.
- Added design and implementation plan documents under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Verification

- Local `./gradlew clean build` passes.
- All GitHub Actions checks on this PR pass (`build`, `fast-sim`, `SonarQube`, `SonarCloud`).
- Docker image builds use GitHub Packages authentication via the existing `GITHUB_ACTOR`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` build args.

author: mssonicbld
body:
#### Description
Updated regex patterns `p1` and `p2` in `PcieUtil.get_pcie_device()` to use raw string literals (`r"..."`) instead of plain string literals.

#### Motivation and Context
On SONiC `20251110.35` (Debian 13 / Python 3.13), `SyntaxWarning` was emitted to stderr on every CLI invocation (`show ver`, `show ip bgp sum`, etc.) on Arista `7060X6-16PE-384C-B` devices.

**Root cause:**
- `__pycache__/pcie_common.cpython-313.pyc` was created by a root process with a restrictive umask, resulting in `0600` permissions.
- Non-root `admin` users cannot read the `0600` `.pyc` -> Python falls back to parsing `pcie_common.py` from source on every CLI invocation.
- `pcie_common.py` contains invalid escape sequences (`\w`, `\s`) in plain string regex patterns -> Python 3.13 emits `SyntaxWarning` on every parse.

Python 3.12+ warns on invalid escape sequences in plain strings; Python 3.13 raises `SyntaxWarning`; Python 3.14 will raise `SyntaxError`. Raw strings (`r"..."`) are the correct and idiomatic way to write regex patterns and eliminate the warning regardless of `.pyc` cache state or permissions.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
- Existing test suite passes: `pytest tests/pcie_common_test.py -v`
- No `DeprecationWarning` or `SyntaxWarning` emitted under Python 3.12/3.13
- No behavioral change - regex patterns are identical

Signed-off-by: Sonic Build Admin <sonicbld@microsoft.com>

body:
Refuerzo de seguridad integral del backend y frontend antes de despliegue a produccion. Cambios alineados con OWASP Top 10 y politicas internas #5, #6, #7, #9 (manejo de secretos y datos sensibles).

Cambios principales:

Secretos / repo
- BACK/.env y FRONT/.env removidos del tracking; ambos agregados a .gitignore
- Creados BACK/.env.example y FRONT/.env.example como plantillas

Autenticacion / JWT
- JwtUtil: sin valor default, exige jwt.secret de >=32 bytes; eliminado padding con ceros que reducia entropia silenciosamente. Expiracion por defecto 8h
- ApiKeyFilter: excluye /api/auth/login del filtro (la API key ya no se expone en el bundle del frontend; es solo server-to-server)
- LoginRateLimiter (nuevo): 5 intentos fallidos por IP+usuario en 15 min ->
  bloqueo de 15 min, devuelve 429 con Retry-After
- AuthController: usa el rate limiter, devuelve mensajes genericos para no permitir enumeracion de usuarios, sanitiza excepciones internas

Autorizacion / endpoints
- DetalleConteoController: @PreAuthorize en todos los endpoints; operario solo ve/modifica registros propios (idUsuario forzado desde el principal)
- MedicamentoController: protegidos GET, /bulk-status, /summary, /dashboard-stats, /search; asignar-diario valida que operario solo pida su propio bloque
- MaestraMedicamentoController: protegidos GETs publicos
- SedeConfigController: GET protegido (antes publico)
- PersonalizadoController: operario no puede crear personalizados a nombre de otros
- CycleGeneratorController: operario no puede generar bloque de otro

CORS / headers HTTP
- WebConfig: orígenes restringidos (ciclico.pharmaser.com.co, apiciclico.*,
  + localhost dev); configurable por propiedad app.cors.allowed-origins
- SecurityConfig: HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy same-origin, CSP minima default-src 'none'

Errores / informacion disclosure
- GlobalExceptionHandler: mensajes genericos al cliente, detalle solo en log (evita filtrar info de SQL/Hibernate)

SFTP / path traversal
- AutomatedImportService: valida filename remoto (sin /, \, ..), normaliza ruta y verifica que el archivo destino quede dentro del directorio de descarga

Frontend
- axiosConfig.ts: removido envio de x-api-key (era visible en el bundle); el frontend autentica solo con JWT Bearer

Documentacion
- SEGURIDAD_CHECKLIST.md: guia paso a paso para rotar credenciales en produccion, validar headers, limpiar historial git, y todo el plan post-deploy

Validacion
- mvn clean compile -DskipTests: BUILD SUCCESS (70 archivos)

author: alexander-bal
body: ## Summary The environment editor lets you scope an environment's egress with a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (Restricted mode, Allowed CIDRs, domain allowlists). But `getK8sCapabilities` hard-coded `kubernetesNetworkPolicy: true`, so on a cluster with **no NetworkPolicy enforcer installed** (e.g. GKE with the NetworkPolicy add-on off — the API server accepts `NetworkPolicy` objects but nothing enforces them) the editor still presented those controls as functional. An operator could configure a "Restricted" egress policy that silently does nothing, believing the environment was isolated. This makes the capability honest. The backend already probed for FQDN-capable providers (Cilium, GKE FQDN, AWS); it now also probes Calico's provider-exclusive `crd.projectcalico.org` group and derives an `enforced` flag. When **no** enforcer is detected, it reports `provider: "none"` and `kubernetesNetworkPolicy: false` instead of `"kubernetes"`/`true`. The editor responds to that: when `provider === "none"` it shows a **"Network policy enforcement unavailable"** alert that names the missing enforcer and states that rules would be accepted but not enforced, and it disables the Egress mode select and the Allowed CIDRs textarea (the domain controls were already gated on FQDN support). Previously those two stayed enabled regardless. This changes only the reported capability and the editor's affordances — it does not change which policy objects the runtime applies (`kubernetesNetworkPolicy` has no other consumer, and no policy builder branches on `provider`). Detection is by discoverable CRD, so a cluster running **plain GKE Dataplane V2** (which enforces standard NetworkPolicy but whose FQDN CRD is feature-gated) would report `"none"`; this is called out in a code comment with a concrete revisit path (probe the `anetd` DaemonSet) for if an environment ever runs that configuration. ---

author: h0lybyte
body:
## Problem
Fast-register still 502s for unlinked Discord users. With #12579's body logging, GoTrue now tells us why:
```
gotrue admin create failed status=403 body={"code":403,"error_code":"not_admin","msg":"User not allowed"}
```
We reach GoTrue directly (Kong wasn't the issue), but the stored `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` isn't accepted as admin — its `role` claim isn't `service_role`/`supabase_admin` (the sealed `service-key` value is wrong/mis-signed).

## Fix
Mint a short-lived (`60s`) `service_role` JWT from `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` and use it as the admin Bearer, instead of the stored key:
- GoTrue's `GOTRUE_JWT_SECRET` is the **same** value (`supabase-jwt`/`secret`) we already mint session JWTs with, so it validates.
- `service_role` ∈ `GOTRUE_JWT_ADMIN_ROLES = 'supabase_admin, service_role'` → GoTrue authorizes the admin call.
- No dependency on the broken stored service key; same in-ecosystem GoTrue admin workflow.

bump 0.1.39. axum-cryptothrone lint ✓.

Image republish (0.1.39) + the gated dbmate deploy of `20260616000000` (the username fns) for the post-create step.

author: hannsxpeter
body:
Slice 11 of the **codeaudit.md** remediation (security hardening nits, all Low).

## Resolved
- **SEC-inject-003** - open redirect: `redirectTo` was passed to `goto()` after auth without validation. Added `safeRedirectPath` (same-origin paths only; rejects `//host`, `/\host`, absolute URLs) and applied it at the login + signup sinks.
- **SEC-secrets-004** - user-feedback / user-report free-text messages bypassed PII scrubbing. They now run through `scrubString` (cards / SSNs / bearer tokens) when the project enables scrubbing; the submitter's own name/email are kept (intentional contact info). New protocol test.
- **SEC-authz-002** - `resolveActiveOrg`'s member-less-org bootstrap now resolves only for the org's creator (`createdBy === userId`), so a stale `userSettings` pointer can't resolve to an unrelated org.
- **SEC-authz-001** - corrected the stale `SveltryIdentity` comment (the active org comes from Convex `userSettings`, not the JWT; the JWT claim is a legacy fallback).

## Accepted with rationale
- **SEC-authz-003** - API tokens are a SHA-1 digest of a 256-bit random secret; security rests on entropy + preimage resistance (which SHA-1 provides), as the in-code comment documents. Upgrading needs an async-crypto + dual-verify migration for no real gain. The audit rates it "defensible".

## Verification
- `bun run check` green; full test sweep green (protocol 174 incl. new scrubString test, backend 7, sdk 8); `convex dev --once` deploys clean.

author: felipeguimares
body:
## Contexto

Iniciei a sessão para começar a **F3.2 (pipeline de ingestão)**, mas a auditoria do estado real do `develop` revelou que o roadmap e o `CLAUDE.md` estavam **dessincronizados da realidade**. Em vez de construir F3.2 sobre uma base falsa, esta PR **re-baseia a documentação da Fase 3 para refletir o que de fato está mergeado** e aplica um **guard de segurança** num caminho quebrado que já estava em produção (latente).

Decisão tomada com o time: **documentar tudo agora, sem deletar scaffolds** (exceto o guard do webhook).

## O que a auditoria encontrou

O roadmap assume **9 PRs isoladas e sequenciais** sobre um `develop` limpo. Isso **não vale mais**: merges anteriores (`iago-scosta/AI-integracao`) scaffoldaram F3.3/F3.4/F3.5 **fora de ordem e pela metade**.

| Fase | Escopo | Estado real |
|---|---|---|
| **F3.1** Infra & providers | adapters, usage.logger, /ai/health | ✅ Feito e wired |
| **F3.2** Ingestão | parsers, chunker, upload, worker | ❌ ~15% — só migration `002` + queue órfã + worker quebrado (`require('./parsers')`/`./chunker` inexistentes); sem endpoints, multer, redis; `knowledge.service.js` vazio |
| **F3.3** RAG retrieval | retriever + MMR + citações | ⚠️ ~40% — `rag/retriever.js` com SQL real filtrado por `knowledge_base_id`, mas "MMR" usa `cosineSimilarity` falso; `ai/rag.service.js` duplicado/vazio; não exposto |
| **F3.4** Agent engine | loop tool-use + tools | ❌ ~20% — `agent.engine.js` importa `context.builder`, `tool.router`, `trace.logger` **inexistentes**; não roda |
| **F3.5** Webhook wire | dispatcher ai_agent | ⚠️ wired numa mina — despachava `type==='ai_agent'` p/ o engine quebrado |

**Bônus fora do roadmap:** existe e funciona a feature **"AI Generated" (nível 2)** — geração/ajuste de fluxo por IA em `ai.service.js`. Não estava documentada. Não é o AI Agent (nível 3).

### Riscos que isso já criava
1. **Crash latente em produção** — qualquer chatbot `type==='ai_agent'` faria o webhook chamar o `agent.engine` quebrado → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → exceção no processamento de mensagem inbound daquela conexão.
2. **Endpoints `/knowledge-bases` do front dão 404** — nada montado nesse path no `routes/index.js` (nem stub).
3. **Arquivos mortos/duplicados** acumulando (`ai/rag.service.js` vazio, trio `knowledge/*` vazio, `ingestion.queue` órfão).

## O que esta PR faz

### Docs (re-alinhamento)
- **`CLAUDE.md` §3** — data atualizada; substitui "F3.1 entregue / próxima é F3.2 limpa" por um **quadro de status auditado** F3.1→F3.5; registra a feature **"AI Generated" (nível 2)**.
- **`docs/AI_AGENT_RAG_ROADMAP.md`**:
  - Aviso de realidade no topo.
  - Quadro **"Estado real auditado"** no início da §6.
  - Anotação `> Estado real (2026-06-16)` em cada fase F3.1–F3.5.
  - **Lista de limpeza (pré-F3.2)** no fim da §6 — o que deletar/refazer e em que fase.
  - Nota na §11 de que a sequência de PRs foi violada.

### Código (única mudança de comportamento)
- **`server/src/modules/webhook/webhook.service.js`** — branch `type === 'ai_agent'` envolvida em **`try/catch`**. A mensagem inbound **já é persistida antes** desse ponto; em falha do AgentEngine apenas logamos e seguimos **sem resposta automática**, em vez de estourar e derrubar o recebimento daquela conexão. Também `return await` no handoff para a rejeição ser capturada.

## O que NÃO foi mexido (de propósito)
Conforme decisão "documentar, não deletar agora": `agent.engine.js`, `rag/*`, `ai/rag.service.js` duplicado, `knowledge/*` vazios, `ingestion.queue.js` órfão. Todos listados na **Lista de limpeza** com a fase dona de cada um.

## Verificação
- `node --check server/src/modules/webhook/webhook.service.js` → OK.
- `git diff -w` confirma que o webhook só ganhou o wrapper try/catch + comentário (lógica inalterada).
- **Nenhuma query SQL nova** → sem nova superfície de tenancy.
- Sem migrations novas; `npm run migrate` / `npm run ai:ping` não afetados.

## Próximo passo
F3.2 redefinida vira o próximo `/start-fase`: limpar os scaffolds da lista + construir a ingestão de verdade (parsers, chunker, `POST /knowledge-bases/:id/documents`, multer, redis no compose, worker robusto, KB/docs CRUD).

author: ia-dev-sindireceita
body:
## What & why
Backend layer for **manual conversation assignment** to attendants (SIN-64978, child of SIN-64961 / levantamento SIN-64957). The HTMX UI is the sibling child, blocked on this. No handlers/templates here.

`Closes SIN-64978`

## Delivered
1. **`AssignConversation` use case** (`internal/inbox/usecase/assign_conversation.go`) — loads the conversation, validates invariants, calls `Conversation.AssignTo`, persists via `AssignmentRepository.AppendHistory`. `reason=manual` on first attribution, `reason=reassign` when a lead already exists. Re-assigning to the current lead is a typed no-op (`ErrAlreadyAssigned`) — no duplicate history row.
2. **`AssignableAttendantRepository` port** (`internal/inbox/port_attendants.go`) + postgres adapter — lists tenant users eligible to receive a conversation (`role IN (tenant_atendente, tenant_gerente)`, mirrors `iam.ActionTenantInboxRead`), returns `{UserID, DisplayName}` for the dropdown. `IsAssignable` is the point-check the use case gates on.
3. **Queue filter** — `ConversationFilter.UnassignedOnly` completes the `all / assigned_to_me / unassigned` tri-state. `assigned_to_me` + the atendente `DisplayName` on the view (`AssignedUserLabel`) already landed in **SIN-64967**; this adds the missing `unassigned` axis only.

## Architecture lenses
- **Hexagonal / P&A** — the use case talks only to ports; zero `database/sql`/SQL in the use case. Attendant lookup, lead-cache sync and the filtered listing are ports with postgres adapters.
- **DDD-lite** — the "only assign to an attendant/gerente of the same tenant" invariant lives in the use case (validated server-side, caller never trusted), not the web layer.
- **Idiomatic Go** — errors as values (`errors.Is`), context propagated, small accept-broad/return-narrow ports, table-driven tests.

## Security (deny-by-default)
- Target user gated via tenant-scoped (RLS) `IsAssignable` → a **cross-tenant** id, an **unknown** id, or a **non-inbox role** all collapse to `ErrUserNotAssignable` (targetUserID IDOR). Conversation loaded under tenant scope → RLS-hidden id → `ErrNotFound` (conversationID IDOR). Both covered by integration tests (`tenant-isolation`, `cross-tenant ErrNotFound`).
- Assignment is **append-only** (`assignment_history`); no UPDATE/DELETE path added.
- Touches authn/authz semantics → flagging for CTO/Security review.

## Design note for review (cross-ticket coherence)
SIN-64967's read-model filters/projects on the **denormalised `conversation.assigned_user_id`** column. This PR's use case therefore syncs that column (`ConversationLeadStore.SetConversationLead`) in step with the ledger append, so the manual-assignment flow is correct end-to-end against the list pane.
**Pre-existing latent gap (not introduced here):** the auto default-lead path (`receive_inbound.attributeInitialLead`) writes only `assignment_history` and never persists `conversation.assigned_user_id`, so auto-led conversations currently read as unassigned in the list. Worth a follow-up ticket — happy to take it.

## Tests & gates
- `go test ./internal/inbox/... ./internal/adapter/db/postgres/` green. Coverage: `internal/inbox` 96.3%, `internal/inbox/usecase` 92.6%, `internal/adapter/db/postgres/inbox` 85.5% (all >85%).
- `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet ./...` (touched pkgs) clean, `staticcheck` clean.
- No existing test modified.

## Rollback
Pure additive (new ports/use-case/adapter methods + one additive bool filter param). No migration. Revert the two commits to fully back out; the new code is unreferenced by any router until the sibling UI child wires it.

body:
**PR 3 of the v0.11.0 series** (ADR-0032).

Replaces `Descriptor.encrypted_vectors: bool` with `vector_encryption: VectorEncryption { None, Dcpe, ClientSide }` across the engine, proto, server, and MCP. Behavior-preserving for the two existing modes; the `ClientSide` variant is **reserved** here and wired (enforcement + fetch path) in the next PR.

- **No data migration:** postcard encodes the former bool and the fieldless enum identically (`false`→`None`=0, `true`→`Dcpe`=1), so existing on-disk DCPE collections decode unchanged — proven by a new round-trip test over the legacy layout.
- **Pre-1.0 API refinement:** REST/gRPC/MCP now take `vector_encryption` (`"none"`/`"dcpe"`) instead of `encrypted_vectors: true`. The DCPE cipher and its cross-language KAT are untouched.
- The Python/TypeScript SDKs still send the old field; they migrate in a later PR (their tests mock the server, so the suites stay green meanwhile).

Full `just verify` green (37 suites).

## B-Tier #3 (part B) — Prometheus /metrics

Second half of B3 (follow-up to #21). Adds the observability endpoint, kept isolated because it introduces a runtime dependency.

### What
- Add **`prom-client`** (Apache-2.0) and expose **`GET /api/metrics`** with default Node/process metrics + a `salvadash_app_info` gauge labelled with the running version.

`METRICS_TOKEN` — set it (deploy env, not committed) to enable scraping. Documented here per the `.env`-protected convention.

body:
Closes #182

## Summary
Automated implementation of [Implementing/fix harness leaves code that fails `cargo clippy`/`cargo fmt`/`eslint` — only caught at pre-merge CI](https://github.com/accidental-hedge-fund/agent-pipeline/issues/182).

**Implemented by**: claude
**Plan reviewed by**: codex
**OpenSpec change**: `format-lint-normalization-in-harness`

## Proposal
## Why

The implementing/fix harness produces code that compiles and passes review but is not formatter/linter-clean; the first signal is a failing pre-merge CI check (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `eslint`), which requires a manual take-over. A normalization step immediately after the harness would either auto-fix style violations or block with a clear reason before a PR is opened.

## What Changes

- **New configurable `format_gate` section** in `.github/pipeline.yml` that lets operators declare one or more formatter/linter commands per language (e.g. `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --fix`, `eslint --fix`).
- After the implementing stage and after each fix-round stage, the pipeline SHALL run every configured `format_gate` command (in order) inside the worktree before opening or updating the PR.
- Commands that support auto-fix (`--fix` / `--write` variants) are applied first; the resulting changes are committed with a `chore: auto-format` commit so the harness commit range stays traceable.
- If a format/lint command exits non-zero after auto-fix, the pipeline blocks with the command output as the reason (rather than silently opening a PR that will fail CI).
- When no `format_gate` is configured, behavior is unchanged (existing pipeline runs are unaffected).

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `harness-format-lint-gate`: Post-harness normalization step that runs configured formatter/linter commands, commits auto-fixes, and blocks on unfixable violations before the PR is opened or updated.

### Modified Capabilities

- `harness-step-verification`: The verification sequence after the implementation and fix-round harnesses now includes an optional format/lint gate between harness exit and PR open/update.
- `pipeline-configuration`: A new optional `format_gate` top-level key is added to `.github/pipeline.yml` schema.

author: jeswr
body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Closes memsafety gap **MS-G3** (epic **sq-toze**, bead **sq-hybl**): there was no standalone AddressSanitizer lane outside cargo-fuzz, so the *deterministic* mmap corruption corpus (the oracle, MS-7) ran without a sanitizer and ASan coverage of the B5 on-disk-format reads was only as deep as the libFuzzer corpus reached.

## What this adds

A new **`.github/workflows/asan.yml`** lane that runs the existing deterministic mmap corruption corpus under AddressSanitizer:

- `crates/sparq-core/tests/mmap_corruption_oracle.rs` under `--features mmap,dict-spill` — the truncate + bit-flip sweep over every on-disk section (header / offsets / length fields / dict blob / compressed-perm blocks); this is the exact B5 surface Miri structurally cannot run (file-backed mappings).
- the `sparq-vectors` `store` + `diskann` open-validation corpus (truncated files / wrong magic / oversized length fields).

Command (documented Rust ASan flow):
```
RUSTFLAGS="-Zsanitizer=address" ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0" \
  cargo +nightly test -Zbuild-std --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu …
```
`-Zbuild-std` (needs `rust-src`) rebuilds std under the same `-Zsanitizer` flag; the GNU (dynamic-libc) triple is required because ASan rejects musl static libc (same constraint `fuzz.yml` documents); `detect_leaks=0` silences LeakSanitizer noise from rayon's daemon threads + the long-lived mmaps (a lifecycle artefact, cf. miri's `-Zmiri-ignore-leaks`).

## Blocking vs informational — NON-BLOCKING

Nightly `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only — **no** `pull_request`/`merge_group`/`push` trigger. `-Zbuild-std` recompiles std under ASan (many minutes), so this is a nightly UB safety net exactly like `miri.yml` / the nightly fuzz tier: it creates no check-run on a PR/merge-queue head, so the required `ci-summary / gate` aggregator never discovers or waits on it. The job name (`asan (mmap corruption corpus, informational)`) also carries the `informational` token belt-and-braces.

## Tested-vs-untested (honest)

The ASan flow (flags + `-Zbuild-std` + non-musl gnu `--target` + leak-suppress) was exercised locally on the agent's `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` host (a valid ASan target). The lane pins the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` runner triple (matching `fuzz.yml`), which was not run in this worktree — the flow is identical across the two gnu triples; **validate on the first scheduled/dispatched CI run.** Being non-blocking, a first-run hiccup cannot block any merge.

## Compliance

- `compliance/memsafety/gap-register.md` — **MS-G3 → CLOSED**.
- `compliance/memsafety/controls.md` — MS-9 now **PASS** (former ASan-blind-corpus caveat removed); coverage-matrix footnote updated.
- `compliance/memsafety/evidence.md` — MS-9 evidence updated with the exact lane commands + the tested-vs-untested note.

Refs sq-hybl, epic sq-toze.

author: gausah01
body:
## Purpose

Fix a CPU split-KV hang seen with `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`.

The worker could get stuck in `reduce_splits` waiting for a split completion flag. The root cause was the split-KV scratchpad was sized using the final output element size / smaller fallback q-head count, while the runtime split path writes temporary split outputs as `float` and can process more q-heads per split.

This could under-size the split-KV reduction buffer and allow split output data to overlap nearby reduction state, including split completion flags. As a result, `reduce_splits` could wait forever.

This PR sizes the relevant temporary outputs as `float` and sizes the split-KV reduction scratchpad using the maximum q-head tile the runtime can use.

## Test Plan

Test CPU throughput benchmark for `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`

```bash
LD_PRELOAD=/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libtcmalloc_minimal.so.4 \
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=64 \
VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=7200 \
vllm bench throughput \
  --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
  --dataset-name sonnet \
  --num-prompts 128 \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature": "0.0", "top_p": "1.0"}'
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --num-warmup 128
```

## Test Result

Before this change, the benchmark hung after prompt rendering and repeatedly printed:

`No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds.
`

After this change, the same benchmark run completes.

```
Throughput: 0.80 requests/s, 925.77 total tokens/s, 102.86 output tokens/s
Total num prompt tokens:  131072
Total num output tokens:  16384
```

author: moltagent
body:
## What

`EmailHandler._fetchEmails` has accepted a `folder` option (default `INBOX`) since it was written, but no handler ever passed it — every read went to `INBOX` regardless of which folder the user named. This wires the existing-but-stranded parameter through the intent layer so a user can name any IMAP folder in natural language.

## How (the model is the language layer; the code is plumbing)

- **`parseIntent`** gains an optional `folder` field in its JSON schema, with DE/EN/PT examples that teach the `INBOX.<NAME>` path convention through the examples (no prose, no hardcoded folder names).
- **`_normalizeFolder`** is the safety net: a bare name returned by the model (`INQUIRIES`) is normalized to `INBOX.INQUIRIES`. `INBOX` and `INBOX.x` pass through unchanged. Normalization happens **once**, at a single chokepoint that covers both the LLM and the fallback parse paths — the folder is computed once and travels canonically (*signals keep custody*).
- **`fallbackIntentParse`** (the regex dumb-fallback that only fires when the LLM parse throws entirely) gains a minimal folder capture, consistent with that function's existing nature; the primary language path stays the model.
- The four read handlers — `handleCheckInbox`, `handleCheckUnread`, `handleSearchEmails`, `handleSummarizeEmails` — forward `intent.folder || undefined`. Absent → `undefined` → the `_fetchEmails` `INBOX` default holds (regression-safe). `handleReadEmail`/`handleDraftReply` and all SMTP/send and IMAP-connection logic are untouched.

## Tests

11 new `TC-FOLDER` cases extend `test/unit/handlers/email-handler.test.js`: normalization (bare → `INBOX.<name>`, `INBOX` not double-prefixed, lowercase/empty/non-string edges), DE/PT extraction, the fallback capture, and a parameterized spy proving `intent.folder` reaches `_fetchEmails` for **all four** read handlers plus the no-folder → `undefined` regression.

- `npm run test:unit` → 223/223 test files pass
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors

## Live verification

Targeted harness driving the **real** `parseIntent` against the **local** `qwen3:8b` (the weakest roster model — if it extracts the folder, the cloud model will too), then the real read handler so the real `_fetchEmails` logs the folder it received — 5/5:

| Input | Lang | Parsed `folder` | Reached `_fetchEmails` |
|---|---|---|---|
| "check my INQUIRIES folder for new emails" | EN | `INBOX.INQUIRIES` | `INBOX.INQUIRIES` |
| "Schau in den SUPPORT Ordner" | DE | `INBOX.SUPPORT` | `INBOX.SUPPORT` |
| "Verifica a pasta PARCERIAS" | PT | `INBOX.PARCERIAS` | `INBOX.PARCERIAS` |
| "check my inbox" | EN | _(none)_ | `INBOX` (default) |
| "look in the ARCHIVE folder" | EN | `INBOX.ARCHIVE` | `INBOX.ARCHIVE` |

Note: email is not configured on the verification box, so a literal Talk turn would error at the IMAP-credential step — which is *downstream* of the folder-forwarding this PR adds. The harness isolates and confirms exactly the changed behavior.

body:
## What

Implements the app_factory **Reference List Runtime Protocol** so vibe-design project design assets become browsable / insertable Tutti references. Follows the spec at `services/tuttid/service/workspace/app_factory_reference/SKILL.md`.

vibe-design was already a Tutti app (manifest + read-only CLI), but `tutti.app.json` declared no `references` block, so this protocol was unimplemented. This adds it.

## Changes

- **`tutti.app.json`**: add `references.listEndpoint: /tutti/references/list`.
- **`server/src/routes/references-routes.ts`** (new): implement `POST /tutti/references/list`.
  - Root level → one navigational `group` per project (`id` = project id, `referenceCount` = exact file count under `kinds`/`timeRange`, unaffected by `filterText`).
  - Inside a project group (`parentGroupId` = project id) → project files as `file` references.
  - Each file reference uses `location: { "type": "app-data-relative", "path": "projects/<projectId>/assets/<name>" }` — never an absolute host path or HTTP URL; the daemon resolves it.
  - Supports `filterText` (direct-child filter), `limit` (clamped 1..50), opaque offset `cursor`, `timeRange` (applied to file `mtimeMs`), and `kinds` (v1 `["file"]`).
  - Path safety via existing `isSafeProjectId` / `isSafeFileName` (no `..`, no separators).
- **`server/src/server.ts`**: register the route.
- **`AGENTS.tutti-app.md`**: document the File References protocol.
- **`server/src/routes/references-routes.test.ts`** (new): 5 route tests.

## Decisions

- Tree shape: **projects as groups → files**.
- Asset scope: **project files only** (`project_files`); `public_assets` / design systems intentionally excluded.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- server vitest: 243 passed (incl. 5 new references tests)
- `node --test scripts/package-tutti-app.test.mjs`: 9 passed (manifest contract validation accepts the new `references` block)

author: dreamcreateweb
body:
Clicking "Open editor" right after signup crashed with a fatal **"Application error: a client-side exception has occurred"** — the open page referenced a JS chunk by an old hash that the freshly-deployed server no longer served, so the chunk 404'd and the `text/plain` 404 body was rejected as a script. A manual refresh fixed it (fresh chunks), but a subscriber must never hit that crash mid‑signup.

- New `<ChunkReloadGuard>` mounted once at the root layout: listens (capture phase) for chunk-load / dynamic-import / MIME-type script failures + matching `unhandledrejection`s and reloads **once** — loop-guarded via `sessionStorage` so a genuinely-missing chunk can't reload forever. Each App Runner instance serves a self-consistent HTML+chunks set, so one reload lands on a matching build. Inert except during a deploy skew; ordinary app errors are untouched.
- Tests cover the matcher and the listener (reload once, no loop, recovers from an unhandled rejection, ignores ordinary errors).

Build clean.

author: vyacheslav-tomashevskiy
body:
Implements **Task 5 — Provenance tool (7 RTC)** from #1: a read-only, keyless LangChain tool that surfaces **RIP-0310 Proof-of-Provenance** status for a Beacon agent id.

### What it adds
- **`rustchain_provenance` tool** (arg: `agent_id` — a `bcn_<hex>` id or display name). Returns a compact, agent-friendly summary mapped to the RIP-0310 layers.
- **Client methods** (`rustchain_langchain/client.py`):
  - `beacon_agents()` → `GET /beacon/api/agents` (registered Beacon identity cards)
  - `beacon_contracts()` → `GET /beacon/api/contracts` (economic activity)
  - `provenance(agent_id)` → composes the deployed signals for one identity (matches by id, falls back to display name; collects the contracts it is party to with payer/payee role).
- **Pure `summarize_provenance(data)`** helper (framework-free, exported), unit-tested on its own.

### Faithful to the spec's stated status
RIP-0310 says plainly that the **Agent** and **Economic** layers are deployed, **Hardware** is a precondition layer on the RustChain node, and the **Content-Provenance binding is specified but not yet built**. The tool reflects exactly that — it reports identity + economic activity that the live Beacon API exposes, and is explicit that there is *no live `BindingCert` endpoint yet*, so it never fabricates a "VERIFIED" content binding the API can't back.

### Safety contract (matches the package)
- Read-only / keyless — only public `GET`s, no wallet writes, no secrets.
- Never raises inside an agent loop — failures are wrapped and returned as a string.
- Compact summary, not a raw JSON blob.

### Tests
`pytest -q` → **20 passed** (6 new): client composition (id + display-name match, not-found), summarizer (found / not-found), tool run, and the never-raise guard — all HTTP mocked, no network in CI. README updated, version `0.2.0 → 0.3.0`.

Verified live against `rustchain.org/beacon/api`: e.g. `bcn_sophia_elya` → identity active + 7 contracts; unknown id → graceful "no agent found (116 registered)".

I'll share an RTC wallet address before merge. /claim #1

author: barefootbetters
body:
## What

A short, ratifiable decision doc — `docs/ai/DESIGN-EFFECT-MODEL-DECISION.md` — answering the architecture question Jeff raised while scoping Berserk: **keep a closed one-keyword-per-mechanic vocabulary (engine change per mechanic), or move toward self-describing, data-driven cards?**

Extends `DESIGN-EFFECT-AUTHORING-SCALE.md` §2b (its "load-bearing finding", D-20201) — this is the next chapter, not a new direction.

## The decision it proposes

- **The Levers shrank the keyword union but didn't open it** — Berserk still needs an engine change. That's the real friction vs. Vision Goal 10.
- **The hard constraint:** determinism/replay/testability means "self-describing" can't be arbitrary per-card logic — it must be a declarative description in a vocabulary the engine interprets.
- **Spectrum:** closed keyword → parameterized keyword (today) → **composable primitives (target)** → full DSL (over-engineered).
- **Recommendation: model C — composable primitives.** Cards compose a small orthogonal primitive set; the decision rule for every new mechanic becomes *"new primitive, or composition of existing ones?"* Compositions ship as pure data (no engine WP). Only a genuinely-new primitive earns engine work.
- Includes the honest **premature-abstraction counter-pressure** (duplicate-first vs. the known 124-mechanic tail) and what it changes for **Berserk** (implement a reusable `discard-top-gain-from-stat` primitive, not a narrow `berserk` keyword).

## Status

**DRAFT for ratification.** Reserves a `DECISIONS.md` D-entry and an update to `DESIGN-EFFECT-AUTHORING-SCALE.md` §2b/§5 on approval. No code; no contract changed yet. This gates whether the next engine work (Berserk) is done the old way or the new way.

body:
## What

Wires up the `[Start Playing]` button in `<backlog-list>` — the first status transition (M3). Clicking it moves a game from the backlog queue into the `playing` status. Closes #10.

## Details

- New `startPlaying(id)` method on `BacklogList`, dispatched from the existing event-delegation `switch` (the `start` case was previously a no-op).
- On click it finds the `UserGame`, sets `status = "playing"` and stamps `dateStarted = new Date().toISOString()` **at the moment of the click** (never on load), persists via `saveState()`, then fires a `status-changed` `CustomEvent` with `detail: { id, newStatus: "playing" }`.
- The list already re-renders on `status-changed`, so the row drops out of the FIFO queue immediately (it no longer matches `status === "backlog"`) — no full page reload, no confirmation.
- `status-changed` is the hook the playing dashboard (M4) will listen on. The multi-game friction warning is **deferred to M4**, so starting is unrestricted for now, per the issue.

## Verification

- `bun run check` → **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints**
- `bun run build` → succeeds, emits `dist/app/index.html`
- Browser (`/app`, dev server): clicking `[Start Playing]` on *Outer Wilds* —
  - fired `status-changed` with `{ id, newStatus: "playing" }` ✓
  - set `status: "playing"` and a valid ISO `dateStarted` in `localStorage`, stamped at click time ✓
  - removed the row from the list immediately (backlog 4 → 3 rows, *Outer Wilds* gone) ✓
  - **0 console errors**

## Docs

- `CLAUDE.md` — updated the "What this is" intro and the `BacklogList` paragraph to describe the Start Playing wiring (replacing the "playing transition is still left to its own issue" note).
- `README.md` — added the *Start Playing* action to the "What's intentionally not here yet" feature list.

## Out of scope

- The playing **dashboard** view and the multi-game friction warning (M4 / issue's own note).
- `[Remove]` and `[Edit]` behaviour (already shipped in earlier issues) untouched.

author: cgfixit
body:
## Summary

Audit and fix of the GitHub Actions CI configuration. The only real, reproducible CI failure was the **Python 3.9 matrix entry**: `requirements.txt` pins `py-clob-client>=0.34.0`, which dropped 3.9 support, so `pip install -r requirements.txt` fails on the 3.9 job. The rest of the requested hardening was either already in place (concurrency group, pip cache) or not applicable (no live-API tests, no module-level env reads, no lint violations).

## FINDINGS SUMMARY

```
1. Integration tests making live API calls: NONE.
   - tests/test_integration.py:27-49 defines _FakeResp/_FakeSession (in-memory stubs).
   - tests/test_integration.py:67-75 uses an AsyncMock `gamma` fixture.
   - All dispatch runs through monitor._poll_wallet(session, ...) with the fake
     session (lines 108/111, 121/123-124, 133-134, 150-151, 165-166) and
     monitor._handle_ws_message(raw) with literal JSON (lines 141, 156, 172).
   - tests/test_data_client.py patches DataClient._get (lines 24,32,38,47,53).
   - tests/test_gamma_client.py patches _get / _get_session (lines 55,64,71,79,86).
   => No test in the suite performs a live Polymarket CLOB or Gamma API call.

2. Module-level env reads that will fail in CI without stubs: NONE.
   - polymarket_copier/config.py reads os.getenv ONLY inside load_config()
     (lines 82, 90-97). No os.environ/os.getenv at module scope anywhere in
     polymarket_copier/.

3. Ruff violations found (F401/F821/E302/W291): NONE.
   - `ruff check .` => "All checks passed!" (E/F/W, line-length 120).

4. py-clob-client 3.9 compat: CONFIRMED INCOMPATIBLE
   (pre-resolved: py-clob-client dropped Python 3.9 in v0.34.0;
    requirements.txt pins py-clob-client>=0.34.0).

5. Any other blockers:
   - ci.yml:24 matrix included "3.9" -> dependency install fails. THE real failure.
   - pyproject.toml:5 requires-python ">=3.9"; pyproject.toml:9 target-version "py39".
   - NOTE (already satisfied): concurrency group present (ci.yml:12-15);
     `cache: pip` present (ci.yml:34 and ci.yml:55).
```

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**
  - Matrix: `["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]` → `["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]`.
  - Test step: `pytest -v` → `pytest -v -m "not integration"`.
  - Concurrency group and `cache: pip` were already present — left unchanged.
- **`pyproject.toml`**
  - `requires-python = ">=3.9"` → `">=3.10"`.
  - ruff `target-version = "py39"` → `"py310"` (kept consistent with the dropped runtime).
  - Registered the `integration` marker under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`.

## Tests marked `@pytest.mark.integration`

**NONE.** No test performs a live Polymarket API call — every network boundary is replaced by an in-memory `_FakeSession`/`_FakeResp` or `AsyncMock` (see Finding 1 for file:line citations). The `integration` marker is registered and CI runs with `-m "not integration"` as a forward-looking convention, so any future live-API test is gated by default. Integration test logic was **not** removed or gutted.

## Ruff violations fixed

**NONE.** `ruff check .` reports "All checks passed!" both before and after the change.

## requires-python

Updated: `>=3.9` → `>=3.10` (and ruff `target-version` `py39` → `py310`) to match the dropped 3.9 runtime.

## Env stub block

**Omitted intentionally.** No module-level `os.environ`/`os.getenv` reads exist — `config.py` reads env only inside `load_config()`. Adding dummy `POLYMARKET_*` env vars would have been speculative, so per the task constraints it was not added.

## Verification

- `ruff check .` → All checks passed!
- `python -m pytest -q -m "not integration"` → **144 passed** (no unknown-marker warnings, confirming the marker is registered).

author: amattas
body:
## Summary

Two configure-time UX changes you asked for.

### 1. Ask for months, not a date range (window ends yesterday)
Operators think in ""how much history,"" and a fixed end date leaves a gap before real-time streaming. `configure` now asks **how many months** of data to generate and derives the window so it **ends yesterday** — streaming then continues seamlessly from today.

- `GenerationConfig` gains `months` (1–120) and derives `start_date`/`end_date` (end = yesterday) when explicit dates aren't both supplied. **Explicit dates still work** (back-compat) and take precedence, so the generation engine and its tests are unchanged. `utility/config.yaml` now persists `months`.

### 2. Record-count estimate with a chance to change settings
After you pick the generation settings, `configure` prints an approximate breakdown so you can gauge volume/runtime, then (interactively) asks whether to use them or re-enter:

`
------------------------------------------------------------
  Estimated records for 2026-03-15 to 2026-06-15 (50 stores):
    Customers (dim)      ~          50,000
    In-store receipts    ~       1,878,600
    Receipt lines        ~      22,320,000
    Online orders        ~          37,200
    Online order lines   ~         107,880
    Payments             ~       1,915,800
    Total (approx)       ~      26,309,480
------------------------------------------------------------
Use these settings? [Y/n]
`

New `retail_setup/generation/estimate.py` (Spark-free, lazy-imported) grounds the numbers in `store_count × days × transactions_per_store_day` and the store profile's basket size.

## Tests
- `test_generation_config.py`: months derivation (ends yesterday), `months` required when no dates, explicit-dates precedence, `_subtract_months` day-clamping/leap-year, months yaml round-trip.
- `test_estimate.py`: totals, scaling with stores/days/months, basket fallback.
- `test_cli_configure.py`: configure writes `months` (not dates) and shows the estimate.
- Suite green; ruff clean. (Pre-existing `test_render_writes_rendered_notebooks` fails only due to Windows `os.symlink` privilege — unrelated.)

## Docs
`utility/README.md` and `website/docs/setup/configuration.md` updated for the months input and the estimate.

> **Stacked on #299** (shares `cli/main.py`). Base is `feat/deploy-retry-and-progress`; merge #299 first and this auto-retargets to `main`.

author: shaunandrews
body:
## Proposed Changes

- Removes the experimental ui-desks interface from Studio so the app no longer exposes or carries the alternate desk/canvas experience.
- Keeps the supported Studio renderer paths intact: default Studio continues to use the legacy renderer, while the agentic UI flag uses the maintained `@studio/ui` renderer.
- Cleans up now-unused desk state so existing app configs stop carrying obsolete desk data after migration.
- Drops the desk-only dependency footprint, including `tldraw`, along with stale UI-mode flags and user-facing desk wording.

---

Most of this PR is deletion. The main new logic is the `06-remove-desks-config` migration, which removes obsolete top-level `desks` data from the Desktop app config after the ui-desks interface is gone.

The migration:

- Checks whether `app.json` exists and has an own top-level `desks` property.
- Treats missing, invalid, or non-object config as "nothing to migrate".
- Locks app config with `lockAppdata()` before writing.
- Re-reads the config while locked, removes only `desks`, and preserves the rest of the file.
- Always calls `unlockAppdata()` in `finally`, including write failures.

The focused tests cover:

- `needsToRun()` returning true only when `desks` exists.
- Missing or invalid config safely skipping the migration.
- Removing only `desks` while preserving unrelated app config.
- Unlocking app data if the write fails.

---

### Do we want the migration at all?

Keeping it makes the removal tidy by deleting orphaned ui-desks state from `app.json`. Removing it would make this PR closer to a pure code deletion, and may be reasonable because only a small number of people likely used ui-desks and any saved desk data is unlikely to be worth preserving or explicitly cleaning up. The stale `desks` key would be inert once the interface and IPC/storage paths are gone.

author: yanekyuk
body: Reorganizes `packages/protocol/eval/` from a single matching harness into a shared-library + thin-harness layout, adds three new quality harnesses, and makes every eval report readable by a non-technical stakeholder. ## New Features - **Shared eval harness library** (`eval/shared/`): generic runner, scorecard aggregation, baseline diff + rolling baseline, stats/CI, CLI flag parsing, console + HTML reporting. Each harness keeps its own rich case/scorecard types while reusing the plumbing. - **`eval/premise/` harness** — decomposer + analyzer quality (atomicity, tier classification, intent exclusion, empty input, speech act, felicity calibration, entropy). 10-case baseline, 100%. - **`eval/profile/` harness** — profile generation with a hard PII/privacy guarantee (`profile.pii.ts`). 8-case baseline, 100%. - **`eval/opportunity/` harness** — quality of the user-facing card written by `OpportunityPresenter.present` (headline, personalized summary, suggested action, intro greeting). Deterministic second-person + no-leakage checks always on; greeting checks opt-in; grounding/framing/tone judged. Runner retries past the presenter's timeout fallback so it measures real model output. - **Plain-language HTML reports** — every harness report now leads with a stakeholder-readable summary (verdict banner + "What we tested" + per-scenario narratives), with the technical scorecard collapsed below. Built generically in `eval/shared/html.ts`. - Wired `eval:premise` / `eval:profile` / `eval:opportunity` package scripts; gitignored per-harness `runs/`. ## Bug Fixes - Report banner now counts **scenarios** a reader can see (`79% — 5 of 8 scenarios passed every time`) instead of `19 of 24 checks`, which conflated cases×runs and didn't reconcile with the themes listed below it. Blurb names a single always-failing theme and tallies the rest. ## Notable finding - The opportunity harness immediately surfaced a real defect: `OpportunityPresenter` prepends a `Hi {Name},` salutation to the intro greeting on most runs, which its own prompt forbids. Captured cleanly in the `greeting/plain-prose` case (not fixed in this PR — eval only). ## Tests - 161 eval unit tests across the four harnesses (shared lib, premise, profile, opportunity), all green. Evals themselves remain opt-in (require `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`), not part of `bun test`. ## Version - `@indexnetwork/protocol` 3.6.3 → 3.7.0 (eval tooling only; `files: ["dist"]` unchanged). --- Need help on this PR? author: rohitsinghal4u
body:
## Summary

Enables C# autogeneration for the Key Vault **Certificates** data-plane via the TypeSpec emitter, mirroring the Secrets change in #43999. With these knobs in place, `tsp-client update` from `azure-sdk-for-net` can produce the low-level transport that the hand-written `Azure.Security.KeyVault.Certificates` package will wrap.

## Changes

**`specification/keyvault/data-plane/Certificates/tspconfig.yaml`**
- Enable `@azure-typespec/http-client-csharp` (modern emitter; same one Administration and Secrets use).
- Enable `@azure-tools/typespec-csharp` (legacy emitter) for packages that haven't migrated yet.
- Both emitters write to `{output-dir}/{service-dir}/{namespace}` under namespace `Azure.Security.KeyVault.Certificates`.

**`specification/keyvault/data-plane/Certificates/client.tsp`**
Adds 9 C# rename customizations. Certificates has a much larger hand-written surface than Secrets, so several generated wire-model names would collide with public/internal types in `Azure.Security.KeyVault.Certificates`. All renames are scoped via the `""csharp""` discriminator and follow the convention already used by Java / Go / Rust on this RP.

| spec type | C# generated name | reason |
|---|---|---|
| `KeyVault` | `KeyVaultCertificatesClient` | disambiguates the low-level client |
| `CertificateAttributes` | `CertificateAttributesBundle` | hand-written `internal struct CertificateAttributes` |
| `CertificateOperation` | `CertificateOperationBundle` | hand-written `public class CertificateOperation` |
| `CertificatePolicy` | `CertificatePolicyBundle` | hand-written `public class CertificatePolicy` |
| `LifetimeAction` | `LifetimeActionBundle` | hand-written `public class LifetimeAction` |
| `SubjectAlternativeNames` | `SubjectAlternativeNamesProperties` | hand-written `public class SubjectAlternativeNames` |
| `CertificateCreateParameters` | `CertificateCreateParametersBundle` | hand-written `internal class` of the same name |
| `CertificateUpdateParameters` | `CertificateUpdateParametersBundle` | hand-written `internal class` of the same name |
| `IssuerParameters` | `IssuerParametersBundle` | hand-written `internal struct IssuerParameters` |

## Other languages

Verified the `""csharp""` scope confines every rename: SDK Validation jobs for Java / Python / Go / JS / Rust on this PR should remain green. No spec-shape change, no API version bump.

## Out of scope

This PR only flips spec-side knobs. The .NET-side adoption — new `CertificateGeneratedClient` thin wrapper, `Internalize-Generated.ps1` post-emit script, `CertificateMapper`, LRO bridges, recorded tests — will land in a separate `azure-sdk-for-net` PR following the pattern already used for Secrets.

- parent `a01cf929674` (docs) → ✅ **GOOD, Top-1 92%**
- `bb78d08fb43` (#45179) → ❌ **BAD, Top-1 0%**

#45179 **removed the y-dim restore** in `_llk_unpack_tilize_uninit_`, on the assumption that *"y-dim is left untouched by tilize, so we don't restore it."* That assumption is wrong: the tile descriptor's y-dim (lower 16 bits of `THCON_SEC0_REG0_TileDescriptor_ADDR32 + 1`) is left dirty after tilize, corrupting subsequent unpack ops → garbage activations → total accuracy loss on Qwen3-32B Galaxy.

## Fix

Restore the pre-#45179 y-dim reset (set the tile-descriptor y-dim back to its default of 1), while **keeping #45179's legitimate z-dim=`num_faces` change**:

```c
cfg_reg_rmw_tensix<THCON_SEC0_REG0_TileDescriptor_ADDR32 + 1, 16, 0xffff0000>(num_faces);  // z-dim (kept from #45179)
cfg_reg_rmw_tensix<THCON_SEC0_REG0_TileDescriptor_ADDR32 + 1,  0, 0x0000ffff>(1);          // y-dim (restored)
```

Body-only change — no signature change, so no metal-API/Compute-API propagation needed.

**Scope:** Wormhole only. #45179 did not touch the Blackhole llk_lib, so BH is intentionally untouched.

> Note: a literal `git revert` of #45179 does **not** build on current `main` — `_llk_unpack_tilize_uninit_`'s signature changed 2→3→2 params across later commits — so this is the targeted reversal of the specific behavioral regression rather than a whole-commit revert.

## Validation — accuracy

⏳ 3 redundant `qwen3-32b-galaxy / wh_galaxy_perf` accuracy runs dispatched on this branch (`a2a5bf9`), expecting Top-1 to return to ~90%+:

- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/27640429944
- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/27640445207
- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/27640458947

(3× for redundancy — the `wh_galaxy_perf` runner has been flaky; we need one clean completion.)

## Validation — LLK tilize/unpack regression coverage

This touches `_llk_unpack_tilize_uninit_`, so the LLK tilize/unpack suite is the relevant regression guard:
- **`test_tilize_uninit.py`** — the regression test #45179 itself added. It asserts only that the **z-dim** is restored to `num_faces`; this fix preserves that, so it stays green. ✅ (it does not check y-dim)
- `test_unpack_tilize_sweep.py`, `test_zzz_unpack_tilize.py`, `test_fast_tilize*.py`, `test_matmul_unpack_tilize.py`, `test_unpack_A.py`, `test_unpack_matmul.py`, and the fuser tilize cases (`tilize_a`, `tilize_only_num_faces_2`, `fpu_tilize_a_then_unpack_a`).

⚠️ Tried to dispatch the dedicated **LLK e2e** workflow on this branch but it `startup_failure`s — **the `llk-e2e.yaml` workflow is currently broken on `main` too** (every scheduled run since at least Jun 13 is `startup_failure`; unrelated to this change). LLK coverage should run via merge-gate / the LLK pipeline once that workflow is fixed.

## Cross-check — author's fix PR #47036

The author of #45179 has an alternative fix in #47036 (`ldjurovic/fix_47016`). Dispatched the same 3 redundant `qwen3-32b-galaxy / wh_galaxy_perf` accuracy runs on it for comparison:

- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/27641367569
- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/27641381663
- https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/27641395782

If #47036 also restores accuracy, it likely supersedes this PR (this one can then be closed in its favor).

cc @ldjurovic (author of #45179) — please sanity-check the y-dim restore is the intended behavior.

Relates to #47049.

author: timkelty
body:
### Description

Moves document sync onto Craft's batched queue job contract so large indexes can progress across spawned jobs without losing stale-document cleanup state.

Based on https://github.com/craftpulse/craft-typesense/compare/v5...imarc:craft-typesense:v5, but fixing some issues (cc @LinneaImarc)

- It put flush/create side effects in `loadData()`. Since `BaseBatchedJob` reloads data for spawned batches, a flush job could delete/recreate the collection again on later batches.
- It stored processed IDs in protected `$upsertIds`, which won’t survive queue serialization between spawned jobs. That makes stale cleanup only aware of the final batch.
- It didn’t guarantee `loadData()` returns a `Batchable` on missing client/collection paths.
- It batched the original criteria query without cloning or forcing stable ID ordering, which makes offset-based batching more fragile.

body:
## What

Prep for a part-number-deduped merge load of a stockroom master into San Carlos (lab 2) inventory. Two backward-compatible admin-endpoint extensions:

1. **`POST /api/admin/import-inventory`** now accepts and persists `order_unit`, `usage_unit`, `count_unit`, `units_per_order_unit`, `units_per_count_unit`. Previously it set only the legacy `unit`, so pack/case items imported as "each" in the count-unit-aware UI. Backward compatible: when only the legacy `unit` is given (or nothing), all three unit roles mirror it and pack sizes default to 1.
2. **`GET /api/admin/labs/:labId/inventory`** now also returns `catalog_number` + `unit`/`usage_unit`/`count_unit`/`units_per_count_unit`, so a loader can dedupe incoming rows against existing items by part number and verify UOM after the load.

## Why

The ULS stockroom export overlaps the 186 curated items already in San Carlos. Reliable dedupe needs part-number matching (names differ: ERP abbreviations vs descriptive names), which requires exposing existing `catalog_number`. And the load must set the real UOM so the 116 pack/case rows don't display as "each".

## Scope

No new table or column (both `inventory_items` columns already exist in `db.ts`). Pure backend wiring, no UI element, so Gate 3 step 8 (browser) is N/A for this PR. The customer-facing verification happens at the actual load step (post-deploy) against the San Carlos list.

## Testing

- `npm run check` (tsc): clean.
- `python script/audit.py`: PASSED, 0 errors.
- Backward-compat reasoned through: existing single-`unit` callers unaffected.
