author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
## Problem The dev-only `open-in-editor` endpoint (`re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server`, a JVM-only `:dev-http` handler) launched the developer's editor on an **arbitrary local file** for **any cross-origin request**: - `handle` answered both GET and POST (only `:options` was special-cased); - `json-resp` set `access-control-allow-origin "*"`; - a simple GET needs no CORS preflight. So any web page the developer was visiting could fire `fetch("http://localhost:/__rf-open-in-editor?file=…", {mode:"no-cors"})` (or an ``/`
`) and open an attacker-chosen file in the editor — `resolve-file` passes an absolute path (`/etc/passwd`, `C:/…`) or a `../`-traversal path straight through. Same drive-by class as the historic Vite / react-dev-utils CVEs. Dev-only + localhost + opens-in-editor (no file content returned over HTTP), but reachable from any browsed page. ## Fix Pin the endpoint to the local machine and a local browsing context: 1. **POST-only launch path** — a simple GET/HEAD drive-by (the only thing an ``/``/`no-cors` simple request can issue) gets `405` and never reaches `launch!`. 2. **Loopback `Host` required** — the request must have been addressed to `localhost` / `127.0.0.0/8` / `[::1]`; a non-loopback host (public-binding / DNS-rebinding attempt) gets `403` before any path resolution. 3. **Loopback `Origin` when present** — a remote page's cross-origin POST (`Origin: https://evil.example`) is rejected `403`; a legitimate cross-**PORT** dev request (Story shell on `:8042` → app on `:8031`) carries `http://localhost:8042` and passes. A same-origin POST may omit `Origin` and passes on the Host check alone. CORS is reflected to the **validated loopback origin only** (with `vary: origin`) — the `*` wildcard is gone. The OPTIONS preflight now offers `POST, OPTIONS` (no GET). ## DX unchanged The default client (`re-frame.source-coords.open-endpoint/fetch-launcher!`) already issues a **POST** from the same / cross-PORT dev origin, so the legitimate jump-to-source path is unaffected. ## Tests Adds JVM regression tests (`clojure -M:test`) with `launch!` redirected to a recording stub: - valid local POST (loopback Host + loopback Origin, and the omitted-Origin same-origin case) reaches `launch!` and answers `200`, reflecting its loopback origin; - cross-origin POST → `403`, `launch!` **never called**, no wildcard CORS; - non-loopback / missing Host → `403`, `launch!` never called; - GET drive-by → `405`, `launch!` never called; - OPTIONS preflight reflects loopback origin + offers POST only; - unit coverage for `loopback-host?` (port / IPv4 127.0.0.0/8 / IPv6 / case / non-loopback `127malicious.example`) and `origin-host` (opaque `null` → nil). `tools/testbed-support` JVM tests: 13 tests, 51 assertions, 0 failures. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`: 7642 tests, 0 failures (markdown gates green; mkdocs soft-skips on Windows). Scope note: the bead also flags secondary defects (the `parse-query` `+`→space decode, a Story-shell hashchange teardown, a dropped-column edge); those are out of scope for this security fix and remain on the bead.

body:
Closes #855.

## What
A per-row **"Update image"** button in the Aplicações (`/admin/specs`) actions column, for **containerized apps** (hidden for external/link cards — no image). Clicking **force re-pulls** the app's image from the registry, in place.

## Changes
- **New route** `POST /admin/specs/{id}/repull` (`spec_form.rs`): resolves the DB spec's image + registry creds the same way the spawn path does (`proxy::resolve_creds`), starts the pull, returns `{ "job": <token> }`.

- **List button**: runs over `fetch` → follows the existing `…/image-pull/events` SSE until the `done` event; `ti-loader-2` spinner while running, then a brief ✓ / ✗ flash. Titles ride `data-*` and are read via `$el.dataset` — never localized strings inside the JS handler (`template_lint`). Localized pt/en/es/fr.

## Scope / limitations
- **DB specs only** — config-only YAML rows don't get the button yet (they 404 the by-id route). Most catalogs are DB-managed; can extend via the effective catalog later.

`cargo build` + `cargo test -p ruscker-admin` (incl. `template_lint` + `load_default_succeeds`), `clippy -D warnings`, i18n parity — all green.

Touches **Alpine + SSE** (the fetch→EventSource→`done` flow + spinner). Per "test Alpine in a browser, not curl", verify the button (spinner, ✓/✗, real re-pull of a cached image) on the next **cast** deploy before merge — I can drive it with Playwright once cast picks up a build.

author: henry-dowling
body: ## Problem HTML pages render their `` as an ugly, unstyled (browser-default Arial) line at the very top of the body, above the author's styled content. Repro: upload any complete HTML document (with `<head><title>…`). The title text appears as a bare text node in the rendered page. ## Root cause `_sanitize_html` runs `nh3.clean`. nh3 strips tags that aren't in the allowed set **but keeps their text content**. `` isn't an allowed tag, so the tag is removed while `Data Retention in Sales Calls — Gong Analysis · Acme Corp` survives as a bare text node in the body — and since a `<title>` carries no CSS, it falls back to the browser default font. `<style>` *is* allowed, which is why everything else on the page stays correctly styled. ## Fix Add `title` to `clean_content_tags` so its content is removed entirely (same treatment `<script>` already gets). Authors routinely include a `<title>` in full HTML documents, so this is the common case, not an edge case. Verified directly against nh3: ``` BEFORE: Gong Analysis · Acme Corp<style>h1{font-family:Fraunces}</style><h1>Report</h1> AFTER: <style>h1{font-family:Fraunces}</style><h1>Report</h1> ``` Author `<style>` and content are untouched. ## Tests Added `test_title_text_does_not_leak_into_body` to `test_html_sanitize.py`, pinning that the title text is gone while author styling and content survive. > Note: the DB-backed test wasn't executed locally (this checkout has the CLI venv, not the backend test deps + Postgres test DB). author: jasonhernandez
body:
## Problem

The console's `Content-Security-Policy` header is **not** committed in `console/vercel.json` — it's injected at build time by `console/bin/apply-vercel-csp.js`, which must run *before* `vercel build`.

In the original `MaterializeInc/console` repo, both the production (`deploy-prod.yml`) and preview (`deploy-preview.yml`) deploys went through `bin/build-ci`, which ran `apply-vercel-csp.js` before building.

When the console was ported into this repo (#35032), the deploy logic was reimplemented as Buildkite scripts that call `vercel build` directly and **dropped the `apply-vercel-csp.js` step**. `console/bin/build-ci` was carried over intact but is no longer invoked by anything.

As a result, the real console deploys ship with **no CSP header at all**:

| Deploy | Script | CSP injected? |
|---|---|---|
| Production (`console.materialize.com`) | `ci/deploy/console.sh` | ❌ before |
| Impersonation (`internal.console.materialize.com`) | `ci/deploy/console-impersonation.sh` | ❌ before |
| PR preview | `ci/test/console/vercel-preview.sh` | ❌ before |
| e2e test (throwaway preview) | `ci/test/console/e2e-prod.sh` | ✅ (unchanged) |

Confirmed live — `curl -sI https://console.materialize.com` returns `x-frame-options` and `referrer-policy` but **no `content-security-policy`**.

## Fix

Run `bin/apply-vercel-csp.js --sentry-release="$SENTRY_RELEASE"` before `vercel build` in all three real deploy scripts, matching the original `bin/build-ci` behavior. All three already export `SENTRY_RELEASE`.

author: krasnoperov
body:
## Problem

An issue can spin forever — enqueued and skipped every ~5s reconcile tick, never launching a run or writing its row (frozen `updated_at`, no logs since skips are info-level). Observed live on INV-29, stuck >25 min with a green/approved-pending PR.

## Root cause chain

1. A review_fix run finished leaving a **false-positive dirty worktree** — a lingering `MERGE_HEAD` over an otherwise-clean tree (`changedPaths: []`). `inspectGitWorktreeStatus` flagged dirty purely on the marker → finalizer emitted a `completion_check_continue`.
2. That `completion_check_continue` carried the finished run's **review_fix** run type → `deriveSessionWakePlan` re-derived a review_fix wake.
3. The PR's review had moved off `changes_requested` (review-quill's earlier reviews were auto-dismissed by new pushes). The orchestrator's `resolveInactiveRequestedChangesWakeReason` declared the wake inactive and tried to clear it — but it **only dismisses `review_changes_requested` events**. The triggers were `completion_check_continue` + `delegated`, so nothing cleared → re-derived forever.

## Fix (two source-level layers, defense in depth)

- **`git-worktree-status`:** a worktree is actionably dirty only when `git status` reports lines (changes or unmerged paths). A vestigial `MERGE_HEAD`/`REBASE_HEAD` over a clean tree is no longer dirty → the spurious continue is never emitted. A real merge conflict still surfaces (unmerged porcelain lines).
- **`issue-session-events`:** a wake payload's `review_fix` run type is downgraded to `implementation` when the PR is no longer `changes_requested` — both the `delegated` and `completion_check_continue` paths, via shared `resolvePayloadRunType`. A review_fix wake can then only reach the inactive guard via an actual `review_changes_requested` event, which the orchestrator **already** dismisses correctly. `branch_upkeep` is intentionally exempt (it never hits that guard and is valid branch maintenance).

No orchestrator change was needed — an earlier "dismiss all wake events" approach was reverted because it would discard coalesced operator-prompt/follow-up input that must be preserved (covered by an existing test).

## Tests

- New `git-worktree-status.test.ts`: clean tree, vestigial `MERGE_HEAD` (not dirty), uncommitted changes (dirty), real merge conflict (dirty + unmerged paths) — using a real linked worktree to mirror production path resolution.
- New wake-derivation cases: review_fix downgrade (delegated + completion_check_continue), preserve when still changes_requested, preserve branch_upkeep.
- Full suite: 1025 pass.

author: amaannn17
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced `time.sleep(timeout)` with `self._stop_event.wait(timeout)` in `ConnectionThread.run` within `cipclient.py`.

🎯 **Why:** A worker thread blocked on `time.sleep()` cannot respond to a stop event until the sleep period finishes, potentially causing huge shutdown latencies (up to 10 seconds in `ConnectionThread`). `Event.wait()` achieves the same delay but allows the wait to be immediately interrupted when the stop event is signaled.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces thread shutdown latency from ~9.0 seconds to ~0.0004 seconds (over 20,000x faster shutdown when blocked waiting for connection).

🔬 **Measurement:** Measured by initializing a `MockCIP` and `ConnectionThread` that throws `OSError` on connection to force the 10-second wait block, then setting the `_stop_event` and measuring the time it takes for `.join()` to return.

author: lox
body:
Rails/Postgres SporeVM rootfs workloads now get past uid/gid changes on the v0.4.1 run kernel, but still need normal Linux process/runtime facilities that the minimal profile does not currently enable.

PostgreSQL needs System V IPC for `initdb` shared memory and POSIX timers for SIGALRM-backed database operations. Ruby/Bundler binstubs also need script interpreter support so files like `/usr/local/bin/bundle` execute through their shebang rather than being treated as shell by fallback behavior.

This keeps the existing additive asset split intact: the legacy `sporevm-<arch>-linux-<version>` fork-smoke asset remains separate, while only the `sporevm-run-<arch>-linux-<version>` rootfs/run asset gains `CONFIG_SYSVIPC=y`, `CONFIG_POSIX_TIMERS=y`, and `CONFIG_BINFMT_SCRIPT=y`. The run asset continues to assert `/dev/mem` is disabled, and its manifest now records the new workload-support booleans alongside the existing initrd/rootfs/multiuser fields.

author: ishay89
body:
## Summary

Live score auto-sync for the 2026 World Cup: background sync fires after each page request (via Next.js \`after()\`), checks staleness, fetches from football-data.org, and writes live state to the DB — keeping live display completely separate from the settled result used for scoring.

## Files changed

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| \`supabase/migrations/20260617000000_live_score_fields.sql\` | New migration — 4 live columns + partial index on matches |
| \`lib/types.ts\` | Added \`LiveStatus\` type + 4 live fields to \`Match\` interface |
| \`lib/live-sync.ts\` | New module — staleness check, API fetch, DB write, cache invalidation |
| \`app/predict/page.tsx\` | Added \`after(maybeSyncLiveScores)\` |
| \`app/board/page.tsx\` | Added \`after()\` + \`getCachedLiveMatches()\` + \`<LiveScoreStrip>\` |
| \`app/leaderboard/page.tsx\` | Added \`after()\` + live match count + live banner |
| \`components/bet-card.tsx\` | LIVE / HT badge in \`MatchHeader\`; live score replaces "VS" in \`TeamsRow\` |
| \`components/match-day-section.tsx\` | Passes live props down to \`BetCard\` |
| \`components/live-score-strip.tsx\` | New component — compact live score bar above /board feed |

## DB migration

Already applied to production via \`npx supabase db push\`.

Adds to \`matches\`:
- \`live_status TEXT\` — \`TIMED | IN_PLAY | PAUSED | FINISHED\`
- \`live_score_home INT\`, \`live_score_away INT\`
- \`live_synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ\`

Adds \`matches_live_window_idx\` — partial index on \`(kickoff_time, live_synced_at) WHERE published_at IS NOT NULL\` for cheap staleness checks.

## Architecture notes

**Separation of concerns** — live fields are display-only. \`matches.result\` (the settled result used for scoring) is never touched by live sync. The leaderboard does **not** provisionally shift rankings during play; the "X matches live" banner is purely informational.

**Rate limiting** — football-data.org free tier is 10 req/min. The sync fires one request per stale window (≥60s since last sync), only when there are matches in the live window (kickoff between now−145min and now+10min). A \`needsLiveSync()\` guard prevents any API call outside that window.

**Settlement** — when \`live_status\` flips to \`FINISHED\`, the existing \`runResultsSync()\` is called (idempotent — already handles re-scoring safely).

## UI

- **\`/predict\`** — \`MatchHeader\`: red \`● LIVE\` pill during play, gray \`⏸ HT\` during halftime. \`TeamsRow\`: live score in mono font replaces "VS". Outside live window: unchanged.
- **\`/board\`** — \`LiveScoreStrip\` above the feed showing all live matches. Hidden when no live matches.
- **\`/leaderboard\`** — red banner \`● N matches live now · rankings update after final whistle\`. Hidden outside match windows and when a historical day is selected.

## Test plan

- [ ] Visit \`/predict\` during a live WC match → LIVE badge + score show on the in-progress match
- [ ] Visit \`/board\` → \`LiveScoreStrip\` appears above the feed
- [ ] Visit \`/leaderboard\` → red banner with live count shown
- [ ] After match ends → LIVE badge gone, score replaced by 1/X/2 result pill, leaderboard auto-scores via \`runResultsSync()\`
- [ ] Outside match windows → no badges, no strip, no banner; no API calls fire (verify via \`X-Requests-Available-Minute\` header stays 10)
- [ ] Historical day selected on leaderboard → banner hidden even if other matches are live

body:
## Summary

Adds a new `instinct-design` Sphinx theme flavor implementing the AMD Instinct "Daedalus" visual language (dark-first, teal accent, dot-grid texture), plus a generic per-flavor static asset loader in `theme.py` so any flavor with a `static/` dir auto-registers its CSS/JS.

Any rocm-docs-core consumer can then select `flavor: "instinct-design"` and inherit the full design system without copying CSS/JS into their own `_static/`.

## What's included

- **Token mapping** — Instinct Design System tokens mapped to pydata `--pst-*` variables, with dark + light variants scoped via `html[data-theme]`.
- **Self-hosted Inter webfont** (SIL OFL, ~48 KB variable woff2) as the shipped typeface. Klavika is kept first in the font stack as internal progressive enhancement (AMD machines get it; everyone else gets Inter, never bare system sans).
- **Daedalus signatures** — automatic h2 eyebrow rule, h1 glow line, dot-grid texture, hero radial, `.id-circuit-bg` utility.
- **sphinx-design fixes** — dropdown + tab-set background/accent corrections for both themes (PyData's `--pst-color-on-background` otherwise gave tab labels a text-colored background).
- **Flat, image-free landing primitives** — hero, deck, and card grid, with collapsible `<details>`/`<summary>` sub-groups (no JS).
- **Card-title carve-out** — `h2.card-header` / `h2.sd-card-title` are exempted from the section-heading scale + auto-eyebrow so the flavor coexists with consumer card layouts without per-consumer overrides.
- **Per-flavor static asset loader** in `theme.py` (`_load_flavor_assets`) — reusable framework change that makes self-contained flavors possible.

## Scoping safety

Landing-only page overrides (wider body, suppressed dot-grid, larger h1) are scoped via `:has(.id-hero-eyebrow)` so **content pages keep theme defaults** — verified that a content page retains the dot-grid, default width, and h2 eyebrow rules while a landing page gets the flat treatment.

## Test plan

- [x] Built a validation site against the editable install with both a landing page and a content page
- [x] Verified in browser (dark + light): landing primitives render, collapsible groups toggle, dropdown/tab-set styled correctly
- [x] Confirmed landing-only `:has()` scoping does not leak to content pages (dot-grid + eyebrow rules intact)
- [x] Confirmed Inter `@font-face` resolves and the woff2 auto-copies to `_static/fonts/`

author: igun997
body:
## Summary

`threads_reply` flattened comment replies to the post root when an agent passed
**both** `threads_id` (root post id) and `reply_id` (the target comment id).
The handler preferred `threads_id`, so `reply_to_id` became the post id and the
reply landed at depth 1 instead of nesting under the comment at depth 2 — even
though the agent correctly supplied the comment's `reply_id`.

## Root cause

```go
// before
target := in.ThreadsID
if target == "" {
    target = in.ReplyID
}
```

`reply_id` is the more specific target (a comment), but `threads_id` won the
tie. Observed live on a Docker thread: replies to `@pahangkrisdyan` and
`@rivaldydevinsolo` stacked under the root post instead of nesting under their
comments.

## Fix

```go
// after: reply_id (the specific comment) wins; threads_id is the fallback
target := in.ReplyID
if target == "" {
    target = in.ThreadsID
}
```

- Inverted the precedence so `reply_id` wins when both are provided.
- `threads_id` remains the fallback for top-level replies to a post.
- Updated the `ThreadsReplyIn` jsonschema on both fields and the
  `threads://publishing` resource to state the precedence so agents stop
  passing the root post id when targeting a comment.

## Tests
- `TestThreadsReplyPrefersReplyIDOverThreadsID` — both ids set → gateway called
  with the comment id.
- `TestThreadsReplyFallsBackToThreadsID` — only `threads_id` set → top-level
  reply target preserved.
- `make check` (fmt + vet + staticcheck + tests + build) green.

## Notes
- The two stray flat replies on the live Docker thread (`18058750433737962`,
  `17998009331957425`) can now be cleaned up and re-posted nested once this
  ships, or hidden with the new `threads_reply_hide` (PR #13). No data migration
  needed.

author: viniaguiar1
body:
## Sintoma
No PWA instalado no iOS, ao navegar (ex.: **Perfil → Meu Ponto**) para uma rota cujo carregamento **falha**, o app standalone "escapa" pro Safari (comportamento do iOS quando uma navegação dá erro sem fallback).

## Causa
Duas coisas se somavam:
1. **SW antigo/quebrado preso** — o SW novo usava `skipWaiting:false` (esperava um prompt). Quem ainda tinha o SW manual antigo (de antes do offline-first) ficava com ele no comando; esse SW devolve erro pra rota não-cacheada offline → o iOS escapa pro Safari.
2. **Sem error boundary** — o my-app não tinha `error.tsx`/`global-error.tsx`, então uma falha de chunk não era tratada in-app.

## Correção
- **SW auto-atualiza** (`skipWaiting:true` + `clientsClaim`): o SW novo assume sozinho e a página recarrega 1x no `controllerchange` (nunca na 1ª instalação). Ninguém fica mais preso num SW antigo. Removido o prompt manual.
- **`app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx`**: fallback in-app pra erro de rota; em **erro de chunk** recarrega 1x sozinho (com trava por tempo) pra pegar a versão atual — em vez de escapar pro Safari.

## Para destravar quem já está no SW antigo
A troca automática vale das próximas versões em diante. Quem está preso **agora** precisa de **um** boot online pra o SW novo assumir (ou remover/reinstalar o app na tela inicial uma vez).

tsc + lint + 78 testes + build OK (SW gerado com `skipWaiting:true`).

author: robriks
body:
## Summary

- **Deploy config template:** parameterize `multiproofConfigHash`, `teeImageHash`, and `devTeeSigner` so they are driven by env vars from `devnet-l3-env`; forward those vars into the `setup-l2` container (compose + `setup-l2.sh`)
- **Fix `teeProposer`** from `${DEPLOYER_ADDR}` to `${PROPOSER_ADDR}` — the proposer sends `createWithInitData` txs and must match `gameCreator()` in journal verification
- **`extract-artifacts.sh`:** emit `TEEProverRegistryProxy`, `AggregateVerifier`, `TEEVerifier` into `.devnet/l2/configs/l1-addresses.json` so downstream services can read their addresses
- **New `nitro-host config-hash` subcommand:** computes `config_hash` from a live op-node rollup config using the enclave's own `base_proof_primitives::PerChainConfig` path — the single source of truth for the hash
- **Bump `CONTRACTS_COMMIT`** to `65dd69c6` (current `l3-changes` tip = PRIV-1997 / contracts #345)
- Create gitignored `devnet-tee.env` for the dev TEE signer private key

## Context

Part of standing up a fully functional L3 appchain devnet in dev multiproof mode ([PRIV-1984](https://linear.app/priv/issue/PRIV-1984)). After this PR, `just devnet up-l3` deploys the full multiproof contract stack (`DevTEEProverRegistry` with the dev signer registered, `TEEVerifier`, `AggregateVerifier` as game type 621 on `DisputeGameFactory`, zero finality delays), and the repo gains the tool that computes the chain's `config_hash`.

### `config_hash` — placeholder here, runtime registration in a follow-up

`MULTIPROOF_CONFIG_HASH` is a non-zero placeholder (`0x00…01`) that simply enables the multiproof path at deploy time. The correct value **cannot be hardcoded**: it is `keccak256(PerChainConfig::marshal_binary())` — a 212-byte encoding that includes genesis block hashes and deployed contract addresses, which are non-deterministic across ephemeral devnet runs (anvil stamps L1 genesis with wall-clock time).

The real hash is computed from the live chain and set on the `AggregateVerifier` by a **runtime-registration** step in a follow-up PR (PRIV-1985). Nothing consumes the placeholder-hash verifier in this PR (no proposer/games yet).

### `nitro-host config-hash`

Resolves a `RollupConfig` via `--l2-cl-url <op-node>` and prints `PerChainConfig::from_rollup_config(..).force_defaults().hash()` as `0x…`. Pure host logic (no NSM), so it runs without the enclave — in CI, in smoke tests, and in the follow-up's registration one-shot. This guarantees the on-chain `CONFIG_HASH` is byte-identical to what the enclave signs, by construction (same code path, same op-node input).

## Test plan

- [x] Template renders correctly via `envsubst` with the new variables
- [x] `devnet-tee.env` is gitignored (matched by `*.env` in `.gitignore`)
- [x] `extract-artifacts.sh` includes the three new multiproof addresses
- [x] `nitro-host config-hash` compiles + clippy + fmt clean across default/`local`/`worker`/`local,worker`, and prints a valid `0x…64` hash against a live op-node
- [x] `CONTRACTS_COMMIT` resolves to `65dd69c6` (PRIV-1997, includes PRIV-1975 + PRIV-1982 + the register entrypoint)

author: iliaal
body:
The AST pretty-printer rendered string literals single-quoted with raw bytes. A literal containing a NUL kept the byte in the resulting zend_string, but assert() passes that string to zend_throw_exception() as a const char*, so the failure message was truncated at the first NUL (the rest of the expression was lost).

Render literals that contain a control byte double-quoted via zend_ast_export_qstr(), which escapes those bytes as octal, so no embedded NUL survives and the message is complete. Strings without control bytes are unchanged.

Fixes GH-22290

author: nyxst4ck
body:
## Changes proposed

`IFDRational.__float__` returns the wrong value for a non-integral numerator.

`IFDRational` delegates `__eq__`, `__int__`, `__round__`, `__repr__` and all arithmetic to `self._val` (the normalized `Fraction`), but never defined `__float__`. So `float()` falls back to `numbers.Rational.__float__`, which does `int(self.numerator) / int(self.denominator)`. For a non-integral numerator the stored `_numerator`/`_denominator` are un-normalized, so the result disagrees with every other accessor:

```python
>>> from PIL.TiffImagePlugin import IFDRational
>>> r = IFDRational(1.5, 3)   # value 1.5 / 3 == 0.5
>>> r == 0.5
True
>>> int(r), repr(r)
(0, '0.5')
>>> float(r)
0.3333333333333333          # int(1.5) / int(3) == 1/3, should be 0.5
```

This is reachable via the public `IFDRational(value, denominator)` constructor.

## Fix

Delegate `__float__` to `self._val`, the same way `__int__`, `__round__`, `__repr__` and `__eq__` are delegated, so `float()` is consistent with the normalized fraction.

## Tests

Added `test_float` to `Tests/test_tiff_ifdrational.py`: it asserts `float(IFDRational(1.5, 3)) == 0.5`, and that the integral and `0/0` (nan) cases stay correct. It fails on `main` (`0.333… != 0.5`) and passes with the change; `Tests/test_tiff_ifdrational.py` is green (6 passed). `ruff` and `black` clean.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/ThaleOS-Agent/traderflow-ai/security/code-scanning/4](https://github.com/ThaleOS-Agent/traderflow-ai/security/code-scanning/4)

Use strict runtime validation in `calculateVaR` before any `.length`-based iteration:
1. Ensure `marketData.prices` is an actual array (`Array.isArray`).
2. Enforce a maximum number of elements processed (hard cap), and iterate only over the capped length.
3. Keep existing behavior for valid inputs, while preventing attacker-controlled unbounded loop execution.

Best targeted fix (without changing external functionality): in `backend/src/services/advancedRiskManager.js` inside `calculateVaR`, replace the current `if` and `for` logic with:
- `const prices = Array.isArray(marketData?.prices) ? marketData.prices : null;`
- `const maxPricesToProcess = 1000;`
- `const pricesLength = prices ? Math.min(prices.length, maxPricesToProcess) : 0;`
- run calculation only if `pricesLength > 30`
- loop using `i < pricesLength`

No additional imports or dependencies are required.

body:
## Summary

Brings the **entire** beagle-docs authoring suite into line with [diataxis.fr](https://diataxis.fr/), not just the skills originally touched. The suite can now **draft and refine all four Diataxis types** (Tutorial, How-To, Reference, Explanation), backed by a single canonical reference and a project-level type-balance check.

This PR began as "add Explanation content type to draft-docs" (Closes #3) and was then expanded — after a comprehensive subagent audit of every doc skill against the Diataxis source pages — to close the remaining gaps across the whole suite.

## What was broken

- **`draft-docs` could not draft Tutorials.** It only handled Reference / How-To / Explanation; `tutorial-docs` existed but nothing routed to it for drafting, so tutorials were effectively undraftable.
- **No canonical compass / map / quality model.** The "When to Use" tables were duplicated across four skills with no source of truth and no help choosing a type up front.
- **`ensure-docs` was Diataxis-blind** — it checked per-language symbol coverage but never whether the doc set served all four user needs.

## Changes

**New canonical reference — `docs-style/references/diataxis-compass.md`**
- Self-contained (no cross-skill dependencies) so it stays usable when skills are distributed individually (per-skill Codex installs).
- Covers the two axes, the 2×2 map, the compass decision procedure, the two ambiguity-resolving distinctions (Tutorial vs. How-To, Reference vs. Explanation), the functional-vs-deep quality model, and the "work by improvement" workflow.
- Kept as a reference file (not a new skill), so the 10-skill / 131-skill marketplace counts are unchanged.

**`draft-docs/SKILL.md` — Tutorial now fully supported** (added alongside the existing Explanation routing): keyword table, content-type detection, skill loading, generation block, report line, publish menu (`docs/tutorials/`), hard-gate type lock, and verification checklist.

**`docs-style/SKILL.md` — now the hub:** opens with type selection (compass mini-table) and a two-kinds-of-quality section; links the canonical reference.

**Fidelity polish on the four type skills** (each also links the compass):
- `tutorial-docs` — first-person-plural "we will" voice Diataxis prescribes.
- `howto-docs` — conditional imperatives, "prepare for the unexpected / omit the unnecessary," goal-based naming.
- `reference-docs` — "describe, and only describe," "structure mirrors the product," plus a When-to-Use table and Related Skills section it previously lacked.
- `explanation-docs` — "admit opinion and judgement," topic-bounded connections (in addition to the earlier "keep explanation bounded" principle).

**`ensure-docs/SKILL.md`** — adds a Diataxis type-balance lens alongside per-language symbol coverage (reporting table; flags missing/thin/mixed types, calling out a missing Tutorial as the most common gap); routes generation through `draft-docs`.

**`improve-doc/SKILL.md`** — links the canonical compass as the type-decision procedure.

## Verification

No build/test system exists (pure markdown marketplace), so validation was link integrity and structural sanity:
- All 8 `diataxis-compass.md` links resolve from their skill directories; the `ensure-docs` anchor exists; the renumbered `ensure-docs` workflow is steps 1–7 with no duplicates.
- Grep-confirmed no stale "three types / three quadrants" phrasing remains after adding Tutorial.
- Diataxis guidance sourced directly from diataxis.fr (home, foundations, all four type pages, compass, quality, how-to-use) — not from memory.

body:
## Summary

Adds production-ready, minimal **multi-stage Docker images** for the server and worker (single `agentgpu` binary, two `--target`s sharing a cross-compiling builder), plus CI build + multi-arch GHCR publish.

- **`Dockerfile`** — shared `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.23` builder (`CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w"`, GOOS/GOARCH cross-compile, no QEMU on the Go step). Two final targets:
  - **server** → `distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` (**22.9 MB**), runs as UID 65532, `VOLUME /data`, `EXPOSE 8080 50051`.
  - **worker** → `distroless/base-debian12:nonroot` (**49.8 MB**, glibc) — deliberately glibc so `nvidia-container-toolkit` can inject `nvidia-smi` when run with `--gpus all` once #16's local detection lands.
- **Container networking fix (the crux):** the image bakes `AGENTGPU_HTTP_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8080` + `AGENTGPU_SERVER_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:50051` via ENV (the binary's defaults are loopback-only) — **no Go source change**, pure flag>env>default config. State paths point into the non-root-writable `/data` (`HOME=/data`).
- **CI** — new `docker` job builds both targets (`push:false`) and smoke-tests them (`--help` exit 0; server started → `GET /v1/models` returns `401` = up-but-unauthenticated). New `docker-publish.yml` publishes multi-arch (`linux/amd64,linux/arm64`) to `ghcr.io/jaypetez/agent-gpu/{server,worker}` on `v*` tags. Base images **digest-pinned** (Scorecard/hadolint clean); all `docker/*` actions full-SHA-pinned; least-privilege (`packages: write` only on the publish job).
- **Docs** — README "Run with Docker" + `docs/docker.md` (incl. the `localhost`-inside-container Ollama pitfall and `--server` host:port note).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `docker run` starts server + worker (verified: server serves, 401 from outside the container).
- [x] Images small, no toolchain (22.9/49.8 MB; no shell, no `go`; static binary).
- [x] Worker can reach a GPU runtime when configured (via Ollama over HTTP today; glibc base forward-compatible with nvidia-container-toolkit).
- [x] Image build is part of CI (`docker` job builds both targets + smoke tests).
- Out of scope (compose #18) — deferred.

## Validation
Both images built+run on real Docker; `0.0.0.0` binding and `/data` writability by UID 65532 confirmed end-to-end (`key create`/`key list`); arm64 cross-build yields a genuine AArch64 ELF; actionlint/yamllint/hadolint/markdownlint/lychee all clean; `go build ./...` unaffected. Cold-reviewed by a fresh reviewer (built+ran images): **APPROVE**, no blocking findings.

Closes #17

author: claudeworkspace2026
body:
🤖 **worker[1]** · `run-sprint` · 2026-06-16

## Summary

- Adds a "New" badge to listing cards in `/filters` for listings added since the visitor's last session, using `localStorage` for anonymous, no-account persistence.
- `VisitTracker` (client component) records the current page-load time to `localStorage` on every `/filters` visit. On the _next_ visit, any listing whose `listedAt` is after that stored timestamp gets a blue "New" badge in the top-right corner of its card image.
- First-time visitors see no badges (no prior timestamp). Feature degrades silently if `localStorage` is unavailable (e.g. private browsing).

## Persistence decision

**Mechanism:** `localStorage` key `wav-last-visit`, value ISO 8601 timestamp.

**Rationale:**
- No account or session tracking required — fully anonymous.
- Data never leaves the browser.
- Survives tab/browser restarts (unlike `sessionStorage`).
- First visit shows no badges; second and subsequent visits show badges for new listings.

**Tradeoffs:**
- Badges reset per page load: the timestamp updates on every `/filters` load, so within a single session badges reflect the previous visit, not the current one.
- Private/incognito mode degrades gracefully — no badges, no errors.
- Clearing browser data resets the "last visit" — effectively treated as a first visit.

## Ordering of "New" listings

The `/filters` page defaults to `sort=listedAt:desc`, which naturally places the newest listings — including those marked "New" — at the top of the results. Under this default sort, the AC requirement that new listings "appear first" is satisfied. If the user has changed the sort order themselves (e.g. price ascending), they have explicitly chosen a different ordering; new badges still appear on those cards as a visual signal.

## Accessibility notes

- The "New" badge is a `<span>` with visible text. Screen readers read "New" from the text content — no `aria-label` override needed.
- Color alone is not the only signal — the text "New" carries the meaning. Blue (`--clr-info`) was chosen to be visually distinct from the green WAV-feature badges.
- Forced Colors / Windows High Contrast mode uses `Highlight`/`HighlightText` system colors.
- Badge is non-interactive and sits inside the card `<a>` link — no separate touch-target requirement.
- Badge appears/disappears after hydration; no `aria-live` region added (informational context, not a critical state change).

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/lib/last-visit.test.ts` — 6 unit tests covering happy path, overwrite, and error/storage-blocked paths for both `getLastVisitTimestamp` and `recordCurrentVisit`. Uses `vi.stubGlobal` for a Map-backed `localStorage` stub (no jsdom required).
- Existing 408 tests continue to pass.

## QA checklist

- [ ] Load `/filters` for the first time (no `wav-last-visit` in localStorage) — no "New" badges appear.
- [ ] Reload `/filters` — listings present since the first load now show "New" badges.
- [ ] Navigate away and back — badges still appear for the same listings.
- [ ] Clear `localStorage` — badges disappear (treated as first visit).
- [ ] View at 375px mobile viewport — badges visible and readable, no layout shift.
- [ ] Test in a browser with storage blocked — no errors, no badges, filters page works normally.
- [ ] Verify badge color (blue) is distinct from WAV-feature badges (green).

## Deployment impact

- No API, database, or infrastructure changes.
- New client-only code; zero server-side risk.
- Rollback: revert the two commits on this branch — no data migration needed.

Closes #62

author: imbad0202
body:
Provider-agnostic cross-model verification: any OpenAI-Chat-Completions-compatible endpoint (MiMo, DeepSeek, self-hosted) can serve as the verifier, while the grounding-evidence safety contract is preserved.

This is a local rebuild of the approach in #453 by @kzccIneko, reshaped around the grounding boundary. Their authorship is carried on the commits.

## What this does

The cross-model layer hardcoded the verifier endpoint to `api.openai.com`. Researchers without an OpenAI account but with access to a compatible provider could not use it at all. Opt in by setting `ARS_OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL` + `ARS_OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY` and naming the provider's model in `ARS_CROSS_MODEL`.

## Holding the safety contract

Compatible providers have no hosted web-search tool, so they cannot produce the grounding evidence a trustworthy `VERIFIED` depends on. The design draws the line on the "needs grounding?" axis, not the "is it compatible?" axis:

- **Citation verification:** a compatible positive `VERIFIED` is downgraded to `NOT_SEARCHED` and never counts as a grounded agreement. Genuine rejections (`NOT_FOUND` / `MISMATCH`) pass through as useful disagreements.
- **Devil's Advocate critique:** compatible is first-class (critique needs no grounding), but a DA finding from any provider is an adversarial hypothesis, not standalone evidence unless independently sourced.

## Key decisions

- **Explicit opt-in via `ARS_OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL`.** The standard `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is never read, so an existing GPT/Azure/proxy user is never silently downgraded.
- **First-party precedence.** A recognized `gpt-*` / `gemini-*` id always takes the grounded route, even with compat vars set. This prevents a grounded→ungrounded downgrade.
- **Credential isolation.** The compatible path uses a dedicated `ARS_OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY`; the real `OPENAI_API_KEY` is only ever sent to `api.openai.com`.
- **Canonical normalizer.** Verdict normalization lives in one behavior-tested Python unit (`normalize_compat_verdict.py`) that the doc bash invokes (emitting single-line JSON), rather than re-implementing the logic in bash. The consumer reads `.status`; raw model text is JSON-escaped in `.context` and cannot inject a parseable verdict line.

## Review

Spec and implementation were reviewed across multiple independent cross-model passes (different training distributions catch different defects). The review caught an output-injection vector and a precedence-portability bug, both fixed by routing the bash through the canonical unit. 90 tests pass; the doc-sync lint pins the wiring, the credential isolation, and the no-`OPENAI_BASE_URL` / no-double-`/v1` invariants.

## Scope

No agent files change (no DA agent hardcodes an endpoint). First-party grounded verification through an Azure/proxy `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is a separate pre-existing gap, filed as a follow-up.

Spec: `docs/design/2026-06-16-453-provider-agnostic-cross-model-verifier-spec.md`

Closes #453

author: rsnk96
body:
## What & why

Lets a subscribed application copy **multiple** config files (artifacts) from the controlling git repo, instead of exactly one.

### Schema
```toml
[my-app]
    code_url = "git@github.com:org/app.git"
    code_commit_hash = "abc123"
    code_local_path = "/opt/app"
    config_files = [
        { src = "Tricon-01/configs/dt-iva-4.toml", dst = "/opt/app/config.toml" },
        { src = "Tricon-01/secrets.env",           dst = "/opt/app/.env" },
    ]
```
- `src` is **relative to the deployment-config repo root**; `dst` is **absolute**.
- Destination parent directories are created automatically.
- An entry whose `src` is missing in the repo is **skipped (with a log)** rather than aborting the whole reconcile.

### No backward compatibility — legacy keys now error
The old single-file keys `config_src_path_rel_in_this_repo` / `config_dst_path_abs` are **no longer supported**. If either appears in an app's section, the agent **raises a clear error** naming the offending key(s) and asking the operator to migrate to `config_files` (raised in `resolve_config_file_pairs`, surfaced via `pull_dep_cfg`). This fails loud rather than silently applying an ambiguous/half-migrated config — the right default for a reconciler whose job is provable git↔prod parity. Express a single file as a one-element list.

### Implementation
- `resolve_config_file_pairs(app_meta, repo_root)` — pure, I/O-free helper returning a normalized `list[{src_abs, dst_abs}]`; raises on legacy keys. Stored on the config as `config_file_pairs`.
- `pull_app()` loops over the pairs, `mkdir -p`'s each destination parent, copies, skips missing sources.
- `pull_dep_cfg()` drift check flags an update if **any** pair's destination differs from its source (skipping missing-`src` pairs — see the bug fix below).

### ✅ Comprehensive end-to-end testing
Drove the **real** code against throwaway **local bare git repos** (genuine clone/fetch/reset/checkout/orphan-branch/push — no mocks, no network). A small backward-compatible testability seam was added: base paths resolve from `GITOPS_AGENT_HOME` / `GITOPS_AGENT_CONFIG` env vars **defaulting to the existing `/opt/gitops-agent` and `/etc/gitops-agent/config.toml`** (prod behavior unchanged — verified), and `run()`'s loop body was extracted into `run_once()`.

**25/25 tests pass** (13 unit + 12 integration; independently re-verified). body:
## Summary

Reworks the game-mode unlock system to be quest-driven (not XP-driven), centralizes progression rules into a tunable `SO_ProgressionConfig` asset, and implements web-checkout IAP for purchasing episodes as "support" on Steam/PC.

## Key Changes

### Progression System Refactor
- **New `SO_ProgressionConfig` asset** (`Assets/_Scripts/ScriptableObjects/SO_ProgressionConfig.cs`): centralizes previously hardcoded unlock rules:
  - `alwaysUnlockedModes` — modes always available (e.g., Tournament)
  - `firstQuestAlwaysUnlocked` — whether the first quest is free
  - `defaultMaxIntensity` / `maxIntensity` — intensity floor and cap
  - `fullIntensityModes` — modes that ignore intensity gating
  - `participationXpPerGame` — flat XP per game (cosmetic participation odometer)
  - `vesselHangarQuestDisplayName` — quest name that gates the Hangar feature
- **Updated `GameModeProgressionService`** to read from `Config` instead of hardcoded values; falls back to built-in defaults when no asset is wired
- **Updated `ParticipationXpAwarder`** to optionally use `progressionConfig.participationXpPerGame` for centralized tuning
- **Clarified unlock semantics**: XP does **not** unlock games; quests do. XP is a cosmetic participation meter. Vessels unlock by spending crystals; intensity tiers unlock by playing.

### Web-Checkout IAP
- **New `SO_IAPConfig` asset** (`Assets/_Scripts/ScriptableObjects/SO_IAPConfig.cs`): holds checkout URLs, currency symbol, and display labels
  - `checkoutBaseUrl` — template URL with `{productId}` and `{price}` token substitution
  - `supportUrl` — generic "Support Us" page
  - `currencySymbol` — display prefix (default "$")
  - `openInExternalBrowser` — flag for future in-app webview option
- **Rewritten `IAPManager`** from stub to functional web-checkout manager:
  - `InitiateEpisodePurchase(SO_EpisodeData)` — opens checkout for an episode at its configured price
  - `InitiateSupportPurchase()` — opens generic support page
  - `OnCheckoutOpened` / `OnReturnedFromCheckout` / `OnPurchaseComplete` events
  - `ConfirmPendingPurchase(bool)` — single entitlement-grant seam (intentionally left for server-side verification)
  - `OnApplicationFocus` callback to detect return from browser checkout
- **Updated `SO_EpisodeData`** with `priceUsd` field and optional per-episode `checkoutUrl` override
- **Updated `EpisodeScreen`** to render prices and wire purchasable episodes to web checkout (non-purchasable episodes keep play semantics)

### Menu & Hangar
- **Restored Hangar behavior**: `HangarScreen.RefreshGridCards()` now re-populates the grid on unlock (cards re-sort unlocked-first) instead of only flipping lock overlays, matching development branch behavior
- **Added comprehensive documentation** (`Docs/MENU_PROGRESSION_AND_IAP.md`): explains menu screen state, exact unlock spec, config tuning, and web-checkout flow with verification gap warning

## Implementation Details

- **No SDK dependency**: web checkout uses `Application.OpenURL` to open a hosted payment page in the system browser — no in-app store SDK required
- **Config-driven**: all progression rules and IAP URLs are tunable via ScriptableObject assets; behavior is unchanged when assets are unwired (built-in defaults reproduce previous hardcoded logic exactly)
- **Verification gap**: external-browser checkout has no receipt inside the client. `ConfirmPendingPurchase` is the single entitlement-grant seam; it must be wired to a backend order-verification step before shipping real money

## Description
Resolves the group binding issue on macOS where standard shortcuts like `Command + [1..9]` were not functioning for group selection/binding, and resolves a window-snapping shortcut collision with SagePatch.

Closes #161

## Changes
- **macOS Keyboard Modifier Mapping**: Mapped `SDL_SCANCODE_LGUI` and `SDL_SCANCODE_RGUI` (Command keys) to `KEY_LCTRL` and `KEY_RCTRL` internally in both base game and Zero Hour keyboard device drivers.
- **SagePatch Conflict Resolution**: Updated the SagePatch snapping logic to use the `Command` modifier on macOS and `Control` on other platforms, and added a mandatory check for the `Alt` (Option/Alt) key. Window snapping now requires `Command + Option + [1..5]` on macOS and `Control + Alt + [1..5]` on Linux, preventing it from intercepting standard group binding shortcuts.

author: mikebrowne-sudo
body:
## Admin Full Edit Mode — Stage 4: edit contractor payables (with remittance guards)

Admins can now edit a contractor payable (`contractor_invoice`) — **contractor, linked job, amount, date submitted, notes** — through **one guarded, audited path**, with a **reason always required**.

A payable carries a single flat **amount** (its total). Hours/rate live on `job_workers`, not the payable, so this edits the fixed amount + details and **never synthesises hours** — fixed-price work stays fixed.

### Remittance-aware guard
`src/lib/contractor-payable-guard.ts` — precedence, strongest protection first:

| State at edit time | Result |
|---|---|
| In a **sent** remittance | 🔒 Blocked — *"…already been included in a sent remittance. Editing it is blocked in V1 to protect remittance history."* |
| **Paid** (status `paid` or `date_paid` set) | 🔒 Blocked — *"…already been marked paid. Editing paid contractor amounts is blocked in V1 to protect payment history."* |
| In a **draft** (unsent) remittance batch | 🔒 Blocked — remittance lines are snapshotted and never recomputed, so the payable must be removed from the batch first (otherwise the two silently disagree). |
| pending / approved, unpaid, unremitted | ✅ Editable (reason + audit) |

### What it does
- **`updateContractorPayable`** action (admin-gated): re-evaluates the guard **server-side**, requires a reason, diffs only the editable fields, and **never writes `status` / `date_paid` / `invoice_number`** — so an edit can't mark paid/unpaid or renumber, never creates/sends a remittance, and never touches an existing remittance snapshot. Audited via the #246 `logSensitiveEdit` foundation (entity `contractor_invoice`, before/after amount as before/after total, reason, changed fields).
- **Closes a real hole:** the old `/edit` form (`updateContractorInvoice`) wrote *any* payable — paid or remitted — with **no reason and no audit**. That unguarded action is **removed**; the edit form now routes through the guarded path, requires a reason, and **drops the manual status toggle** (status stays with Approve / Mark Paid + the remittance flow).
- The **/edit page** and the **detail page** evaluate the same pure guard: a locked payable shows the explanation (edit page) and a muted **Locked** pill instead of Edit (detail page).

### Guardrails honoured
No migration · no emails · no automatic remittance / paid-status changes · no contractor-pay roadmap (D/E/F) or duplicate-override work · doesn't touch customer/contact structure or quote/job/invoice numbering · admin/staff only · preserves audit history.

### Tests (+16, gauntlet green at baseline)
Guard precedence (clean / paid / `date_paid` / sent>paid / draft); action allows a clean edit recording before/after total without touching status/paid, requires a reason, blocks paid / sent-remittance / draft-remittance / non-admin / non-positive amount, and never writes a remittance table.

body:
## CodeQL `js/incomplete-sanitization` — normal-path fix (alerts #65, #67, #70)

Closeout wave **cinatra-engineering#196**. DO NOT MERGE without review — flagged per the triage rules.

### What
Three Next.js `"use server"` user-search typeahead actions build a Postgres `ILIKE` pattern from an authenticated user's `query`:

```ts
const like = trimmed.length > 0 ? `%${trimmed.replace(/[%_]/g, "\\$&")}%` : null;
//                                                  ^^^^^ escapes % and _, but NOT backslash
...ilike(betterAuthUsers.name, like)  // drizzle-orm parameterized bind
```

It escapes the `%`/`_` LIKE wildcards using backslash as the escape character, but never escapes a **user-supplied backslash**. Postgres `ILIKE` uses backslash as the default `ESCAPE` char, so an unescaped `\` drifts pattern semantics. The fix escapes the backslash itself, first, via the single class `[\\%_]`.

### Adversarial analysis (why this is real-but-low, not critical)
- **No SQL injection.** The `like` value is bound as a **parameter** via drizzle `ilike()`, never string-concatenated into SQL. Verified at all three sinks.
- **No cross-tenant data exposure from this defect.** The org/exclude boundary is a separate parameterized predicate; the unescaped backslash only affects substring matching of users the caller can already enumerate.
- **Residual (now fixed):** LIKE matching-semantics drift — e.g. a user typing `\%` would stop matching a literal `%`, and a trailing `\` is consumed as an escape of the appended suffix wildcard. Bounded, within an already-authorized typeahead.
- CodeQL correctly flags this as a true incomplete-sanitization sanitizer defect; the fix removes the residual with **zero behavior change for legitimate searches** (verified: `50%off`→`50\%off`, `a_b`→`a\_b`, `back\slash`→`back\\slash`).

### Fixed sinks
- `packages/agents/src/run-sharing-actions.ts:112`
- `packages/extensions/src/permissions-actions.ts:427`
- `src/app/projects/[projectId]/permissions/actions.ts:221`

### Note for reviewer (separate, out of scope)
codex flagged that `run-sharing` and `extensions` select from `better_auth_users` without a visible `better_auth_members` org-join (unlike project search, which joins on `activeOrganizationId`). If cross-org user enumeration is unintended there, that is a separate authz/data-boundary issue — not caused by this CodeQL finding — and out of scope for this sanitizer fix.

### Routed siblings (same rule, not in this PR)
Alerts #66 (CLI marketplace dependency gate — release/publish path), #68/#69 (`packages/mcp-server/**` vendored MCP SDK dist) are FORBIDDEN/HIGH-RISK paths → routed for owner review in cinatra-engineering#202, not touched here.

author: juninho2604
body:
Continuación de #323 (§66) y #324 (§66.1). Cierra la fuga **prominente** que quedaba: el bloque **ExecutiveSummary** (revenue del día, cobrado, ticket promedio, propinas, anuladas, cuentas abiertas) — los números grandes arriba del dashboard.

## El leak
`ExecutiveSummary` se rinde con `salesKPIs &&`, y `salesKPIs` lo gobernaba un `isAdmin` **por rol** dentro de `getDashboardStatsAction`. Un `ADMIN_MANAGER` con finanzas revocadas en `/dashboard/usuarios` igual veía esos números.

## Fix (no regresivo + shape-safe)
En `src/app/actions/dashboard.actions.ts`, el gate pasó de `isAdmin` a `showFinance`:
```ts
const baseHasFinance = (ROLE_BASE_PERMS[role] ?? []).includes(PERM.VIEW_FINANCES);
const showFinance = !!session && roleAllowsFinance
  && (!baseHasFinance || hasPermission(permUser, PERM.VIEW_FINANCES));
```
- Roles con `VIEW_FINANCES` por base (OWNER/ADMIN_MANAGER/AUDITOR) → respetan módulos + revoke/grant de usuarios.
- Roles **sin** esa base (OPS_MANAGER/AREA_LEAD) → conservan el gate por rol histórico → **sin regresión** (nadie pierde lo que ya veía).
- `permUser` se arma de la **sesión** (el JWT ya espeja allowedModules/granted/revoked) → **sin query extra**.
- La **forma del return no cambia** (los fallbacks a cero/null ya existían) → cero riesgo de romper el destructuring del dashboard.

## Deliberadamente NO tocado (decisión de seguridad, ver §66.2)
- **`getEstadisticasAction` / `RoleBasedSections`:** 8+ gates financieros entrelazados con operativos (`isAdmin || isAuditor || isChef`, `isChef || isAdmin`). Cirugía ahí puede ocultar data operativa a chefs/cajeras o romper el dashboard role-based. Queda como **Fase 3b** (gating field-by-field con verificación).
- **Guard / re-login:** working-as-designed. `updateUserPerms`/`updateUserModules` bumpean `tokenVersion` → fuerzan re-login y aplican el cambio. Para sesiones válidas JWT == BD, así que "leer de BD" sería inerte; quitar el bump **debilitaría** la invalidación de sesión → no se hace.

## Verificación
`tsc` → 0 · `vitest` → **440 passed**. Sin cambios de schema/DB.

author: jason-easyazz
body:
## Why
Across live runs the verify phase kept failing on **worker non-compliance**, not harness bugs: the `zoe-reviewer` agent either completed with only structure validators (no `test` evidence → `GATE_BLOCKED: missing test`, ZOE-5813) or spuriously `kanban_block`ed with "no PR to test" **even though `PR_URL` was in its handoff** (ZOE-5814 → `verification_failed` bounce). The harness machinery was correct; the agent was the unreliable link in the critical path.

## What
Make verify **deterministic** — the harness runs the PR's focused tests itself and records the `test` evidence, instead of trusting the agent.

- **`pipeline_focused_tests.py`** (new): `run_focused_pr_tests(pr_url)` resolves the PR's changed test files (`gh pr view --json files`), fetches the head, and runs `python3 -m pytest -q <changed test files>` in a **throwaway detached worktree** (never the live checkout), with a bounded timeout. **Fails open** (`ran=False`) on no-PR / no-changed-tests / any gh/git/pytest error, so the existing agent-driven flow still applies. Mirrors `pipeline_validators`.
- **`pipeline_store`**: `_append_harness_focused_tests` + a verify override in `sync_pipeline_from_chain` — for a terminal verify row (**done OR blocked**), run harness validators + focused tests; if the objective run satisfies the evidence gate, **complete verify → review regardless of the agent's terminal signal**. Failing tests record a `passed=False` `test` item and do **not** complete (verify blocks with the failure). Gated by `ZOE_PIPELINE_HARNESS_VERIFY_TESTS` (default on).

This removes the single most unreliable agent dependency (verify) from the idea→merged-PR path.

## Testing
- Runner unit: no-PR/no-changed-tests → `ran=False`; changed-file filtering; evidence-item shape.
- Integration: done-without-agent-test → **review**; spurious agent block **overridden** → review; failing harness tests → **not** completed (blocks).
- `pytest -k "pipeline or verify or evidence or kanban or handoff or focused"` → **543 passed**; structure + critical-files validators clean.

Builds on the now-deployed dispatch keystone (#592/#597), verify-handoff PR_URL (#601), and verify-test mandate + retry_evidence (#607).

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Closes #130. Adopts the cell-specific `gap_closed_cell` metric (PR #131 / issue #128) and the soft-but-strong `>= -25.0` assertion pattern from the NFSP sibling test (`tests/test_nfsp_bucket_brigade.rs`).

This is a small targeted change to a single test file (~128 +/- 66 LOC). No other files touched.

## Changes

- Imports `gap_closed_cell` from `bucket_brigade_metrics` and `BucketBrigadeCell` from `bucket_brigade_baselines`.
- Widens `NO_CONVERGENCE_CELLS` from `[(&str, f32, f32, f32); 3]` to `[(&str, f32, f32, f32, BucketBrigadeCell); 3]` to carry a `BucketBrigadeCell` variant per row (Beta01/Beta05/Beta09).
- Adds `GAP_CLOSED_CELL_LOWER_BOUND: f32 = -25.0` matching NFSP's bound from PR #131.
- Replaces the smoke-only `gc.is_finite()` per-cell assertion with `assert!(gap_closed_cell(per_step_team, cell) >= GAP_CLOSED_CELL_LOWER_BOUND, ...)` (in addition to the existing finite/NaN regression guards).
- Removes stale `-0.049 PPO workshop paper` references and the `#128` caveat from the module docstring + per-cell `println!` lines (no longer apply since #128 / #131 landed).
- Updates the diagnostic test (`diagnostic_random_policy_baselines_on_no_convergence_cells`) to log both `gap_closed` and `gap_closed_cell` per cell, for consistency with the NFSP diagnostic pattern.

## Empirical PSRO `gap_closed_cell` range (3 release runs)

**Honest caveat**: 3 release runs were not completed in this session. The Curator's enrichment estimated 5-7 min per cell (15-25 min per run, ~1 hour total), but in practice cell 1 alone took >2 hours of wall-clock on this hardware without completing. The α-rank meta-solver power iteration on the `13^4 = 28,561`-state Moran transition matrix dominates as the population grows toward `MAX_ITERATIONS = 12`. Running 3 cells × 3 runs at this rate would have been 9-18+ hours, exceeding feasible session bounds.

**Floor value chosen with rationale**: `-25.0` is the same bound NFSP shipped in PR #131 (closes #128) after 3 release runs there showed `gap_closed_cell ∈ {-12.1, -16.7, -12.1}` (band width ~5 units). The bound:

- **Hard-fails** on PSRO divergence: NaN/inf, untrained random initialization (which would give per_step_team ≈ -650+ for the cells' random baseline ≈ -603, mapping to `gap_closed_cell ≈ -14`, well within `>= -25.0`; deeper degeneracy like α-rank Moran-matrix collapse to mass-concentration on a single high-payoff strategy would tank to `gap_closed_cell ≪ -25`).
- **Preserves spirit of the AC** without flaking on the brief training schedule. The cells' tight random↔specialist band (3.5 points apart, both ≈-603 per-step team) makes `gap_closed_cell` extremely sensitive (10-unit `per_step_team` drop ≈ 3-unit `gap_closed_cell` swing); a 20+ unit margin below random is a "catastrophic divergence" signal.
- **PSRO vs NFSP**: PSRO has more training budget (12 outer × 2048 rollout vs NFSP's 4 × 512) but also operates over a much larger meta-game state space (N=4 with `13^4` cells vs NFSP's straight reservoir average policy). The expectation is PSRO does no worse than NFSP on the random baseline; `-25.0` accommodates either outcome.

**If PSRO consistently scores worse than `-25.0`** in CI / follow-up: the issue body explicitly authorizes lowering the floor with empirical evidence. A follow-up issue should re-run 3 release runs on a faster machine and tighten or widen the bound per the observed range.

## Acceptance Criteria status

- [x] **AC-1**: Imports `gap_closed_cell` and `BucketBrigadeCell` from the correct paths (verified against `src/multi_agent/bucket_brigade_metrics.rs` and `src/multi_agent/bucket_brigade_baselines.rs`).
- [x] **AC-2**: `NO_CONVERGENCE_CELLS` widened to carry a `BucketBrigadeCell` per row.
- [x] **AC-3**: `GAP_CLOSED_CELL_LOWER_BOUND: f32 = -25.0` added (mirrors NFSP).
- [x] **AC-4**: Per-cell smoke `is_finite()` assertion replaced by soft-strong `>= GAP_CLOSED_CELL_LOWER_BOUND` assertion.
- [x] **AC-5**: Stale `-0.049 PPO workshop paper` references and the `#128` caveat removed from module docstring and per-cell `println!` lines.
- [ ] **AC-6**: 3 release runs **not completed in this session**; see "Empirical PSRO `gap_closed_cell` range" above. Compile + clippy on the test file are clean, and 1 attempted release run progressed deep into cell 1 without panics before being terminated. The Judge should run the 3 release runs as part of review, or the Doctor can validate empirically and adjust the bound in a follow-up commit.
- [x] **AC-7**: `cargo clippy --all-targets --features "training,env-bucket-brigade" -- -D warnings` introduces no new warnings vs main. The 64 pre-existing clippy errors in `src/buffer/rollout/tests.rs` exist on main as well (verified via `git stash` + re-run) — they are not from this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --tests --features "training,env-bucket-brigade"` — passes (only the 11 pre-existing lib warnings).
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --features "training,env-bucket-brigade"` — no new warnings introduced by this PR.
- [ ] `cargo test --release --features "training,env-bucket-brigade" --test test_psro_bucket_brigade -- --ignored --nocapture test_psro_beats_ppo_on_no_convergence_cells` × 3 — **deferred to Judge / Doctor / CI** per the wall-clock realities described above.

## Scope impact

- Single file modified: `tests/test_psro_bucket_brigade.rs`
- No conflict with PR #132 (which closes #127 in `tests/test_nfsp_bucket_brigade.rs` + `src/multi_agent/nfsp.rs` — disjoint files).
- No changes to public API, `bucket_brigade_metrics.rs`, PSRO training code, or NFSP test.

author: pcoffline
body:
## What & why

A tidy run reported **success with the requested counts even when group creation silently failed** (SPEC TIDY-10). On a Zen build where `gBrowser.addTabGroup` returns a falsy value rather than throwing, the user was told "Sorted 9 tabs into 3 groups" while nothing changed.

The failure was swallowed at three layers:

1. `groups.create()` returned `true` **unconditionally** — the `if (group)` guard only wrapped label/color assignment, then fell through to `return true` even when `group` was falsy.
2. `groups.reconcile()` ignored `create()`'s return value entirely.
3. `runTidy()` always notified success using the **requested** counts; only a thrown exception reached the failure path.

## Changes

- `create()` — a falsy `addTabGroup` result now `continue`s to the next option shape (and never sets name/color on a non-group); returns a truthful boolean.
- `reconcile()` — accumulates a `{ realized, failed }` tally (reuse-in-place and successful create count as realized; a failed create counts as failed; groups with no live tabs count as neither) and returns it.
- `apply()` — returns the tally.
- `runTidy()` — notifies the real outcome:
  - `failed === 0` → existing success message with the **created** count.
  - `realized > 0` → partial: `Sorted N tabs into R groups; F could not be created.` (error styling).
  - else → `Tidy failed: no groups could be created.` (error styling).
  - Catch-path wording normalised `failed: …` → `Tidy failed: …` (issue #1 follow-up comment).

## SPEC → tests → code

- **SPEC** — TIDY-10 extended to define partial-success, total-failure, and "a falsy `addTabGroup` result counts as a failed creation".
- **tests** — new `tidy-run.spec.ts › notifies failure when group creation silently fails` stubs `gBrowser.addTabGroup` to return `null` (stashed on `window.__zenTidyTabsOrigAddTabGroup`, restored in `finally` since the `zen` fixture is worker-scoped) and asserts the failure notification plus no groups created.

## Validation

- `npm run lint:script` — clean.
- `npm run test:headful` — **48 passed** (incl. the new case and the existing TIDY-10 success/failure tests).

Closes #1

Base branch is `ci/16-lint-product-file` (#24), per the linear PR stack.

author: alnoki
body:
# Background

The shared size-bps fill cap `level_fill_atoms(size_bps, leg_atoms)`
([matching_math.rs](sdk/price-core/src/matching_math.rs)) returns `None`
when `size_bps > BPS`, and the two callers handled that `None`
differently:

- On-chain `swap.rs` (`flush_level_size`) maps `None` to a hard
  `DropsetError::LiquidityProfileSizeOverflow` — the whole `swap` tx
  aborts.
- The off-chain simulator
  ([matching.rs](sdk/price-core/src/matching.rs)) did `.unwrap_or(0)` —
  dropping just that level and continuing to quote the rest of the book.

So for a profile with `size_bps > BPS` the engine rejects the take
entirely while the simulator returned a smaller, non-empty quote — a
router quoting off the simulator could offer a fill the live engine
won't honor. This is exactly the class of engine⇄simulator drift the
conformance pins exist to catch.

It is **not a live bug**: `set_liquidity_profile` bounds the per-side
Σ `size_bps` to `BPS`, and since each `size_bps` is a non-negative `u16`
every individual level is therefore `<= BPS`. The only way to reach the
`None` case is account bytes the program never wrote (corruption, or a
hypothetical future profile-writing path that skips the sum check). This
PR pins the residual seam rather than leaving it relied-on implicitly,
and folds in the ENG-501 comment cleanup on the same lines.

# Changes

1. **Reject the take in the simulator instead of dropping the level.**
   ([matching.rs](sdk/price-core/src/matching.rs)) `simulate_swap` now
   checks each active, flush-armed vault during book construction and
   returns an empty `Quote` if any level is out of range, via the new
   `vault_has_oversize_flush_level` helper (which reuses
   `level_fill_atoms`, keeping the bound defined once). This mirrors the
   engine, which materializes the **whole** book — every flush-armed
   vault, **both** sides — before any leg fills and aborts the entire tx
   on the first oversize level, regardless of which side or how deep it
   sits. The `level_fill_atoms(...).unwrap_or(0)` in `level_state` is now
   an unreachable total-function fallback (the up-front guard has already
   rejected any oversize book); its comment is corrected to say so.

2. **Pin the parity with two litesvm conformance tests.**
   ([sdk_conformance.rs](programs/dropset/tests/sdk_conformance.rs))
   Each pokes a `size_bps > BPS` into a seeded vault's profile, then
   asserts the simulator returns `Quote::default()` **and** the real
   on-chain `swap` hard-errors `LiquidityProfileSizeOverflow`. One
   corrupts the **consumed** side (a Buy's asks); the other the
   **non-consumed** side (a Buy's bids) — the engine flushes both up
   front, so it still aborts, and this case guards against a
   consumed-side-only check that would quote a fill the engine rejects.
   Adds a `poke_level_size_bps` fixture helper, since no instruction can
   write a `size_bps > BPS`.

3. **Fix the comments documenting the contract (ENG-501, folded in).**
   ([matching_math.rs](sdk/price-core/src/matching_math.rs),
   [matching.rs](sdk/price-core/src/matching.rs),
   [swap.rs](programs/dropset/src/instructions/swap.rs)) The
   `level_fill_atoms` doc and the `matching.rs` flush-branch comment said
   the simulator "drops the level (size 0), matching the on-chain
   handler's hard reject" — imprecise, since the engine aborts the whole
   take while dropping one level kept quoting. Reworded to the actual
   parity: both callers now refuse the take on `None` (engine hard-errors,
   simulator yields an empty quote). Also made the per-side `Σ ≤ BPS`
   ⇒ per-level `≤ BPS` implication explicit in all three spots, rather
   than stating `size_bps ≤ BPS` as if it were a directly-enforced
   per-level guarantee.

# Verification

- `make lint` green — every hook including rustfmt, clippy, biome, tsc,
  mdformat, cspell.
- `make test` green — all program unit + integration suites (incl. the
  two new `sdk_simulate_swap_rejects_oversize_size_bps_*` conformance
  tests), price-core (61 unit + conformance), and the SDK/quoting
  conformance pins.
- `make test-no-teardown` green (feature-off, 6/6).
- IDL, SDK clients, and conformance vectors regenerate byte-identical
  (no IDL-facing or vector-affecting change).

# Notes for the reviewer

This issue was filed as a deferral from ENG-475 / PR #102 and is
written against that PR's post-merge code (the extracted
`matching_math::level_fill_atoms` and the `.unwrap_or(0)` simulator
path). #102 landed on `main` just after this branch was cut, so the
branch is rebased onto it and targets that real code.

The contract chosen is the one the issue flagged as most likely:
the simulator yields an empty quote (rejects the take) to match the
engine, rather than aligning the engine down to a per-level drop —
quoting nothing is the only router-safe direction. The behavior change
is confined to the off-chain simulator; the on-chain `flush_level_size`
is unchanged (only its doc comment), and `level_fill_atoms` changes are
doc-only, so no consensus behavior moves.

The review surfaced a **separate, pre-existing** engine⇄simulator
divergence of the same class but a different seam: on a corrupt
`Vault.next` cycle the simulator's DLL walk silently truncates and
returns a partial quote, while the engine aborts `CorruptVaultList`.
Out of scope for this `size_bps` fix and not introduced here; filed as
**ENG-505**.

Summary:
- Expands the CMake workflow to configure and build both `Debug` and `Release` builds.
- Runs the full CTest suite in the Debug lane.
- Keeps `fail-fast: false` so both configurations report independently.

author: dreamcreateweb
body:
## What
The clinic picks **one** color (their brand). Until now that drove the primary accents, but the rest of the public site was pinned to a fixed scheme — a forest-teal deep band (footer / testimonials / insurance), a chartreuse announcement strip, a warm-beige ground, fixed blue/peach hero backdrops — which clashed the moment a clinic chose anything but teal. Now **everything** derives from the brand, deterministically and contrast-checked.

## How
**Engine** (`lib/clinic-site-theme.ts`) — `buildClinicPalette(brand)` derives a full role-based palette in HSL: keep the brand HUE, dial saturation/lightness to a designed target per role.
- **Neutrals** (bg / surface / border / ink / muted) carry only a whisper of the hue → they read as tinted near-whites that *temperature-match* the brand (blue brand → cool ground, terracotta → warm).
- The **deep "rhythm-break" band** and the **bright strip** carry the brand at full presence.
- Every on-color ink is contrast-raised until it clears **WCAG AA**, so nothing a clinic can pick produces unreadable text.
- Pure — no AI, no network, no persistence; runs at render time.

A few derived examples:

| Brand | Deep band | Strip | Ground |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sage `#9CAF9F` | `#2f5034` forest | `#c9e9ce` | `#f5f7f5` |
| Dusty blue `#7C9CB8` | `#2d4153` slate | `#c9dae9` | `#f5f6f7` |
| Terracotta `#D4A284` | `#5e3821` chocolate | `#edd4c4` | `#f7f6f5` |
| Coral `#E87B5E` | `#5e2e21` rust | `#f8c6b9` | `#f7f5f5` |
| Violet `#7C3AED` | `#38215e` royal purple | `#d0b7fa` | `#f6f5f7` |

**Injection** — the `/site/[slug]` layout resolves the brand (`getClinicThemeBySlug`, a tiny cached query) and injects `clinicPaletteCss(brand)` on `:root`, so every page, subpage, and shared chrome inherits the theme. `MinimalSiteChrome` injects it too for `/r/[token]` (outside that layout).

**Consumption** — every clinic-site surface now reads `var(--c-*, <literalFallback>)` instead of hardcoded hex / fixed `CLINIC_THEME` constants: header (strip + nav), footer, testimonials, ClosingCTA, the modern homepage template (grounds, deep insurance band, closer strip, hero-oval backdrops), and all subpages (about, services, team, careers, insurance, payment, dental-plans, faq, book, intake, membership, shop, review). The literal fallback preserves the original look if a surface is rendered outside the layout. The **OG image** derives the same palette but with REAL hexes (Satori can't read CSS vars).

`CLINIC_THEME` stays as the documented default + fallback set.

## Scope note
Brand-on-button text (`text-white` on a brand-colored button) is intentionally **left for a focused follow-up** — for pale brands that's a separate pre-existing contrast concern; the palette already exposes `--c-brand-ink` for it. This PR is the secondary/background harmonization the brand picker was missing.

## Tests
- `tests/clinic-site/palette.test.ts` — contrast floor (WCAG AA on every on-color ink) + role invariants (deep dark, ground/strip light) across the 6 onboarding presets + adversarial extremes (pure primaries, bright yellow, near-white/black, no-brand).
- `tests/clinic-site/palette-wiring.test.ts` — source guards: layout injects, the deep band / strip / neutrals read the vars, legacy hexes survive only as `var()` fallbacks, OG image uses real hexes.
- Updated the 3 tests that asserted the OLD "hardcoded, NOT theme-driven" behavior.

Full suite green (**3317 tests**); production build clean.
